# Creator tool and property reference

<!-- Generated by tools/creator_docs.py; edit its sources, then --write. -->
[Handbook](README.md) · [Command gates](tool-permissions.md) · [World settings](world-settings.md)

Snapshot of shipped help for authoring commands, generic definitions and the
reviewed property/behavior families. It includes inherited tools these workflows
depend on. Runtime AHELP may append schemas; world-owned help can override this
stock text. Example names and room IDs require corresponding world content.

Use the chapter guides for workflows and current limitations. This reference
preserves help wording and uses the stock files rather than world overrides.
Runtime schemas can add detail to property help. Legacy mentions of
CoffeeMud or server administration do not reintroduce removed network services.

<a id="accept"></a>

## ACCEPT

Source: [help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/help.ini), line 2117.

```text
Command : ACCEPT
Usage   : ACCEPT [NUMBER/NAME]
Example : accept 2
Short(s):
CoffeeSUD: takes on a job from the quest board you looked at last, by its number there or
its name.  Without a board, it takes on a quest offered to you, as QUESTS ACCEPT does.
```

<a id="achievementrewards"></a>

## ACHIEVEMENTREWARDS

Source: [arc_misc.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_misc.ini), line 1234.

```text
CoffeeSUD: rewards an achievement's REWARDS (and MPREWARD, and quest rewards) may give
besides the stock ones, each a number then the word with its settings in brackets.  1
SCRIPT(LOAD=progs/x.script) or 1 SCRIPT(ONCE_PROG 100;mpecho Well done.;~) (lines between
semicolons; no word of it a lone number): run once on the character, its ONCE_PROG and then
its FUNCTION_PROG ONACHIEVE.  1 EFFECT(ID=Prop_Adjuster PARMS="con+1" TICKS=0): the effect,
for good with TICKS=0 (kept with the character), else for that many ticks.  500
FACTION(ID=elves.ini), or 1 FACTION(ID=elves.ini AMOUNT=500): standing added.  1
VAR(NAME=chapter VALUE=2): a script variable of the character (WHO= for another name, * for
the game's).  1 RECIPE(SKILL=Weaponsmithing NAME="rune blade"): a recipe known for good
(AHELP PROP_KNOWNRECIPES).  ACHIEVEMENTS shows what each gives; on an [ACCOUNT] achievement
they go to each later character.  Example: Friend of the Grove: REWARDS="1000
FACTION(ID=elves.ini) 1 EFFECT(ID=Prop_Resistance PARMS=\"poison 10%\") 1
SCRIPT(LOAD=progs/grove_friend.script)".
```

<a id="affixes"></a>

## AFFIXES

Source: [arc_misc.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_misc.ini), line 944.

```text
CoffeeSUD: random enchantments as data, in world/affixes.xml, else
resources/randareas/affixes.xml (or the world's own copy in world/resources/randareas/).
Each <AFFIX id="flaming" name="Flaming" pos="prefix" (or suffix) kinds="weapon,ammo"
(weapon, armor, ammo, item, any) level="5-30" pickweight="10" power="1" cursed="false">
holds <AFFECT class="Prop_WearAdjuster" parms="damage+2"/> tags.  An item gets at most one
prefix and one suffix that fit its kind and level, picked by weight: its name takes them (a
Flaming short sword of Bleeding), its level rises by the power, its value by a tenth for
each, and a cursed one cannot be taken off.  Random enchantment (ItemGenerator ENCHANTED=)
uses them when the file has any, as do AFFIXES=[MATH] on Prop_LootTable and RandomItems and
AFFIXES="0?2" on a template ITEM.
```

<a id="ageing"></a>

## AGEING

Source: [arc_misc.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_misc.ini), line 1069.

```text
CoffeeSUD: ageing as data.  A GenRace's AGEEFFECTS="MIDDLEAGED: STR-1 DEX-1 WIS+1;
VENERABLE: STR-2 CON-2" takes the place of the usual effects of age for that race: each
age's stat changes (any stat by name or its first letters), and none at an age not named;
the ages are INFANT, TODDLER, CHILD, YOUNGADULT, MATURE, MIDDLEAGED, OLD, VENERABLE and
ANCIENT.  AGEDISEASES="VENERABLE:Disease_Cancer:0.01, ANCIENT:Disease_Arthritis:1" in the
ini or world.ini takes the place of the usual ageing diseases: each a percent chance, at
each check of age, from that age on.  On each birthday AGE_PROG [BIRTHDAY|CATEGORY|an
age|ALL] runs on the character's scripts and those around them, $0 the age category, $1 the
age, $2 BIRTHDAY or CATEGORY (CATEGORY when the age category changed); and the achievement
event EVENT="AGECATEGORY" CATEGORY=[AGE] is won on reaching that age.
STARTAGE_[NAME]="[ZAPPER MASK]:[YEARS]" entries start a new character who meets the mask at
that age (the first that fits): STARTAGE_VETERAN="-TATTOOS +ORIGIN_VETERAN:35".
```

<a id="armorsmithing"></a>

## ARMORSMITHING

Source: [common_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/common_help.ini), line 126.

```text
<ABILITY>Usage    : ARMORSMITH (LIST/MEND/REFIT/SCAN/LEARN/INFO) [ARMOR NAME]
Usage    :   ... (FROM [RESOURCE NAME])
Example  : armorsmith platemail shirt
:        : armorsmith list
:        : armorsmith list vest
:        : armorsmith list left wrist
:        : armorsmith list 5-10
:        : armorsmith list all
:        : armorsmith info vest
:        : armorsmith mend vest
:        : armorsmith refit sleeves
:        : armorsmith scan
:        : armorsmith scan bob
:        : armorsmith learn vest
This skill allows a player to craft armor pieces from metal.  This skill requires
Blacksmithing in order to learn it.  The extent of the items which can be crafted expands as
 the player goes up in level.  To begin smithing, the player must be in a room with an open
fire burning, and must have placed the metal he or she wishes to make the item from on the
ground.  This command may also be used to mend damaged metal armors, get info on a list
item, refit metal armors which are the wrong size, or learn how to smith a found item,
provided a blank recipe page, or recipe book with blank pages is in his or her inventory.
The player may also scan the room or other players for equipment that may be mended by this
skill, using the scan parameter. The raw metal for armorsmithing can be obtained using the
Mining skill, and better metals through the Smelting skill. Using better metals will
increase both the strength and the required level of the crafted item, and some metals
require less material to make the same items.

This skill also allows the player to learn how to smith an item he or she has found.  To do
this, the player needs to have a blank Recipe page, or a Recipe book with blank pages in his
 or her inventory.
```

<a id="as"></a>

## AS

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 58.

```text
Command : AS
Usage   : AS [PLAYERNAME/MOBNAME]/(PORT X)/PLAYERS (HERE) [COMMAND]
Example : as "bob" inventory
Example : as bob here drop all
Example : as PLAYERS here drop all
Example : as bob cast fireball monster
Example : as port 2325 list users
Short(s):
A command that allows one to issue other commands as if they were another player or mob.
Anyone can use it on their own characters in the world: see PARTY.  This is the best way to
manage a players inventory or bank accounts from the command line. The optional "here"
parameter should follow the name if the command is to be issued with the player in the same
room as the archon. The optional "port x" parameter can be used to execute commands on other
 mud hosts, so long as the admin qualifies as a SysOp on the target port.

```

<a id="ask"></a>

## ASK

Source: [help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/help.ini), line 335.

```text
Command : ASK
Usage   : ASK ([MOB NAME]) [MESSAGE]
Usage   : ASK ([MOB NAME]) ABOUT
Example : ask Where am I?
Example : ask miner about the collapse
Example : ask miner about
Short(s):
Causes your character to speak to one or more characters or mobs in the same room as
yourself.  You may specify the mob to speak to, or just speak in general.  Words highlighted
 in what someone says are topics you can ask others about; ASK [MOB NAME] ABOUT, with
nothing after it, lists the topics you know that they have something to say about (with no
name, whom you are talking with).
```

<a id="assert"></a>

## ASSERT

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 1785.

```text
Command  : ASSERT
Usage    : ASSERT HERE [ROOM ID]
Usage    : ASSERT HAS [ITEM]
Usage    : ASSERT VAR [HOST] [NAME] [=/!=/</>/<=/>=] [VALUE]
Usage    : ASSERT QUEST [NAME] STEP [NUMBER]
Example  : assert here Moor#1
Example  : assert var Hero PAIDTROLL = 1
Short(s) :
In builder mode or a DEV=1 game, answers ASSERT ok: ... or ASSERT FAIL: ... and why, for
playtest files: you are in the room, carry the item, a global script variable compares so
(numbers as numbers), or a quest is running at the step. Playtest files, world/tests/*.play,
 hold one command a line and #expect TEXT, #reject TEXT, #assert ..., #wait N, #save SLOT,
#seed N, #char NAME,RACE,CLASS and #restore SLOT; tools/playtest.sh runs them, each in a new
 game on a scratch copy of the world, in turns with a fixed seed, prints PASS or FAIL for
each with the failing lines, and exits 1 if any failed.
```

<a id="behavior-aggressive"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_AGGRESSIVE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 95.

```text
Behavior   : Aggressive
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : aggression flags (MESSAGE=[msg]) aggression masks
Example    : +elf -fighter
Example    : message="All must die!!" -elf +fighter
Example    : MOBKILL MISBEHAVE +elf -fighter
Description:
Makes the mob attack any player mob it can detect in the same room, from the moment the new
mob enters.  Horribly wounded mobs are not aggressive. Mobs will also not be aggressive
towards Archons and builders with the CMDMOBS security flag.If no other parameters are
given, the mob will attack anyone.
Valid aggressive masks include:
message=[msg] something for the mob to say whenever he's fixing to attack
delay=x (makes the mob delay x ticks before looking for a victim)
mobkill (makes this behavior attack mobs as well as players)
nogang (makes this behavior pass over players already in combat)
misbehave (makes this mob attack even when wounded or a follower)
checklevel (makes this mob attack only those within 6 levels below him)
BRIBE=[AMOUNT],[TICKS OF PEACE],[TICKS TO PAY] - this is a comma-delimited
BRIBEPAYMSG=x, BRIBEPAIDMSG=x, (see also ahelp on AGGRESSIVE BRIBE)
WARN="[LINE]|[LINE]" - CoffeeSUD: a warning first, one line a tick, then the attack if they
are still
there; WARNTICKS=[N] how many ticks (the number of lines); BACKOFF=true: one who sits down
or
holds no weapon is not attacked while they stay so, and is warned afresh if they stop;
NEAR=1:
the rooms next door hear it.  VeryAggressive and MobileAggressive take them too.
Example    : WARN="The wolf bares its teeth.|The wolf snarls and crouches!" WARNTICKS=2
BACKOFF=true +ITEM "-raw meat"
See AHELP ZAPPERMASK, where allowed is aggressed, and disallowed is spared.
```

<a id="behavior-arrest"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_ARREST

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 163.

```text
Behavior   : Arrest
Targets    : Areas
Parameters : (/CUSTOM/[FILENAME])(;[LAW KEY]=[LAW VALUE] ...)
Example    :
Example    : custom
Example    : laws_mycity.ini
Example    : custom;JUDGE="justice judge" OFFICERS="cityguard police"
Example    : laws_riverton.ini;SALESTAX=5 OFFICERS="cityguard"
Description:
CoffeeSUD: a law as world content.  A law file in resources/ (or world/resources/), with
KEY=VALUE overrides after a semicolon, is kept in the area's BEHAVES in its .cmare, so every
 new game has it.  A custom law edited with a law book in builder mode is written to
world/laws/[AREA].ini (the area's name, as its .cmare is named), which is then the law; in a
 game the law as saved wins (changes after a conquest stay in the save), and a new game
starts from the file.
This powerful behavior allows you to set up the enforcement of laws inside of a city. The
only parameter is the name of an ini file in the resources directory.  If left blank, the
default laws.ini file will be used.  The ini file specifies the judges, enforcement mobs,
the laws and their punishments, and the location of jails.  The messages seen by the
criminals is also contained therein.  The word custom may also be placed in the parameters
in order to make the area laws changeable using either a StdLawBook or a GenLawBook.
```

<a id="behavior-bossphases"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_BOSSPHASES

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 209.

```text
Behavior   : BossPhases
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : [TRIGGER]: [ACTION], [ACTION]...; [TRIGGER]: ...;
(RESET=FULLHEAL/LEAVECOMBAT/LEASH/NEVER)
Example    : ONENGAGE: SAY "Fools!"; AT=60%: SUMMON skeleton warrior x2; AT=25%: AFFECT
Prop_AbilityImmunity "WEAPONS" 3, MOVETO Crypt#9, HEAL 20%; ONDEATH: ROOM EMOTE "The
phylactery cracks."
Description:
CoffeeSUD: a boss's phases, each firing once a fight.  Triggers: ONENGAGE (the fight
starts), AT=[N]% (its hit points under N%), AT=ROUND [N] (the fight's Nth round),
AT=ADDSDEAD (all it summoned are dead), ONDEATH.  Actions, commas between them: SAY, EMOTE
or YELL [TEXT]; CAST [ABILITY] (on its foe, or itself if it helps); SUMMON [CATALOG NAME, or
 a mob class] x[N] (they follow it, attack its foe, are tagged SUMMONED, and go when the
phases rearm); BEHAVE [BEHAVIOR] ([PARMS]) and UNBEHAVE [BEHAVIOR]; AFFECT [ABILITY]
("[PARMS]") ([TICKS]) and REMOVE [ABILITY] on itself; IMMUNE [TICKS] (no damage); HEAL [N]%;
 MOVETO [ROOM ID]; ROOM EMOTE [TEXT]; ROOM AFFECT [ABILITY] ([TICKS]); CALL [FUNCTION] (its
scripts' FUNCTION_PROG).  It starts in phase 1, and each AT= that fires starts the next: its
 scripts' PHASE_PROG [N] runs, and PHASE($i) reads it.  RESET says when the phases rearm:
FULLHEAL (the default, when it is whole again out of a fight), LEAVECOMBAT (when the fight
ends), LEASH (when EncounterReset resets it) or NEVER.  It is back to phase 1 when it dies;
a saved game keeps the phase.
```

<a id="behavior-bribegateguard"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_BRIBEGATEGUARD

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 194.

```text
Behavior   : BribeGateGuard
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : Price of entry, Gate System
Example    : price=5 gates=Avalon
Description:
The mob will work akin to a gate guard, but you have to have at least the price on your tab
for the guard to open it (or let you open it from that side) Any payment made over the price
 is retained, in a manner akin to a bank chain, so if any other guards are in the same Gate
System, they will all use the same tab.  DO NOT put one on each side - unlike Gate Guards,
these guys don't play well with others. If you want players to be able to sneak by them,
merely make sure they can't see sneaking or invis - whichever.  The hiding player will have
to wait for another player to get the door open to sneak through.
```

<a id="behavior-combatabilities"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_COMBATABILITIES

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 332.

```text
Behavior   : CombatAbilities
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : (as derived class) and +SKILLID -SKILLID
Parameters : (MINTICKS=[NUM] MAXTICKS=[NUM] CHANCE=[NUM])
Parameters : (BSIZE=[NUM])
Example    : (as derived class) -Spell_Sleep
Description:
Gives the mob the urge to use their skills, spells, prayers, songs, and other abilities
during combat.
This behavior should not be used WITH any of the other CombatAbilities behaviors, such as
Fighterness, Thiefness, Mageness, Clericness, Druidness, or CombatAbilities. It should be
used alone on a mob.

The parameters are as described in one of the derived classes, but in addition, you can also
 specify the IDs of certain skills that the behavior will either be allowed to be used in
combat even if it is not normally allowed, or be disallowed to be used in combat even if the
 mob has the skill and it would normally be allowed, depending on whether the ID is preceded
 by + or -. The BSIZE argument will limit the size of the skill rotation used.

*Note: In turn-based combat system, CombatAbilities will only work if the NPC has more than
one attack, and is able to make its one normal weapon attack.

CoffeeSUD: whom it helps and how.  SUPPORT=LEADER (the default: itself and the mob it
follows), SELF, GROUP (its group here) or MASK:"[ZAPPER MASK]" (anyone here the mask fits,
NPCs too, whom it need not follow).  HEALAT=[N]: it heals only those under N% of their hit
points, the most hurt first, and before anything else.  CUREFIRST=Poison,Disease: it cures
those first, with its abilities whose names say so.  BUFFOUTOFCOMBAT: out of a fight it
buffs those it helps who lack the effect.  HEALAT, CUREFIRST and BUFFOUTOFCOMBAT have it
look every 3 ticks out of a fight too.  These work on the presets (Clericness and the rest)
too.
Example    : Clericness MIXEDDEFENSIVE SUPPORT=MASK:"-RACE +Goblin" HEALAT=60

CoffeeSUD: rotations.  A +SKILL entry may take rules in brackets: EVERY=[N] (every N rounds
of the fight), FIRST=[N] (not before round N; with EVERY, its first round), ONCE (tried once
 a fight, whether it works or not), BELOW=[N]% (only while its own hit points are under N%),
 COOLDOWN=[N] (N rounds between tries, a fizzle too), WEIGHT=[N] (picked N times as often as
 the others), SELF (on itself) and TARGET=CASTER (on the foe here with the most spells,
prayers, chants or songs).  A skill with EVERY, FIRST, ONCE or BELOW is used only when its
turn comes, before anything else, the first due in the list's order; the rest are picked at
random as before, by WEIGHT.  OPENER=[SKILL] is its first round's.  Stock skills take them
too.  The counts start again with each fight.
Example    : OPENER=Skill_Trip +Poison_Sting(EVERY=2) +Fighter_Kick(WEIGHT=3)
+Spell_Fly(ONCE BELOW=25%)
```

<a id="behavior-concierge"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_CONCIERGE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 375.

```text
Behavior   : Conceirge
Targets    : MOBs, Items, Rooms, Areas
Parameters : [ALL PRICE]/[AREA/ROOM]=[PRICE]/[PARAM]=[VALUE]; ... ;
Example    : 1.5
Example    : Midgaard#3001=1.5; Smurfville=2.0; =70 ; AREAONLY=true
Example    : Midgaard#3032; =100 ; AREAONLY=false; MAXRANGE=100
Description:
This behavior makes the mob a deliverer of information to players, specifically the
directions to rooms or areas.  The mob will charge for his services if you specify a price
in the parameters, or he will do it for free if you don't, or if the last price specified
was 0.  The parameters can include a comma delimited set of room IDs, area names, or even
short title descriptions for quickly entering rooms within short range of the mob.

The parameters may also include certain other variables as part of the parameter list.
These include AREAONLY = true or false, to specify whether the concierge knows anything
about places outside his area.  MAXRANGE=number for the maximum number of rooms away from
the concierge that is known.  GREETING=message will give a special concierge greeting
message for all players who enter the room its in. ENTERMSG will give a message to players
who mount the concierge (rideables only).  TALKERNAME=name will change the apparent name of
the speaker. PERROOM=number will set a per-room price for the distance from the current room
 to the one sought.  NOWATER=true to prevent trails over water. NOAIR=true, to prevent
trails through the air. NOLOCKS=true to prevent trails through locked doors. NOHOMES=true to
 prevent trails through private homes. NOINDOOR=true to prevent finding or trailing through
indoor rooms. NOCLIMB to prevent trails through climbable exits. NOCRAWL to prevent trails
through crawlable exits.  Use PORTAL=true to have the concierge create a magical portal
instead of giving directions. Use CLAN=[CLAN NAME] to have the concierge restrict
destinations to clan conquered or property rooms.  Use MOBILE=true to have a concierge mob
force the player to follow them to the destination.
```

<a id="behavior-conquerable"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_CONQUERABLE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 35.

```text
Behavior   : Conquerable
Targets    : AREAs
Parameters : (JOURNAL="[JOURNAL NAME]") (LAW=(TRUE/FALSE))
Parameters : (OWNERSHIP=(TRUE/FALSE)) (LOYALTY=[PCT])
Parameters:  (LEVELDIFF=[NUM])
Example    : JOURNAL="The Conquest Times" LAW=FALSE OWNERSHIP=FALSE
Description:
This behavior makes the area conquerable by clans using items put together using ClanCraft.
  See the general help on CONQUEST for more information on what this means and how it works.
  The JOURNAL entry, if given, will log conquest events to a journal of that name.  The LAW
entry is required in order to allow an area to be set up by conquering clans with a system
of law. The OWNERSHIP entry is true if All private property is automatically signed over to
the conquering clan, and false if it is left alone.  The LOYALTY is a percent 0-100 that a
populace gains is loyalty to their rulers, with default 0.  The LEVELDIFF is how far below
the killer a targets level can be to get Points, with default equal to coffeemud.ini EXPRATE
 x 2.
```

<a id="behavior-decay"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_DECAY

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 419.

```text
Behavior   : Decay
Targets    : MOBs, Items
Parameters : min, max ticks, a percent chance, trigger masks
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=75 answer=" goes poof!"
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=75 -LEVEL +<17
Example    : notrigger answer=" " use2=true
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=75 -CLASS +Paladin
Description:
According to the timing and percent chance described by the parameters, the mob or item with
 this behavior will vanish at the expired time.  MOBs do not begin their countdown until
attacked, items when they are picked up, weapons when they are first wielded, armor when it
is first worn, rideables when mounted.  These item triggers can be changed by setting
parameter USE2=true to trigger when a scroll or book is read, drink drunk, food eaten, pipe
smoked, or rideable mob mounted.

The countdown may also depend on whether the mob or player triggering the countdown meets
any masks specified.   You may force the object to decay immediately by placing the
NOTRIGGER mask inside your parameter string.  The message seen when the object decays can
also be modified by changing the ANSWER parameter. For value masks to determine whether a
countdown begins,
see AHELP ZAPPERMASK, where allowed is decayed, and disallowed is ignored.
```

<a id="behavior-delayedtransporter"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_DELAYEDTRANSPORTER

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 3240.

```text
Behavior   : Delayed Transporter
Targets    : Rooms, Mobs, Items
Parameters : Max and min ticks, pct chance, room ids separated by ';'.
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=25;Midgaard#3001;Sewers#6020;Midgaard#3020
Description:
This behavior defines a series of random rooms.  All rooms are separated by semicolons as
shown above.  The first parameter can be empty to use defaults, or may contain a setting for
 minimum ticks, maximum ticks, and the percent chance of occurrence after the random number
of ticks has expired.  In the above example every 10-20 ticks, there is a 25% chance that
every mob in the same room as the behaving object will be teleported to one of the three
listed rooms (at random).
CoffeeSUD: put PARTY=true|LEADER|EACH, FARE=[price], PERHEAD=true, MASK="[passenger mask]",
DEST=ORDER|RANDOM, LOOK=true, DEPARTMSG="[text]" and ARRIVEMSG="[text]" before the first
semicolon. PARTY shares a group countdown and prevents a follower departing alone. PERHEAD
counts eligible characters; PARTY=LEADER charges the leader and EACH charges individual
shares. All entry and payment checks complete before any passenger moves or pays. Countdown
and ordered destination progress survive saves.
```

<a id="behavior-emoter"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_EMOTER

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 548.

```text
Behavior   : Emoter
Targets    : Room, MOBs, Items, Areas
Parameters : Flags, Max/Min ticks, pct chance, expires, emote strings, ';' separated.
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=25;wiggles his bottom.;smiles evilly.;burps!
Example    : smell chance=25 expires=10;smells horrible!;is really stinky!
Example    : chance=100 inroom="Here#1,Here#2";looks horrible!;is bad!
Example    : broadcast sound chance=25;grumbles!;eeeks!
Example    : ;grumbles!;eeeks!
Example    : min=1 max=2 chance=25;sound grumbles!;visual leers broadly.;social smile
Description:
This behavior defines a serious of random emotes.  All emote strings are separated by the
semicolons shown above.  The first parameter can be empty for defaults, or may contain a
setting for minimum ticks (min=10), maximum ticks (max=20), the percent chance of occurrence
 after the random number of ticks has expired (chance=25), a total number of occurrences
before expiration (expires=0), a list of rooms where the emoter MUST be for the emoter to
work (inroom=...), a tag to make the emote sound based (sound), a tag to make the emote
smell based (smell), flag to keep emoters private (PRIVATE), or a tag to make the emote
broadcast to adjacent rooms (broadcast).  In the first example every 10-20 ticks, there is a
 25% chance that the object with this property will select one of the emotes randomly and
perform it for all those in the same room who can see it.  In the second example, a smell
based emote will be performed 25% of the time, but will only emote 10 times before the
behavior is removed from the object.  In the third example, there is a 100% chance that, if
the object is in room Here#1 or Here#2, it will emote one of the two choices. In the fourth
example, a sound based emote will be performed 25% of the time in the room of the behavior,
and in any adjacent rooms.

You can also mix and match the types of emotes by putting the keywords SIGHT, SMELL, NOISE,
and SOCIAL PUFF, as the first word in each emote string.  This denotes the type of emote for
 the rest of the string.  The last example shows how to enter a mixed emote.  Each emote
type will respect visibility, smellability, hearingness, etc.. unless the EMOTEONLY flag is
used.
CoffeeSUD: first-field options NOREPEAT=n, RETRY and QUIETAFTER=n select eligible lines,
suppress recent repeats, and quiet ambience during combat or reading. Each line may begin
with DAY/NIGHT/DAWN/DUSK, seasons, RAIN/SNOW/FOG, INDOORS/OUTDOORS, IFVAR name=value,
MASK="zapper", ONCE and WEIGHT=n before its SIGHT/SOUND/SMELL/SOCIAL type. ONCE is saved per
 character. Area emotes test each room's own conditions.
Example: min=8 max=20 chance=40 RETRY NOREPEAT=2;NIGHT SOUND an owl hoots.;IFVAR WOLVES=1
WEIGHT=3 ONCE SOUND wolves howl.
```

<a id="behavior-encounterreset"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_ENCOUNTERRESET

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 712.

```text
Behavior   : EncounterReset
Targets    : MOBs, Rooms
Parameters : (RADIUS=[N]) (IDLE=[N]) (HEAL=[N]) (HOME=true/false) (DESPAWNADDS=true/false)
(ROOM=true/false)
Example    : RADIUS=1 IDLE=5 HEAL=100
Example    : IDLE=10 ROOM=true
Description:
CoffeeSUD: a boss that the party walks away from resets.  After a fight, when none of those
it fought has been within RADIUS rooms (1; 0 for its own room) for IDLE ticks (5), it goes
back to its start room (HOME, true), heals HEAL percent of its hit points (100) and all its
mana and moves, sheds what was cast on it to harm it, loses the adds it summoned
(DESPAWNADDS, true: NPCs following it that have no home, or with the tag SUMMONED), forgets
its threat, and its scripts' RESET_PROG runs.  ROOM=true resets every NPC of its start room
with it; on a room, every NPC there is reset together.
```

<a id="behavior-escortee"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_ESCORTEE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 727.

```text
Behavior   : Escortee
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : DEST=[ROOM ID] (MODE=LEAD/FOLLOW) (WAITFOR=LEADER) (WAITCALL=[N])
(WAITMSG="[TEXT]") (PANIC=FLEE/HIDE/COWER) (AVOID=[ROOM ID],...) (TALK="[ROOM ID]:[TEXT]")
(ONARRIVE="[MOBPROG]") (ONDEATH="[MOBPROG]") (TIMEOUT=[N] ONTIMEOUT="[MOBPROG]")
Example    : DEST=Riverford#1 MODE=LEAD WAITFOR=LEADER PANIC=COWER TALK="Bridge#3:They say
trolls live under here." ONARRIVE="say Thank you, friends!;mpsetvar $n ESCORTED 1"
Description:
CoffeeSUD: an NPC escorted to DEST.  Its leader is the one it follows when the escort begins
 (a quest's MPFORCE $i follow $n); until then it waits.  MODE=FOLLOW (the default): it
follows its leader; MODE=LEAD: it stops following and walks the way itself, a step a tick,
and the party follows it.  WAITFOR=LEADER: while its leader is not with it, it does not go
on, and after WAITCALL ticks (3) it calls WAITMSG ("Wait for me!").  PANIC: when attacked it
 flees, dives for cover or cowers (both stop the fight).  AVOID: rooms (by ID, or the end of
 one) it will not go into.  TALK (and TALK1= to TALK9=): a remark the first time it comes to
 that room.  ONARRIVE, ONDEATH and, after TIMEOUT ticks, ONTIMEOUT: MOBPROG lines, ; between
 them, run with its leader as $n: a word, MPSETVAR, MPCALLFUNC, MPQUESTWIN.  Arrived, it
stops following.  Its leader, arrival and remarks are kept in a saved game.
```

<a id="behavior-fieryroom"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_FIERYROOM

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 676.

```text
Behavior   : FieryRoom
Targets    : Rooms
Parameters : min, max ticks, a percent chance, flags and strings
Example    : min=5 max=10 chance=100;damage=77 Title="A Horribly
             Blackened Spot" Description="This place was once just like
             any part of the road.  Now it is nothing more than a sooty pit."
             NOSTOP eqchance=50
Description:
This behavior makes a room operate like it is on fire.  This can include dealing direct
damage to players, burning flammable equipment and making non-flammable equipment heat up
(i.e. is dropped), emote that it is burning, and eventually turn into a burnt-out room.
The first parameter can be empty for defaults, or may contain a setting for minimum ticks
(min=10), maximum ticks (max=20), and the percept chance of occurrence after the random
number of ticks has expired (chance=25).

Additional Settings and Flags:
DAMAGE=XXX         - The amount of damage dealt to inhabitants every behavior tick
TITLE=[text]       - The Room Display to change the room to when done burning
DESCRIPTION=[text] - The Room Desc to change the room to when done burning
EQCHANCE=XXX       - The unlikeliness of EQ bursting into flames or heating up.
BURNTICKS=XXX      - How many behavior ticks to keep burning (Moot with NOSTOP)
NOSTOP             - Prevent the room from ever burning up.  TITLE, DESCRIPTION and
                     BURNTICKS become irrelevant
NONPC              - Don't deal damage or eq burn/drop to NPC's
NOFIRETEXT         - Don't display burning emotes while the room is burning.

All of the parameters are optional. Defaults are:
DAMAGE=10
TITLE="A Charred Ruin"
DESCRIPTION="Whatever was once here is now nothing more than ash."
EQCHANCE=0  (no default Eq destruction)
BURNTICKS=12
```

<a id="behavior-floodable"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_FLOODABLE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1910.

```text
Behavior   : Floodable
Targets    : Rooms
Parameters : (RISE="[MASK]") (ONVAR="[HOST] [VAR]==[VALUE]") (TIDE=HIGH) (RATE=[TICKS])
(DRAIN=[TICKS]) (FLOWTO=[DIR]) (FLOAT=[WEIGHT]) (TITLE1= to TITLE3=) (DESC1= to DESC3=)
(MSG1= to MSG3=)
Example    : RISE="-WEATHER +RAIN +THUNDERSTORM" RATE=15 DRAIN=30 FLOWTO=east
Example    : ONVAR="pump sluice==open" RATE=5
Description:
CoffeeSUD: a room that floods, made from RoomStates, in levels: 0 dry, 1 ankle-deep, 2
waist-deep (one swims; loose things weighing up to FLOAT, 2 by default, float off through
FLOWTO, or away), 3 full (the air is water: one drowns once one's breath runs out).  While
RISE (a mask on someone standing there), ONVAR (a script variable) or TIDE holds, the water
rises a level each RATE ticks (10), else it drains a level each DRAIN ticks; rising water
puts out lights.  Each level may have its own TITLE, DESC and MSG (what those coming in are
told).  FLOODLEVEL() reads the level.
```

<a id="behavior-genbehavior"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_GENBEHAVIOR

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 800.

```text
Behavior   : GenBehavior (a generic behaviour: CREATE BEHAVIOR [ID])
Targets    : what its CANIMPROVE says: MOBs, ITEMs, ROOMs, AREAs, EXITs
Parameters : [NAME]=[VALUE]..., over the defaults its PARMS field gives
Example    : TollKeeper price=5 exit=west
Description:
CoffeeSUD: a behaviour defined as data, in builder mode.  CREATE BEHAVIOR TollKeeper makes
one and opens its editor: NAME, HELP (what AHELP TOLLKEEPER shows), CANIMPROVE (MOBS, ITEMS,
 ROOMS, AREAS, EXITS, with commas), PARMS with their defaults (price=20 exit=north), SCRIPT,
 ACCOUNT (what it says it is doing) and VARSCOPE (empty: its variables are its host's, as a
Scriptable's; *: its own).  The script is MOBPROG, with <SCRIPT> JavaScript in it if it
likes, or LOAD=[FILE]; it reads its parameters as PARM(price), $%PARM(price)% in text, IF
PARM(free) (set, and not 0 or false), and parm('price') in JavaScript.  Then TollKeeper
price=5 exit=west goes wherever a behaviour ID goes: on a mob or item, MPBEHAVE, a quest's
GIVE BEHAVIOR, a faction or a plane.  Each copy has its own engine and its own values; all
share the definition, so MODIFY BEHAVIOR TollKeeper changes every one at once.  MODIFY
BEHAVIOR [ID] [FIELD] [VALUE] sets one field without the editor (\
 in a SCRIPT is a new line).  WHEN=, TOD= and HOURS= work in its parameters as in any
behaviour's.  DESTROY BEHAVIOR [ID] removes it; what has it keeps it until the world is
loaded again.  SAVE writes it to the world's custom/behaviors/ folder, its script in a file
beside it.
```

<a id="behavior-healer"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_HEALER

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 862.

```text
Behavior   : Healer
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : min, max ticks, and a percent chance
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=75
Description:
The mob with this behavior gains Cure Disease, Cure Light Wounds, Cure Serious Wounds,
Bless, and Sanctuary.  At random, the mob will cast these spells on any player-mobs in the
room.

CoffeeSUD: SPELLS=[ID],[ID] its own spells in place of those six; HEALAT=[N] heals only
those under N% of their hit points, the most hurt first (its cures, for poison and disease,
first of all); TARGET=GROUP (its group) or TARGET=MASK:"[ZAPPER MASK]" whom it heals, NPCs
too.  With any of them it chooses whom it heals rather than at random.
Example    : min=1 max=2 chance=100 HEALAT=70 SPELLS=Prayer_CureSerious,Prayer_CureDisease
TARGET=MASK:"-NPC"
```

<a id="behavior-hireling"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_HIRELING

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 878.

```text
Behavior   : Hireling
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : price to hire;minutes of service
Example    : 10000;30
Description:
Allows a mob to hire him or herself out for a given amount of time. The first parameter is
the price to hire the mob, followed by a semicolon and the number of minutes that amount of
money purchases.  Additional money may be given by the player to extend the time.  When the
time expires, the mob returns to his or her start room.

CoffeeSUD: terms, KEY=value after them (quote a value with spaces): KEYWORDS=[WORD],... the
words that ask its terms (HIRE, HIRELING, WORK, WORKS, TIME, AVAILABLE); MSG_OFFER (@x1 the
price, @x2 the term), MSG_HIRED (@x1 the term, @x2 its skills), MSG_REFUSE, MSG_EXPIRE and
MSG_NOORDER, its own lines (Prop_NPCLines rewords the stock ones too); CONTRACT=MINUTES (the
 second number), DAYS (that many game days), "QUEST:[NAME]" (until the employer's quest is
won, failed or dropped) or UNTILFIRED (until SAY FIRED); UPKEEP=[N] wages a game day, taken
from the employer, who after two unpaid days is left; FLEEHP=[N]: below N% of its hit points
 in a fight it quits, unless its opinion of the employer (Prop_Affinity) is at least
LOYAL=[N] (25); REFUSE=[COMMAND],... orders it will not take.  The contract and wages are
kept in a saved game.  HIRE [MOB] shows its terms as a menu, and HIRE [MOB] PAY pays its
price.
Example    : 500;0;CONTRACT="QUEST:goblinwar" UPKEEP=5 MSG_HIRED="My blade is yours till the
 goblin king falls."
```

<a id="behavior-itemgenerator"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_ITEMGENERATOR

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 916.

```text
Behavior   : ItemGenerator
Targets    : Areas, Rooms, Containers, Mobs
Parameters : [min/max ticks] [% chance] [min/max items/dups] [enchanted=%][mobs] [locale
mask]; [mask]
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=75 minitems=1 maxitems=10 maxdups=0;-LEVELS +>10
Example    : minitems=10 maxitems=20 MOBS -ALL +CITY;-MATERIAL +IRON +BRONZE
Example    : minitems=10 maxitems=20 enchanted=20;-NAME "+Short Sword"
Description:
This behavior will generate a list of items from the standard common skills. It will also
add random enchantments and curses to items a percentage of the time dictated by the
enchanted parameter (default=10).  Items are selected from the list on a pseudo-random
basis, with the chance weighted in favor of the least valuable items in favor of the most
valuable.  This is to decrease the chances of a plethora of Spidersteel swords.

The parameters before the semicolon describe the rate and amount of items generated.  The
room or area will attempt to generate an item every (min) to (max) ticks, assuming the
percent chance (chance) is made.  It will then generate at least the minimum (minitems)
number of items from the list, but never more than the maximum (maxitems) number of
monsters.  Duplicates are allowed unless (maxdups) is set to some value.  Items taken away
will be replaced by this behavior, even if they are looted.  This behavior will generate
items when on a room, in the inventory when on a mob, or in the shop when on a shopkeeper.
If on an area, a random room in the area will be picked for the item. The TYPE of room in
that area which will be selected for population may also be specified. -ALL to disallow all
locales, followed by +AIR +CITY +JUNGLE (etc) to reallow certain locales.  -CITY -UNDERWATER
 and others may be used to restrict certain locales.  If no locale types are specified, then
 all rooms in an area will be populatable.  Valid locates include: "STONE",  "WOODEN",
"CAVE", "MAGIC", "UNDERWATER", "AIR", "WATERSURFACE", "METAL", "CITY", "WOODS", "ROCKY",
"PLAINS", "UNDERWATER", "AIR", "WATERSURFACE", "JUNGLE", "SWAMP", "DESERT", "HILLS",
"MOUNTAINS". If the behavior is on a mob, or the MOBS flag is given in the parameters, then
the item will be placed on a mob IF POSSIBLE (if the behavior is on an area, and a room with
 no mobs is randomly selected, it may not happen).  Items placed on mobs will be
automatically worn if possible.

The parameters after the semicolon are a mask to help select what kind of items are
generated for the several rooms or whatever.  For the mask flags, see AHELP ZAPPERMASK,
where allowed is generated, and disallowed is not.
```

<a id="behavior-itemupgrader"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_ITEMUPGRADER

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1024.

```text
Behavior   : ItemUpgrader
Targets    : MOBs, Items
Parameters : UPGRADE1="FROM=[NAME]|tag:[TAG]|catalog:[ITEM] TO=catalog:[ITEM]/ADJ=\"dam+[N]
att+[N] arm+[N]\" (COST=[GOLD]) (MATERIALS=\"[NAME] x[N], [NAME]\") (LEVEL=[N])
(KEEP=[KEEPS]) (MSG=\"[TEXT]\")" (UPGRADE2..9=) (UPGRADES=world/upgrades.txt)
Example    : UPGRADE1="FROM=notched TO=\"catalog:Starfall, the reforged blade\" COST=2000
MATERIALS=\"starmetal ingot x3\" LEVEL=20 KEEP=TAGS,STATE"
Description:
CoffeeSUD: a smith, or a workbench, that upgrades items along set paths.  Each row (UPGRADE1
 to 9, or one a line in the file UPGRADES names, the same keys) is FROM, the items it takes
(a name, tag:X or catalog:X, | between), and TO, a catalog item it becomes in its place
(held or worn as it was; KEEP as MPTRANSFORM's), or ADJ, the same item better (dam, att,
arm, lvl).  COST is gold, MATERIALS what is used up (x3 for three), LEVEL the least level,
MSG what is seen.  An item with Prop_UpgradePath carries its own row.  UPGRADE [ITEM] tells
what it would take; UPGRADE [ITEM] CONFIRM does it.
```

```text
Behavior   : JSBehavior
Targets    : Mobs, Items, Exits, Rooms, Areas
Parameters : SCRIPT=[FILE] ([NAME]=[VALUE])...
Example    : SCRIPT=world:js/props/bellringer.js EVERY=12
Description:
Runs a JavaScript file, as Prop_JScript does, that may define okMessage(host, msg) (false
refuses the message), executeMsg(host, msg), tick(host, tickID), onAdded(host),
onRemoved(host) and catchUp(host, ticks) (AHELP CATCHUP).  A behaviour is not asked for stat
 changes: Prop_JScript has those hooks.  What a hook changes in parms is written back to the
 behaviour's parameters.
```

<a id="behavior-jscriptable"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_JSCRIPTABLE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1050.

```text
Behavior   : JScriptable
Targets    : Mobs, Items, Exits, Rooms, Areas
Parameters : LOAD=[FILE] (SCOPE=[INDIVIDUAL/GLOBAL/NAME]), or the script itself
Example    : LOAD=world:js/npc/ferryman.js
Description:
Scripts its host wholly in JavaScript.  The script defines the handlers it wants: onLoad,
onGreet(who), onArrive(room), onLeave(who), onSpeech(who, text), onGive(who, item), onGet,
onDrop, onWear, onRemove (who, item), onOpen, onClose, onLock, onUnlock (who, thing),
onDeath(killer), onKill(victim), onDamage(who, amount), onCast(who, ability, target),
onLook(who), onTick, onHour(hour), onDay(day), onCommand(who, verb, rest) (true handles a
command typed near the host), canMessage(msg) (false refuses it), afterMessage(msg) and
onReload(old).  Its other functions answer MPCALLFUNC and CALLFUNC.  The script has me, cm,
CMMsg and state, the host's cm.store, saved with the game.  A SCOPE other than INDIVIDUAL
shares one script among the hosts that name it.  guides/JavaScriptSUD.html has a ferryman.
```

<a id="behavior-memory"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_MEMORY

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1082.

```text
Behavior   : Memory
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : (KIN="[MASK]") (TRACK=[NAME]:[REGEX]) (FORGET=[TIME]) (HOSTILEIF=[COND])
(GREETIF=[COND] GREET="[TEXT]") (REFUSEIF=[COND] REFUSE="[TEXT]") (SHARE=[AREA/MASK])
Example    : KIN="-NAMES +villager" SHARE=AREA HOSTILEIF=KILLEDKIN>0 REFUSEIF=STOLE>0
REFUSE="Thief! Out!" GREETIF=HEALED>0 GREET="Welcome back, $n." FORGET=30d
Description:
CoffeeSUD: the NPC remembers what each character did: MET (with FIRSTMET and LASTMET, game
dates), ATTACKED (once a fight), HURT (the damage), HEALED, GAVE (the value given), STOLE,
KILLEDKIN (of those KIN fits), TALKED, and TRACK=NAME:regex (TRACK1= to TRACK9= for more), a
 count of what it sees them do that the regex fits.  Each is a script variable of the NPC,
MEM_[FACT]_[NAME], so a script reads VAR($i MEM_ATTACKED_$n) or $<$i MEM_GAVE_$n>, and it is
 kept in a saved game.  FORGET=30d (or 12h) lets a fact fade that long, in game time, after
it last grew.  HOSTILEIF: it attacks them on sight.  GREETIF with GREET: it greets them when
 they come in ($n is their name).  REFUSEIF with REFUSE: it will not buy, sell or teach for
them.  A condition is FACT>N, FACT>=N, FACT=N or FACT<N, joined by & or |.  SHARE=AREA, or a
 mask, tells what it learns to the other Memory NPCs in its area (those the mask fits): rob
one villager and the village knows.
```

```text
dragons! You can set how often this occurs, and what % of the players max hp is taken from
```
