<a id="behavior-mobile"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_MOBILE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1160.

```text
Behavior   : Mobile
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : min, max ticks, a percent chance, flags, locale parms
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=75 wander -air -underwater
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=75 opendoors
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=75 leash=3 opendoors
Description:
According to the timing and percent chance described by the parameters, the mob with this
behavior will travel in a random available direction. Mobs will not leave rooms containing
visible Archons and builders with the CMDMOBS security flag. The wander flag is required if
the mob is allowed to leave his or her area. The opendoors flag will allow the mob to open
closed doors when walking around, or to unlock locked doors if the mob has the key. The
leash parameter will prevent the mob from getting too far from home. The TYPE of room from
which the mob is restricted may also be entered. -ALL to disallow all locales, followed by
+AIR +CITY +JUNGLE (etc) to reallow certain locales.  -CITY -UNDERWATER and others may be
used to restrict certain locales.  The full locale list is: STONE, WOODEN, CAVE, MAGIC,
UNDERWATER, AIR, WATERSURFACE, METAL , CITY, WOODS, ROCKY, PLAINS, JUNGLE, SWAMP, DESERT,
HILLS, MOUNTAINS, SPACEPORT, SEAPORT
```

<a id="behavior-mobileaggressive"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_MOBILEAGGRESSIVE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1184.

```text
Behavior   : MobileAggressive
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : min, max ticks, a percent chance, flags, message=[msg], and masks
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=75 -underwater -thief +elf
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=75 wander -air -elf
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=75 message="aha!" -air -elf
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=75 mobkill misbehave
Description:
According to the timing and percent chance described by the parameters, the mob with this
behavior will travel in a random available direction. The mob will attack any player mob it
comes across. They will be especially aggressive towards players within 16 levels of
themselves in adjacent rooms. If no other parameters are given, the mob will attack anyone,
anywhere. The wander flag is required if the mob is allowed to leave his or her area. The
TYPE of room from which the mob is restricted may also be entered. -ALL to disallow all
locales, followed by +AIR +CITY +JUNGLE (etc) to reallow certain locales.  -CITY -UNDERWATER
 and others may be used to restrict certain locales. The full locale list is: STONE, WOODEN,
 CAVE, MAGIC, UNDERWATER, AIR, WATERSURFACE, METAL , CITY, WOODS, ROCKY, PLAINS, JUNGLE,
SWAMP, DESERT, HILLS, MOUNTAINS, SPACEPORT, SEAPORT.

Masks may also be used to specify who the mob is likely to attack.  Mobs will not be mobile
or aggressive towards Archons and builders with the CMDMOBS security flag. If no other masks
 are given, the mob will attack anyone within 8 levels.
Valid aggressive masks include:
message=[msg] something for the mob to say whenever he's fixing to attack
delay=x (makes the mob delay x ticks before looking for a victim)
mobkill (makes this behavior attack mobs as well as players)
nogang (makes this behavior pass over players already in combat)
misbehave (makes this mob attack even when wounded or a follower)
checklevel (makes this mob attack only those within 6 levels below him)
BRIBE=[AMOUNT],[TICKS OF PEACE],[TICKS TO PAY] - this is a comma-delimited
BRIBEPAYMSG=x, BRIBEPAIDMSG=x, (see also ahelp on AGGRESSIVE BRIBE)
See AHELP ZAPPERMASK, where allowed is attacked, and disallowed is spared.
```

<a id="behavior-mobteacher"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_MOBTEACHER

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1257.

```text
Behavior   : MOBTeacher
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : Char class name(s), ability name(s), expertise name(s), [pct%],
Parameters : noteach flag, nocommon flag, noexps flag, or empty=teach all.
Example    : mage evoker illusionist transmuter
Example    : 100% mage 10% Thief_Steal NOCOMMON
Example    : Spell_Sleep 5% Spell_Wish
Example    : Spell_BurningHands
Description:
This behavior makes the mob suitable to teach skills, spells, prayers, songs, or expertises
as specified in the parameters.  If the parameter is empty, the mob will be able to teach
all abilities.  If the parameter contains the name of a character class, the mob will only
teach abilities of that class. *Any* class may always practice with a MOBTeacher, but the
mob may only teach those abilities for the character class the parameters describe.  The
classes listed by mob teacher are NOT base classes.  To have a teacher able to teach skills
from an entire base class, all sub-classes must be listed.
Percentages may be included inside the parameters as well.  The percentage will always apply
 only to the character classes or spells listed after the percentage, not before.
Encountering another percentage entry will override the previous.  A percentage will dictate
 the chance that a given spell will be known by the teacher, or the chance that a particular
 spell in a given character class will be known.
Two flags can also modify your list.  The NOCOMMON flag prevents the teacher from teaching
common skills, even if they would normally be on his list.  The NOEXPS flag prevents the
teacher from teaching expertises, even if he would normally qualify for them.
If this behavior has NO parameters whatsoever, the mob will teach all basic skills.
Expertises will only be taught if the mob otherwise qualifies for them himself, and
Character Class changes will only be taught if the mob is that class. The noteach flag will
prevent the mob from teacher or using all those awesome skills.
Example    : Prayer_Bless Prayer_Sanctuary STUDENTMASK="-CLANRANK '+Temple of
Arden>=ACOLYTE'" SKILLMASK.Prayer_Sanctuary="-CLANRANK '+Temple of Arden>=PRIEST'" PRICE="5
per level"
CoffeeSUD: the teacher's rules, in any order among the rest: STUDENTMASK="[ZAPPER MASK]"
(whom it teaches at all; REFUSEMSG="[TEXT]" is what it says to others), SKILLMASK.[ABILITY
ID]="[ZAPPER MASK]" (whom it teaches that skill), PRICE="[N] per level" or PRICE=[N] (money
it takes for each lesson, on top of the usual cost) and HIDDEN=[ID],[ID] (skills it teaches
but leaves off TEACHLIST).  They gate TEACH ME, GAIN, PRACTICE and TRAIN with it, and TRAIN
with no trainer named passes over one who refuses.  TEACHLIST shows a student what this
teacher offers them.
```

<a id="behavior-moneychanger"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_MONEYCHANGER

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1293.

```text
Behavior   : MoneyChanger
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : (CUT=[NUM]) (DEFAULT=[NUM]) ([CURRENCY]=[NUM])
Parameters : (CUT=[NUM]) (SPACEMAXCUT=[NUM]) (SPACEMAXDISTANCE=[PCT])
Parameters : (RATE.[CURRENCY]=+[PCT]/-[PCT])
Example    :
Example    : cut=5
Example    : default=0 GOLD=5 INGITS=10
Example    : cut=5 spacemaxcut=90 spacemaxdistance=35
Example    : cut=5 RATE.CROWN=-30 RATE.LEAF=+10
Description:
CoffeeSUD: RATE.[CURRENCY] is a premium (+) or discount (-) in percent on what coins of that
 currency fetch, before the cut (RATE.DEFAULT for the default currency); it is no fee, so
the changer still takes every currency.  MPEXCHANGE sets a rate for every money changer in
the world, kept in the save.
Whenever a player gives the money changer coins, the money changer will give back to the
player a bag containing an equivalent amount of money in the money changers native currency.
  The "cut" that the money changer takes, in general, can be defined with the CUT parameter,
 by making CUT equal to a percentage.  If you wish, you can also define exchange rates for
the several currencies in your system by setting each currency name equal to a percentage.

When dealing with intersteller currencies, there are two other parameters, which can be used
 to automatically calculate a scaled "cut" of the exchange based on how far away the
exchanged currencies planet is from the money changers.  To do this, you can add spacemaxcut
 to denote the percentage to take when the currency is from an unknown or maximum distance,
and spacemaxdistance to denote a percentage of the entire galactic radius to use as a
maximum.
```

<a id="behavior-morale"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_MORALE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1322.

```text
Behavior   : Morale
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : (FLEEAT=[N]%) (OUTNUMBERED=[X]) (BREAK=LEADERDEAD,[N]%DEAD,HP<[N]%)
(LEADER="[ZAPPER MASK]") (ACTION=FLEE/SURRENDER/BERSERK) (CHANCE=[N]) (MSG="[TEXT]")
(RALLY=[ROOM ID]/HOME REGROUP=[N]) (SURRENDERAT=[N]%) (SURRENDERMSG="[TEXT]")
(BRAVE="[ZAPPER MASK]")
Example    : FLEEAT=40% BREAK=LEADERDEAD ACTION=FLEE RALLY=Warren#12 REGROUP=15
Example    : SURRENDERAT=20% SURRENDERMSG="Mercy! I'll show you the loot!"
Description:
CoffeeSUD: the mob's nerve breaks: when its hit points fall under FLEEAT, when its foes here
 outnumber its side OUTNUMBERED to one, or as BREAK says: LEADERDEAD (its leader dies: the
one LEADER names, or the mob it follows), [N]%DEAD (that share of its side has fallen),
HP<[N]% (its side's hit points together).  Its side is its group, its leader's, and NPCs of
its race here who fight.  Then, at CHANCE percent a tick (100), it says MSG (":text" for an
emote) and does ACTION: FLEE (to RALLY, a room ID or HOME, where it waits REGROUP ticks
(10), then comes back with the NPCs it finds there following it, and attacks the ones it
fled from), SURRENDER, or BERSERK (a third more damage and a tenth less attack until the
fight ends).  Under SURRENDERAT it surrenders whatever else: it drops its weapon, its foes
and it make peace, it says SURRENDERMSG, and its scripts' SURRENDER_PROG runs ($n one it
fought).  BRAVE: those the mask fits never break.
```

<a id="behavior-movingroom"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_MOVINGROOM

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1408.

```text
Behavior   : Mover
Targets    : Rooms
Parameters : min=3 max=3 chance=100;[xmlsection];[ticks at stops];[ticks between stops]
Example    : min=3 max=3 chance=100;SUBWAY;3;10
Description:
The above example would set the room's parameters to the ones listed in the SUBWAY section
of the file resources/moving.xml.  There is a subway example already there.
NOTE!      : The follow conditions -must- be met before setting the room to this behaviour.
1.
The rooms that you want this room to open out to -must- already be defined before you make
the XML section.
2.
The XML document -must- be writen before you set this behaviour.
3.
You -cannot- have the moving room override an exit, ie. if room A links south to Room B
you cannot have the mover link north to room A.
*******************
XML DOCUMENT NOTES:
*******************
You can use the following strings in the XML document to be translated on the fly
$disproom  : if mover is at a stop this is the room it is opened to otherwise
. Example  : this is the next room that this room will open too.
$inopendir : this is the direction the door on the inside (the mover) opens.
$outopendir: this is the direction the door on the outside (where the mover stoped) opens.
$traveldir : this is the current direction that the room is moving in.

<STOPS> here you would list the ROOMID of each room the mover will stop at example.
<STOP1>[first stop]</STOP1>n
<NORMALDIRECTION> and <REVERSEDIRECTION>
-in these tags you define the parameters for the mover while is is going back and forth.
-normal is stop1 to stopwhatever and reverse is stopwhatever to stop1.
-TRAVELDIRECTION = the direction it is traveling from point a to point b.
-DOORSDIRECTION = the direction the doors open out of the mover.
--<INSIDE> and <OUTSIDE>
---in these tags you define what is echoed to the client in the mover and outside.
---ARRIVALINFO = what is echoed when the room gets to the stop
---DEPARTINFO = what is echoed when the room leaves the stop
<ROOMDESCRIPTIONS>
-here you define what is appended to the end of the room descriptions.
-<NORMALDIRECTION> and <REVERSEDIRECTION>
--<INSIDE> and <OUTSIDE>
---DOOROPENED = if the door is opened append this.
---DOORCLOSED = if the door is closed append this.

There are two examples in the XML document you can look at for further info.

Ideas for this would be, subways, busses, wagon trains (caravans) spaceships, stargates,
everchanging paths in mazes, elevators, ect.
CoffeeSUD: ROUTE=[file under world/routes/] or ROUTE="[inline XML]", LINE=[section],
WAIT=[ticks at stops], TRAVEL=[ticks per leg], DEPART=[game hours, comma separated],
SIGN="[item name]". Position, direction and remaining time are saved. Boarding exits and
descriptive text are temporary overlays excluded from export. TIMETABLE shows the line and
position. The legacy file is resources/movingroom.xml.
```

<a id="behavior-mudchat"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_MUDCHAT

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1340.

```text
Behavior   : MudChat
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : (([data file]=)[group])(+[extra entries]
Example    : smurf
Example    : chat.dat=smurf
Example    : chat.dat=smurf+(smurfy);9Smurfy!
Example    : mychat.dat=cityguard
Example    : mychat.dat=
Example    : +(here there);9neither;5well, where?;1nowhere
Description:
Allows the mobs to speak and respond to speech.  The chat.dat file, from which speech
behavior is derived, contains many "templates" for different speech behaviors.  MudChat will
 attempt to choose the correct speech behavior for the mob based on the mobs name.  This may
 be overridden by specifying a speech behavior in the parameter [group].  Speech patterns in
 the chat.dat at present include: default, dog fido beastly fido_dog, cat kitten lion, pig
boar, doll toy, papa_smurf smurf, monster, smurfette, healer cleric doctor.

If the first character in the parameters is a +plus-sign, then a semi-colon delimited list
of chat data is expected, in the same format as is found in chat.dat.

If a +plus-sign occurs after the data file and/or group name, then new entries may be added
that way also, with the entry lines semi-colon delimited as above.

CoffeeSUD: DELAY=[N] anywhere in the parameters is how many ticks it waits before it answers
 (2).  When replies come at once (DIALOGUETIME, TIMEMODE DIALOGUE), its answer comes before
the player's next prompt whatever the delay.

CoffeeSUD, in a chat file: a line ?[CONDITION] before an entry is a script condition, as
after IF, that must hold for it: $t and $n are the speaker, $i the mob, as in
?QUESTSCRIPTED($t mine) and VAR($t MET == 1).  A reply starting with & runs the rest as a
MOBPROG line, the mob its host and the speaker $n (9"Clear the rats.~&mpsetvar $n JOB
given).  $@[GROUP] at a reply's end switches to that group for that speaker alone, for six
minutes; $@![GROUP] until it is changed, kept in the saved variable MUDCHAT_GROUP_[SPEAKER]
of the mob; $@- back to the base group.
```

<a id="behavior-nanny"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_NANNY

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 255.

```text
Behavior   : Nanny
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : RATE=[PRICE] NAME="[PLACE NAME]" WATCHES="[CODES]" (|~| [XML])
Example    : rate=2.5 name="The Stables" watches="mounts,wagons"
Description:
Makes the mob a protector and watcher of mobs and items of various sorts, for money. The
rate parameter describes the base gold value he charges for each thing dropped off, per
hour.  The name is a description of the type of place he runs.  The watches parameter
contains one or more comma-delimited words (no spaces!) describing the kinds of things he
will charge people to watch and protect, and may include one or more of the following:
babies - baby items born from mud breeding
children - child mobs (after babies grow up)
mounts - rideable mobs of all sorts
cars - land-rideable items that aren't wagons
aircars - air-rideable items
wagons - rideable land items that are wagons
followers - mobs that aren't children, mounts, etc.
boats - rideable items of the sea

This behavior will automatically save the items and mobs in the room he is watching over,
and prevent items from decay.  Combat against himself or mobs under protection is forbidden,
 as is removing any mob or item that has not been paid for.  The first mud-hour is free, and
 protection will not begin until the owner leaves.

NOTE - due to the way this behavior stores records, do not place this behavior on a mob that
 is cataloged in the CATALOG system.
CoffeeSUD: NETWORK=[name] links sister stables; SENDFEE=[price] adds a remote retrieval fee.
 STABLE <mount>, STABLE LIST and RETRIEVE <mount> manage explicit custody. Owners can
collect mounts from another keeper in the network, paying accrued keep plus the send fee.
These requests also work in speech; custody and payment records survive saves.
```

<a id="behavior-niceabilities"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_NICEABILITIES

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1490.

```text
Behavior   : NiceAbilities
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : (MIN=X MAX=X CHANCE=X) (; [ZAPPERMASK])
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=75
Example    : min=10 ; -RACE +ELF
Description:
According to the timing and percent chance described by the parameters, the mob with this
behavior will use any of its benevolent abilities, including spells, prayers, songs, or
others, for the benefit of player mobs in the same room.  If a zappermask is specified, the
benefits only go to the matching.

CoffeeSUD: HEALAT=[N] before the ; has it heal the most hurt of those it helps who are under
 N% of their hit points, and nothing else.
Example    : min=1 max=1 HEALAT=60 ; -RACE +Goblin
```

<a id="behavior-patroller"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_PATROLLER

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1530.

```text
Behavior   : Patroller
Targets    : MOBs, Items
Parameters : min, max ticks, % chance, rideok flag, diameter; room ids or directions
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=75 rideok=true;Midgaard#3001;#3002;#3003;RESTART
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=99 rideok=only;Midgaard#3001;#3002;#3003;RESTART
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=15;east;.;north;north;east
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=15 diameter=100;Midgaard#1;New Thalos#10;.;.;restart
Description:
According to the timing and percent chance described by the parameters, the mob or item with
 this behavior will travel the path assigned in the parameters.  Cardinal directions and
room numbers are all valid entries, though the cardinal directions must always be valid from
 the objects current position to work.  The 'RESTART' parameter may be placed in the path to
 force the object to start the path from the beginning.  If no 'RESTART' parameter is given,
 the object will by default retrace their steps back to the beginning of the path.  The '.'
parameter (a period) in the path will direct the patroller to pause one step at that point.
  If any doors are encountered along the patrol route, they will be unlocked and opened by a
 mob.  Items will ignore doors. If a route of room ids is given, the patroller will
automatically "track" from their current position to the next room on their patrol list,
even if it is not adjacent. The diameter parameter should be enlarged when it is possible
for the patroller to become more that 20 rooms "off track".

By default, rideable mobs and items will stop patrolling when they are ridden.  Setting
rideok to true will make it so that they continue their patrol even when ridden, though they
 can still be driven by passengers.  Setting rideok to only will keep the rideable on track,
 and prevent driving by passengers.

See Prop_StayAboard for a helpful support property for patrollers with riders.

CoffeeSUD: more steps.  WAIT=[N] waits N ticks; DO=[COMMAND] has it do a command (DO=lock
door, DO=say Gate secure.); EMOTE=[TEXT] an emote; IF=[MASK] goes on only if the mask fits
the patroller, else to the next RESTART (or the start).  These are not walked back on a
route with no RESTART.  ROUTE=[NAME]:[FIRST STEP];... starts a named route, its steps up to
the next ROUTE=: the one named for the time of day (DAWN, DAY, DUSK or NIGHT) is walked,
else ROUTE=DEFAULT, else the first, from its start when it changes.  RESUME=true with the
ticks: after a fight it walks back to where it left its route before going on.
Example    : min=3 max=3;Gate#1;WAIT=5;DO=say Gate secure.;Wall#4;EMOTE=peers over the
battlements.;RESTART
Example    : min=3
max=3;ROUTE=DAY:Gate#1;Wall#4;RESTART;ROUTE=NIGHT:Barracks#1;Barracks#2;RESTART
```

<a id="behavior-pursue"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_PURSUE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1593.

```text
Behavior   : Pursue
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : (CHANCE=[N]) (MAXROOMS=[N]) (DELAY=[N]) (MASK="[ZAPPER MASK]") (LEASH=[N])
(STAY) (GIVEUPMSG="[TEXT]") (REMEMBER=[N])
Example    : CHANCE=80 MAXROOMS=4 LEASH=8
Example    : CHANCE=50 MAXROOMS=10 MASK="-RACES +Goblin" REMEMBER=30
Description:
CoffeeSUD: the mob chases one who flees it.  CHANCE is the percent chance it gives chase
(60), MASK whom it chases.  It follows them room by room, a room a tick after DELAY ticks
(1), and attacks them where it catches them; past MAXROOMS rooms in all (3), or LEASH rooms
from home, or when it loses the trail, it gives up (GIVEUPMSG, "<S-NAME> give(s) up the
chase.") and walks home, or with STAY stays where it is.  REMEMBER=[N]: one who fled it and
comes back within N ticks is attacked on sight.
```

<a id="behavior-questchat"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_QUESTCHAT

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1378.

```text
Behavior   : QuestChat
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : optional or additional chat data, or filenames ,or chat-mob-type
Example    : smurf
Example    : +(here there);9neither;5well, where?;1nowhere
Example    : chat.dat=smurf
Example    : mychat.dat=cityguard
Example    : mychat.dat=
Example    : +(speak | talk | words::DONE_SPEAKING);9only said this to YOU once.
Description:
An extension of the MudChat behavior, with a special feature for Quests. Allows the mobs to
speak and respond to speech.  The chat.dat file, from which speech behavior is derived,
contains many "templates" for different speech behaviors.  MudChat will attempt to choose
the correct speech behavior for the mob based on the mobs name.  This may be overridden by
specifying a speech behavior in the parameters.  This behavior extends the basic
functionality of MudChat in the following ways:

1. If the first character in the parameters is a plus-sign, then a semi-colon delimited list
 of chat data is expected, in the same format as is found in chat.dat.

2. If format#1 is used, the trigger pattern may be followed by a double-colon, and then
immediately by a variable string.   This string will designate that the given pattern is
only responded to for a given player ONCE.  The string will also be added to a list of
strings under the players name in any Quest object. This list will then be available through
 a Scriptable QVAR function, as QVAR(questname CHAT:PLAYERNAME), and it is what the mob goes
 by: it lasts for the run of the quest, and a saved game keeps it.
```

<a id="behavior-randomencounters"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_RANDOMENCOUNTERS

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1619.

```text
Behavior   : RandomEncounters
Targets    : Areas, Rooms
Parameters : TABLE=[NAME] (CHANCE=[N]%) (COOLDOWN=[N]/[N]DAYS) (LOCALES="[KIND],[KIND]")
(TRIGGER="[ZAPPER MASK]") (MAXACTIVE=[N]) (DESPAWN=[N]) (BUDGET=[N]%)
Example    : TABLE=darkwood CHANCE=10% COOLDOWN=6
Example    : TABLE=moors CHANCE=15% LOCALES="PLAINS,HILLS" TRIGGER="-LEVEL +>3" BUDGET=80%
Description:
CoffeeSUD: as the party moves, each room it enters may bring an encounter from the table
world/encounters/NAME.enc (AHELP ENCOUNTER), rolled on the next tick for the one who leads
the party in (if they are still there).  CHANCE is the percent a room (10); COOLDOWN=N lets
N rooms go by after one, N DAYS game days; LOCALES the kinds of room (WOODS, PLAINS,
CITY...); TRIGGER a mask on the one who came in; MAXACTIVE the monsters of its encounters
about at once (6); DESPAWN how many ticks they stay once the party has left them (10),
unless fighting; BUDGET adds MOBS entries until the monsters' power is that share of the
party's (C15's mob ranks count).
```

<a id="behavior-randomitems"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_RANDOMITEMS

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1634.

```text
Behavior   : RandomItems
Targets    : Areas, Rooms, Containers, Mobs
Parameters : [min/max ticks] [% chance] [min/max items] [mobs] [locale mask]; [xml/filename]
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=75 minitems=1 maxitems=10;myitems.cmare
Example    : minitems=10 maxitems=20 MOBS -ALL +CITY;stuff.cmare
Example    : minitems=10 maxitems=20 ;<ITEMS><ITEM>..etc..
Example    : maxitems=3 CATALOG="pine cone=5,amber=1" DESPAWN=TICKS=200
Description:
This behavior will read a list of items from a CMARE file of items generated using the
"EXPORT AREA ITEMS" or "EXPORT ROOM ITEMS" command.  The path to this file should be the
last parameter, following a semicolon.  The path is considered relative to the CoffeeMud
resources directory.  The xml from such a file may also be pasted in as the last parameter
instead.

The parameters before the semicolon describe the rate and amount of items generated.  The
room or area will attempt to generate an item every (min) to (max) ticks, assuming the
percent chance (chance) is made.  It will then generate at least the minimum (minitems)
number of items from the list, but never more than the maximum (maxitems) number of
monsters.  Duplicates are allowed.  Items taken away will be replaced by this behavior, even
 if they are looted.  If the behavior is on a room, all items will be generated in that
room.  If on an area, a random room in the area will be picked for the item. The TYPE of
room in that area which will be selected for population may also be specified. -ALL to
disallow all locales, followed by +AIR +CITY +JUNGLE (etc) to reallow certain locales.
-CITY -UNDERWATER and others may be used to restrict certain locales.  If no locale types
are specified, then all rooms in an area will be populatable.  Valid locates include:
"STONE",       "WOODEN", "CAVE", "MAGIC", "UNDERWATER", "AIR", "WATERSURFACE", "METAL",
"CITY", "WOODS", "ROCKY", "PLAINS", "UNDERWATER", "AIR", "WATERSURFACE", "JUNGLE", "SWAMP",
"DESERT", "HILLS", "MOUNTAINS". If the behavior is on a mob, or the MOBS flag is given in
the parameters, then the item will be placed on a mob IF POSSIBLE (if the behavior is on an
area, and a room with no mobs is randomly selected, it may not happen).  Items placed on
mobs will be automatically worn if possible.   If the behavior is on a shopkeeper, it will
put the items up for sale.

CoffeeSUD spawn rules, before the semicolon (or with no semicolon and no file):
CATALOG="name=weight,name=weight" picks the catalog's entries by weight (counted and capped
as catalog: is); WHEN="[ZAPPER MASK]" is tested on the room a spawn would go to (-SEASON
+WINTER, -HOUR +20, -LOCATION +ROOMSTR(moonlit)...), and nothing spawns where it fails;
DESPAWN=WHENFALSE (when the mask no longer passes where it is), DAWN (at dawn or by day) or
TICKS=[N] (N of the behavior's ticks after it came) makes a spawn leave, unseen: not while a
 player is in its room, nor while it fights; on an area, NEAR=PARTY:[N] spawns only within N
 rooms of the player's side, and MAXAREA=[N] spawns nothing while the area holds N spawns
(of any spawner).  The rules for rooms (WHEN, NEAR, MAXAREA, DESPAWN) are for items left in
rooms.
```

<a id="behavior-randommonsters"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_RANDOMMONSTERS

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1683.

```text
Behavior   : RandomMonsters
Targets    : Areas, Rooms
Parameters : [min/max ticks] [% chance] [min/max monsters] [locale mask]; [xml/filename]
Example    : min=10 max=20 chance=75 minmonsters=1 maxmonsters=10;monsters.cmare
Example    : minmonsters=10 maxmonsters=20 -ALL +CITY;criminals.cmare
Example    : minmonsters=10 maxmonsters=20 ;<MOBS><MOB>..etc..
Example    : minmonsters=2 maxmonsters=4;catalog:a goblin,a goblin shaman
Example    : maxmonsters=6 CATALOG="grey wolf=4,dire wolf=1" WHEN="-SEASON +WINTER"
DESPAWN=DAWN NEAR=PARTY:3 LEVEL=PARTY+-2
Description:
This behavior will read a list of monsters from a CMARE file of mobs generated using the
"EXPORT AREA MOBS" or "EXPORT ROOM MOBS" command.  The path to this file should be the last
parameter, following a semicolon.  The path is considered relative to the CoffeeMud
resources directory.  The xml from such a file may also be pasted in as the last parameter
instead.
Or the last parameter may be catalog:NAME,NAME, the catalog's mobs: their copies are
counted, and none is made past an entry's cap.

The parameters before the semicolon describe the rate and amount of monsters generated.  The
 room or area will attempt to generate a monster every (min) to (max) ticks, assuming the
percent chance (chance) is made.  It will then generate at least the minimum (minmonsters)
number of monsters from the list, but never more than the maximum (maxmonsters) number of
monsters.  Duplicates are allowed.  Monsters who die will be replaced by this behavior, even
 if they wander out of the room or area.  If the behavior is on a room, all monsters will be
 generated in that room.  If on an area, a random room in the area will be picked for the
monster. The TYPE of room in that area which will be selected for population may also be
specified. -ALL to disallow all locales, followed by +AIR +CITY +JUNGLE (etc) to reallow
certain locales.  -CITY -UNDERWATER and others may be used to restrict certain locales.  If
no locale types are specified, then all rooms in an area will be populatable.  By default,
non-flying mobs will never be generated in air rooms, nor will non-swimming mobs be
generated underwater. Valid locates include: "STONE", "WOODEN", "CAVE", "MAGIC",
"UNDERWATER", "AIR", "WATERSURFACE", "METAL", "CITY", "WOODS", "ROCKY", "PLAINS",
"UNDERWATER", "AIR", "WATERSURFACE", "JUNGLE", "SWAMP", "DESERT", "HILLS", "MOUNTAINS".

CoffeeSUD spawn rules, before the semicolon (or with no semicolon and no file):
CATALOG="name=weight,name=weight" picks the catalog's entries by weight (counted and capped
as catalog: is); WHEN="[ZAPPER MASK]" is tested on the room a spawn would go to (-SEASON
+WINTER, -HOUR +20, -LOCATION +ROOMSTR(moonlit)...), and nothing spawns where it fails;
DESPAWN=WHENFALSE (when the mask no longer passes where it is), DAWN (at dawn or by day) or
TICKS=[N] (N of the behavior's ticks after it came) makes a spawn leave, unseen: not while a
 player is in its room, nor while it fights; on an area, NEAR=PARTY:[N] spawns only within N
 rooms of the player's side, and MAXAREA=[N] spawns nothing while the area holds N spawns
(of any spawner).  LEVEL=PARTY, PARTY+[N], PARTY-[N] or PARTY+-[N] makes each spawn the
level of the party's highest, give or take, its stats by the level formulas.
```

<a id="behavior-randomquests"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_RANDOMQUESTS

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1731.

```text
Behavior   : RandomQuests
Targets    : Areas, Mobs
Parameters : (MIN=[TICKS]) (MAX=[TICKS]) (CHANCE=[0-100]) ([var=value] ...)
Example    : minquests=3 maxquests=5 template=normal_capture1
Description:
This behavior will generate a random quest inside a host area, or generate a random quest on
 behalf of the host mob.  The arguments are all optional, and are numerous:
MIN, MAX, and CHANCE determine how frequently an attempt will be made to generate a quest.
Be generous with this, as quest generation is a cpu-intensive process.  Default is 10-20
ticks.
MINQUESTS, MAXQUESTS determine how many quests will be generated at one time. If any
existing quests ellapse, then new ones will be generated.  Default is 1-3 quests.  If
multiple quests are offered by the same mob, then, by default, the player must complete each
 one in order.
PATH is used to specify the xml document to read the random quest data from. Default is
randareas/example.xml.
TAGID is the tag of the QUEST object inside the PATH document to generate. Default is
"all_quests".
EXPIRE is the amount of time a quest will run for before expiring forever. Expiration occurs
 even if a quest is accepted moments before.  The default is "3 hours".
MAXATTEMPTS is the number of attempts that will be made to generate a particular quest.
This is necessary because not all areas, people, or circumstances will support evey quest
type.  The default is 3.

A saved game keeps the quests this behavior generated, whole, with their progress, and a
restore makes them again; the behavior takes them back rather than generating others.

The following are not aspects of this behavior, but are variables passed on to the
percolator who generates the quests, and are only meaningful because of their definitions in
 /resources/quests/random/*.xml.
TEMPLATE is the name of the quest template to use.  Default is normal.
AVOIDSCANS can be set to YES to avoid quest templates that scan an entire area.
AREA_NAME can override the name of the areas where the announcer is found.
SOURCE_NAME can override the name of the quest announcer.
TARGETAREA_NAME can override the name of the area where the quest occurs.
MULTIAREA can be set to YES to allow the quest to occur other than the source area.
TARGETNAME is quest-type specific, but can mean the name of a quest target mob or item.
NUM_TARGETS is quest-type specific, but can mean the number of items/mobs to target.
AGGRESSION is quest-type specific, but can be set to YES or NO.
XP_AMOUNT_AWARDED is the amount of xp to award for completing a quest.
GOLD_AMOUNT_AWARDED is the amount of money to award for completing a quest.
SOURCE_FACTION and SOURCE_FACTION_AMT are the faction (its ID) the quest's giver belongs to
and how far, picked from the giver; the reward templates use them to award faction with the
giver, as SOURCE_FACTION_AMT / 500.
QUEST_POINT_AWARDED can be set to YES or NO.
QUEST_MULTIPLE can be set to YES, NO, or PREV
ANNOUNCECHANNEL can be anything from SAY, LOCAL, QUESTCHAT, etc.
TARGET_MIN_AREALEVEL AND TARGET_MAX_AREALEVEL to set a range for randomly picked target
areas
```

<a id="behavior-regenerate"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_REGENERATE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1799.

```text
Behavior   : Regenerate
Targets    : Areas
Parameters : (FILE=[TEMPLATE] ID=[AREA ID] VARS="[VAR]=[VAL] ...")
(SEED=RANDOM/DAILY/WEEKLY/SAME/[N])
Parameters : (WHEN=MUDDAY:[N],MOON:[PHASE],ONEMPTY,SCRIPT) (KEEP="[ROOM ID] ...")
Example    : WHEN=MOON:FULL SEED=RANDOM
Example    : WHEN=ONEMPTY SEED=DAILY KEEP="Old Tunnels#0"
Description:
CoffeeSUD: the area re-rolls itself.  It is built again from FILE and ID (with VARS), or
from its GENSOURCE (what GENERATE AREA recorded) when they are left out, as REGENERATE AREA
does: the rooms marked GENLOCK, the rooms KEEP names and the rooms a running quest uses (or
someone or something in them) stay as they are, the rest are made again, and the gate and
every other exit go to the rooms of the same IDs.  WHEN is one or more of MUDDAY:N (every N
days of the area's calendar), MOON:FULL (or another phase: NEW, WAXCRESCENT, ... as it
begins), ONEMPTY (as the party leaves, so it is fresh when they come back) and SCRIPT (only
when MPREGENERATE asks; the default).  SEED is RANDOM (a new one each time, the default),
DAILY or WEEKLY (one for the game day or week: the same all that day), SAME (the
GENSOURCE's) or a number.  It never re-rolls while a player, or one following a player, is
inside: it waits for them to leave.  The area's GENERATED_PROG runs after.  Its STATE (when
the days count from, the moon last seen, a re-roll waiting) is kept in a saved game; the
rooms are kept as rooms changed in play.
```

<a id="behavior-resetwhole"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_RESETWHOLE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1820.

```text
Behavior   : ResetWhole
Targets    : Rooms, Areas
Parameters : # of ticks of inactivity before reset
Parameters : (TICKS=[INACTIVITY TICKS])/(RLHOUR=[HOUR])/(MUDHOUR=[HOUR])
Parameters : (DAYS=[GAME DAYS]) (EXCEPT="[MASK]") (MSG="[TEXT]")
Example    : 4000
Example    : DAYS=7 EXCEPT="-NAME +'the Goblin King'" MSG="Fresh tracks lead into the
tunnels."
Description:
This behavior provides an alternative means of resetting your rooms and areas.  The system
will total reset a room (mobs and items) which has not been visited by a player in the given
 amount of ticks.  Remember that a tick is about 4 seconds. You can alternatively specify a
real life hour (0-23) or mud hour of the day with the RLHOUR or MUDHOUR parameters.
CoffeeSUD: DAYS is game days on the area's calendar after the party was last there, in place
 of TICKS. EXCEPT is a mask of the mobs and items that never come back once gone: a slain
boss or taken loot stays gone, one still there at the reset stays; a name with spaces goes
in single quotes, +'the Goblin King'.  MSG is shown to the first who comes in after a reset.
  RLHOUR reads the real clock, which means nothing with pause and turn-based time; use
MUDHOUR or DAYS. An Area with this behavior will skip over any rooms which also have this
behavior, allowing you to have different total reset times for certain rooms.  Of course,
this behavior does not override the existing REJUV system for mobs and items, so if you
would like to use the ResetWhole system exclusively, you should set the rejuv rate on all
the mobs and items in your game to 0, which disables their internal rejuvenation.
CoffeeSUD: ONREENTRY=true resets on return after everyone has left; MINAWAY=[game hours]
sets the minimum absence. SKIPROOMS="[room mask]" leaves matching rooms unchanged; e.g.
SKIPROOMS="-LOCATION '+ROOMSTR(Sanctum)'". RESETMSG="[text]" aliases MSG. Last access and
absence survive saves. InstanceArea INPLACE=true reapplies its type adjustments after
resetting the real rooms, using the entering leader level.
```

<a id="behavior-resourceoverride"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_RESOURCEOVERRIDE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1847.

```text
Behavior   : ResourceOverride
Targets    : Rooms, Areas, Mobs
Parameters : (min=x) (max=[ticks]) (chance=[%]) ([RESOURCE]) ([ROOM TYPE])...
Parameters : .. ("item name([RESOURCE] [SUBTYPE])") ("[RESOURCE] [SUBTYPE]")
Example    : MIN=5 MAX=5 CHANCE=100 CORN WHEAT RICE
Example    : CORN WHEAT RICE ROCKY MOUNTAINS PLAINS
Example    : CORN "some weird corn(CORN WIERDCORN)" "CORN WIERDCORN"
Example    : SPRING=flowers,herbs SUMMER=blueberries AUTUMN=apples WINTER=none MSG="The
orchard turns with the season."
Example    : MUSHROOMS SEASON=autumn HOUR=20-23,0-4
Description:
This class allows one to override the normal resources generated by rooms for many common
skills, or by corpses during butchering.  This skill will randomly select from the list
enumerated in the parameters instead of the normal list. If this behavior is added to an
area, you can add to the parameters a list of room types to apply the new resources to.
Room types include: STONE, WOODEN, CAVE, MAGIC, UNDERWATER, AIR, WATERSURFACE,      METAL,
CITY, WOODS, ROCKY, PLAINS, UNDERWATER", AIR, WATERSURFACE, JUNGLE, SWAMP, DESERT, HILLS,
MOUNTAINS

Resource types can be listed by name or their code number.  You can also put a resource type
 in double-quotes followed by a space and sub-type. Lastly, a custom resource can be made by
 putting the name in quotation marks followed by the resource type and sub-type in
parenthesis.

When changing the parameters of an existing ResourceOverride on an area, be sure to use
RESET AREA to change back any rooms previously affected.

CoffeeSUD: by the calendar (of the room's area).  SPRING=, SUMMER=, AUTUMN= (or FALL=) and
WINTER= each give a season its own comma list of resources (none for nothing), which swap in
 as the season turns; a season with no list uses the plain list, if there is one, or else
the rooms' own.  SEASON=, MONTH= and HOUR= (comma lists, with ranges as 20-23) limit when it
 applies at all; outside them the rooms have their own resources back.  MSG="[TEXT]" is
shown in a room when the calendar changes its resource.
```

<a id="behavior-riddler"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_RIDDLER

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1924.

```text
Behavior   : Riddler
Targets    : MOBs, Items
Parameters : RIDDLE="[TEXT]" ANSWERS="[ANSWER]|[ANSWER]" (RIDDLE1..9= ANSWERS1..9=)
(RANDOM=true) (FUZZY=[N]) (ASK=GREET,LOOK,COMMAND) (TRIES=[N]) (ONRIGHT="[ACTIONS]")
(ONWRONG="[ACTIONS]") (ONOUT="[ACTIONS]") (RIGHTMSG="[TEXT]") (WRONGMSG="[TEXT]")
(ONCE=CHARACTER/SAVE/NONE)
Example    : RIDDLE="What has roots nobody sees, and is taller than trees?"
ANSWERS="mountain|mountains" FUZZY=1 TRIES=3 ONRIGHT="door open here north; exp $n 100"
ONOUT="force $i kill $n"
Description:
CoffeeSUD: a mob or a thing that asks riddles.  RIDDLE and ANSWERS (more with RIDDLE1 to 9
and ANSWERS1 to 9; RANDOM picks one, else the first); case, a, an, the and punctuation do
not count, and FUZZY=1 forgives one wrong letter (or two swapped).  ASK (all three by
default): GREET asks one of the player's side who comes in, LOOK one who looks at it,
COMMAND one who types RIDDLE.  They answer by saying it (SAY) or with ANSWER [TEXT].  After
TRIES wrong answers (3) ONOUT runs; ONRIGHT and ONWRONG run on each answer (script commands,
 MP left off if you like, $n who answered; as Prop_Switch's).  ONCE=CHARACTER (the default)
asks each character until they solve it, SAVE until anyone does (kept with it), NONE always.
```

<a id="behavior-roomstates"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_ROOMSTATES

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1882.

```text
Behavior   : RoomStates
Targets    : Rooms, Areas
Parameters : STATE=[NAME] (TITLE=) (DESC=) (ATMOSPHERE=) (CLIMATE=)
(ADD="[ID]([PARMS]);...") (BLOCK=[DIRS]) (OPEN=[DIRS]) (ENTERMSG=); TO=[NAME] (FROM=[NAMES])
 (WHEN="[MASK]") (AFTER=[TICKS]) (TICKS=[N]) (ONVAR="[HOST] [VAR]==[VALUE]"); START=[NAME];
(ROOMS=[ROOM IDS])
Example    : STATE=dry TITLE="A dusty shaft"; STATE=collapsed TITLE="A collapsed shaft"
ADD="Prop_RoomDark()" BLOCK=down; TO=collapsed ONVAR="mine collapse==1"; START=dry
Description:
CoffeeSUD: named versions of a room, declared in one place; clauses go with a semicolon
between. A STATE sets the room's title, description, atmosphere (WATER, AIR...) and climate
(WET, COLD...), gives it effects and behaviours (ADD, with their parameters in brackets;
taken away when the state ends), refuses ways out (BLOCK), opens doors (OPEN) and says
ENTERMSG to those coming in; what it leaves unset is the room's own.  A transition (TO) goes
 from the states named (FROM, or any) when WHEN holds (a mask on someone standing there, as
-WEATHER +RAIN) AFTER ticks in a row, after TICKS in the state, or when a script variable
holds (ONVAR, the host * when not given). On an area, all its rooms (or ROOMS=) change
together.  MPROOMSTATE and ROOMSTATE() set and read it; a save keeps it.
```

<a id="behavior-scene"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_SCENE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 2002.

```text
Behavior   : Scene
Targets    : Rooms, MOBs
Parameters : statements, ; between them or one to a line in FILE=[PATH]: (NAME=[NAME]) ACTOR
 [NAME]=[MASK OR NAME] ... [NAME]: [COMMAND] ... (PAUSE [N]) (ECHO [TEXT]) (DO [MOBPROG])
(IF=[CONDITION]) (ONCE/REPEAT=[DAYS]) (DELAY=[N]) (INTERRUPTIBLE)
Example    : NAME=bribes;ACTOR guard1=tall guard;ACTOR guard2=-NAMES +"short guard";guard1:
say Heard the bandits hit the mill again.;guard2: emote spits.;PAUSE 1;guard1: say The
[[captain]] takes their coin, they say.;DO mpsetvar $n HEARD_BRIBES yes;TOD=NIGHT
Description:
CoffeeSUD: NPCs play out a scene for a player character to overhear.  ACTOR names each part
and how to find the NPC in the room: a zapper mask (starting + or -), or words of its name;
on an NPC, SELF is the NPC itself.  Then the lines, one a tick (a turn in turn-based time),
DELAY=[N] ticks apart: [NAME]: say ..., [NAME]: emote ..., or any command the NPC can do;
ECHO [TEXT] for the room; PAUSE [N] for N ticks of silence; DO [MOBPROG] runs a script line
with $n the character it plays for (MPSETVAR, MPQJOURNAL, MPCALLFUNC...).  $n in a line is
that character's name, and [[topic]] in a line said teaches the topic (AHELP NPCTOPICS).  It
 begins when a player character is in the room it has not played to, all its actors are
there, awake and not fighting, and IF=[CONDITION] holds (a script condition, $n the
character, $i the first actor); WHEN=, TOD= and HOURS= hold it back too (AHELP
BEHAVIOR_WHEN).  Played to its end, each player character there has heard it: the variable
SCENE_[NAME] on them is the game day, and it is not played to them again (ONCE, the
default), or not for REPEAT=[DAYS] game days.  It stops, not heard, when the character or an
 actor goes, or an actor fights.  INTERRUPTIBLE: a character who speaks to an actor stops it
 and the actors turn to them; it plays to them again when they have left and come back.
Where it is in a scene is kept in a saved game; STAT BEHAVIORS shows it and any statement it
 did not understand.
```

<a id="behavior-schedule"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_SCHEDULE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 1960.

```text
Behavior   : Schedule
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : [WHEN]: [PLACE] ([ACTIVITY]...) (SAY [TEXT]/EMOTE [TEXT]); ...;
(SHOPMSG="[TEXT]")
Example    : DAWN: Mill#2 WORK "pours grain into the hopper|wipes flour from his hands";
DAY: Market#5 SHOP; DUSK: Inn#1 SIT "stool" SAY Long day.; NIGHT: Mill#9 SLEEP "straw bed"
LOCK
Description:
CoffeeSUD: a daily routine over several places.  Entries are separated by ';'; the first
whose WHEN holds is the one in force.  WHEN is DAWN, DAY, DUSK or NIGHT, or hours (2-5, or
7, on the area's clock), with any of DAYS=[FROM]-[TO] (days of the month), SEASON=, WEATHER=
 (CLEAR, RAIN, SNOW...) and MASK="[ZAPPER MASK]" (on the mob) after it.  PLACE is a room ID
(it runs to the first activity word, so an ID with spaces is fine), HOME or START (where the
 mob starts), or ANY:"[ROOM MASK]" (a room of its area that fits).  The activities: SLEEP or
 SIT, each with an optional item to do it on; WANDER [N]; SHOP (it trades only while here:
elsewhere, or on the way, it says SHOPMSG); WORK "[EMOTE]|[EMOTE]" (now and then); LOCK
(closes and locks the place's doors while there, and unlocks them when the entry ends);
HIDE.  SAY or EMOTE, last, is said on arriving.  It walks there, holding Mobile off on the
way, and goes back to it after a fight; woken, it goes back to sleep after a while.  When no
 player is in the area of either room it is put there at once, so a restored game, a time
jump or an area nobody is in finds it where its routine says.  With no entry in force it
stays where it is.  STAT($i SCHEDULE) is the entry in force, and STAT BEHAVIORS shows it.
```

<a id="behavior-scriptable"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_SCRIPTABLE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 2060.

```text
Behavior   : Scriptable
Targets    : MOBs, Items, Rooms
Parameters : (see below)
Example    : LOAD=progs/mrinfo.script~
Description:
This behavior allows the reactions and behaviors of the mob to be scripted. The parameter
may be complete scripts, and/or LOAD commands as specified below. If you choose to use a
file for your script, then each script command line must be terminated by a linefeed or a
semicolon.  If you choose to put your entire script into the parameters, you must terminate
EVERY line with a semicolon (;).
Multiple scripts with multiple triggers may be included.  Each script and trigger must be
separated by the ~ character.  See examples in the resources/progs directory!
Now to the script itself:
The first line must be a trigger word followed by any parameters.  Valid triggers and
parameters are as follows:
LOAD=[SCRIPT PATH] - insert a new script from another file.  Ex: LOAD=progs/my.script~
GREET_PROG [PCT CHANCE] - When players enter the room, given the chance.
ARRIVE_PROG [PCT CHANCE] - When the mob enters a new room, or enters the game.
ALL_GREET_PROG [PCT CHANCE] - Same as GREET_PROG, but works with sneakers too.
LOGIN_PROG [PCT CHANCE] - When players logs into the game, given the chance.
LOGOFF_PROG [PCT CHANCE] - When players log out of the game, given the chance.
LEVEL_PROG (GAIN/LOSS/ANY) [PCT CHANCE/MASK] - When a player anywhere gains a level (or
loses one), given the chance. $g is the new level.
SPEECH_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When someone says the words.
BRIBE_PROG [AMOUNT OF GOLD] - When the amount or better is given to the monster.
GIVE_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When something is given to the monster.
RAND_PROG [PCT CHANCE] - Triggers at random, given the chance.
ONCE_PROG - Triggers on the first occurrence, but never again (until reset).
FIGHT_PROG [PCT CHANCE] - Triggers during combat, given the chance.
ENTRY_PROG [PCT CHANCE] - Triggers whenever the monster enters a new room.
EXIT_PROG [PCT CHANCE] - Triggers whenever anyone exits the room of the monster.
DEATH_PROG (@GLOBAL (MASK)) - When the monster dies; with @GLOBAL, any death anywhere, of
one who fits the mask.
KILL_PROG (@GLOBAL (MASK)) - When the monster kills; with @GLOBAL, any kill anywhere, by one
 who fits the mask.
HITPRCNT_PROG [HP PCT] - When the monster reaches the hit points % remaining.
MASK_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When a mob performs an action with these
words.
IMASK_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When this mob performs an action with these
words.
REGMASK_PROG (P) [EXACT PHRASE]/[REGULAR EXPRESSION] - When a mob performs an action
matching.
ACT_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When a mob performs an action with these
words.
SOCIAL_PROG (EXACT) (ME) [SOCIAL NAME] - When a mob performs the given social: a name that
starts it, the whole name with EXACT, aimed at this mob with ME. $g is the social's full
name.
CHANNEL_PROG [CHNAME] (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When channels a message with
these words.
QUEST_TIME_PROG [QUEST NAME] [TIME LEFT] - When the running quest reaches the number of
minutes left. A time left of -1 fires at each step of the quest, and -2 when it ends, for
the objects the quest gave the script to.
QUEST_PROG [START/ACCEPT/STEP/WIN/FAIL/END/ANY] [QUEST NAME/*] (DETAIL) - When a quest
starts, is accepted, steps, is won, ends without a winner (FAIL), or ends; heard by every
object with the trigger, wherever it is. The detail is a step number for STEP, and for FAIL
and END the outcome: WON, EXPIRED, STOPPED or DROPPED. $n is the player (the accepter, the
winner, the one who dropped it) or 'the quest', $g the quest's name, $0 the detail.
QUESTFAIL_PROG [QUEST NAME/*] - CoffeeSUD: when a quest fails for a character (MPQUESTFAIL,
or a KEYPLAYER FAIL death); heard by every object with the trigger, the character's own
quest scripts too. $n is the character, $g the quest's name, $0 why.
TALK_PROG ([WORDS]/P [PHRASE]/ALL) - CoffeeSUD: when a character begins a conversation with
the mob by TALK (and TALK ABOUT a topic): ALL, or no words, for any; else when the topic has
 one of the words, or the phrase. Runs at once. $n is the character, $g and $0 the topic
(empty for none). With no TALK_PROG that fits, the character says the topic (or Hello) to
the mob instead, for its MudChat and SPEECH_PROGs, and with no topic is shown its services.
MEMORY(npc who LASTTOPIC) is the topic.
SET_PROG ([SET]/ALL) - CoffeeSUD: on a piece of an item set (Prop_ItemSet) or its wearer: a
tier came on or went off; $0 the tier, $1 ON or OFF, $n the wearer.
USE_PROG ([KEYWORDS]/ALL) - CoffeeSUD: on either thing of USE X (ON Y): it was used; the
keywords are looked for in the other thing's name (none, or ALL, for any); $n who, $o the
first, $t the second (or the first, alone).  Without one, world/combinations.txt is looked
at.
COMBINE_PROG ([KEYWORDS]/ALL) - CoffeeSUD: on either thing of COMBINE X WITH Y, as USE_PROG.
SWITCH_PROG ([STATE]/ALL) - CoffeeSUD: on a thing with Prop_Switch, or its room: it moved to
 that state; $0 the state, $n who moved it.
PARTYDEFEAT_PROG - CoffeeSUD: on a room or an area: every one of the party there is down
(PLAYERDEATH's DOWNED) or dead; $n the last to fall.  The script decides what happens;
without one, coffeemud.ini's PARTYDEFEAT does.
AMBUSH_PROG ([SURPRISED/SPOTTED/AVOIDED]/ALL) - CoffeeSUD: on a room with Prop_Ambush, or an
 NPC there: when it springs and how it went; $0 the outcome, $n the one who came in.
WAVE_PROG ([N]/ALL) - CoffeeSUD: on a room with WaveSpawner, or an NPC there: when wave N
(or any) comes; $0 is the wave, $n one of the party.
ARENAWIN_PROG - CoffeeSUD: when a WaveSpawner's last wave is beaten; $n the winner.
ARENALOSE_PROG - CoffeeSUD: when the party leaves or falls in a WaveSpawner's arena; $n who
started it.
PHASE_PROG ([N]/ALL) - CoffeeSUD: when the mob's BossPhases enters phase N (or any): $g and
$0 are the phase, $n its foe.
YIELD_PROG - CoffeeSUD: when the mob yields (Prop_Essential MODE=YIELD): $n is who beat it.
DEFEAT_PROG - CoffeeSUD: when a killing blow knocks the mob out instead (Prop_Essential
MODE=KNOCKOUT): $n is who beat it.
SURRENDER_PROG - CoffeeSUD: when the mob surrenders (Morale SURRENDERAT=): $n is one it
fought.
RESET_PROG - CoffeeSUD: when EncounterReset puts the mob back after its foes left: $n and $i
 are the mob.
QUESTTIMEOUT_PROG ([QUEST NAME/*]) - CoffeeSUD: when a character's own deadline for a quest
(MPQTIMER) comes; runs at once on the character's scripts, a bare QUESTTIMEOUT_PROG on those
 the quest gave them, busy or not. With no such trigger there, the quest fails for them,
EXPIRED. $n is the character, $g and $0 the quest's name.
TIME_PROG [LIST OF HOURS] - Mob runs program at listed hours of the day: numbers, DAWN, DAY,
 DUSK or NIGHT (the hour the area's clock begins it), or ranges, 6-18 or 6-18/3 for every
third hour.
DAY_PROG [LIST OF DAYS] - Mob runs program at listed days of the month, or ranges of them
(1-7).
DELAY_PROG [LOW TICKS] [HIGH TICKS] - Mob runs program at the given interval range.
LOOK_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When matching something is looked at.
LLOOK_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When matching something is llooked at.
GET_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When matching something is gotten.
OPEN_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When matching something is opened.
CLOSE_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When matching something is closed.
LOCK_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When matching something is locked.
UNLOCK_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When matching something is unlocked.
PUT_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When matching something is put in something.
DROP_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When matching something is dropped.
REMOVE_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When matching something is removed.
CONSUME_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When matching something is ate/drank.
WEAR_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When matching something is worn/wielded.
DAMAGE_PROG - When damage taken by mob or given by item. Item#2 is the weapon. $g will have
the amount.
BUY_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When matching something is bought (items
only).
SELL_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When matching something is sold.
EXECMSG_PROG (@GLOBAL) [MSG CODE] (P) [COMMAND WORDS] - When a msg of type msg code is
executed. HELP MSG TYPES, or LIST MSGTYPES. With @GLOBAL, the world-wide messages of that
type (DEATH, LEVEL, LOGIN, QUIT, LEGALWARRANT, LEGALSTATE, WINQUEST, ENDQUEST) wherever they
 happen, heard once. SKILL_PROG and FACTION_PROG take @GLOBAL first too.
CNCLMSG_PROG [MSG CODE] (P) [COMMAND WORDS] - Before a msg of type msg code is allowed. HELP
 MSG TYPES, or LIST MSGTYPES.
In either, =S, =T or =O [STAT]=[VALUE] in place of the words checks the source, target or
tool: the value may have * wildcards, and =S MASK=[ZAPPER MASK] checks a mask. MSG() reads
the message, MPMSG changes it.
FUNCTION_PROG [FUNCTION NAME] - declares a runnable function, with parms in $g, see
MPCALLFUNC.
SKILL_PROG [LEARN/IMPROVE/MASTER/FAIL/ANY] [SKILL ID/NAME/*] (MASK) - When a character near
the host learns a skill, gains proficiency in it, reaches its most, or fails its roll, and
fits the zapper mask. Heard by the room, its items and mobs, and its area. $t is the skill,
$g its proficiency.
DISCOVER_PROG [ROOM/AREA] (PARTY) (MASK) - When a character first visits the room, or the
area's first room they visit; with PARTY, only if no one else in their group has been there.
 $g is the room's ID.
WEATHER_PROG [WEATHER/ANY] (OLD WEATHER) - When the host's area's weather changes to the
weather (CLEAR, CLOUDY, WINDY, RAIN, THUNDERSTORM, SNOW, HAIL, HEAT, SLEET, BLIZZARD, DUST,
DROUGHT, COLD, FOG), from the old one if given. $g is the new weather, $0 the old, $1 the
forecast. EXECMSG_PROG WEATHERCHANGE, TODCHANGE and DATECHANGE hear a change of weather, of
the time of day, and a new day, in the area.
MOON_PROG [PHASE/ANY] - When the moon over the host's area becomes the phase (NEW,
WAXCRESCENT, WAXQUARTER, WAXGIBBOUS, FULL, WANEGIBBOUS, WANEQUARTER, WANECRESCENT). $g is
the phase, $0 the one before.
GAME_PROG [NEWGAME/RESTORE/SAVE/NEWCHAR/SWITCHTO/SWITCHFROM/PAUSE/RESUME/TIMEMODE/ANY]
(MASK) - When the game starts new or restored, is saved, a character is made, the player
switches characters, pauses, resumes or changes the time mode; heard by every object with
the trigger. $n is the character, $g the save's name for SAVE and RESTORE and otherwise the
event, $0 the event, $1 the detail (the other character, or TURNS or REALTIME). SAVE runs at
 once, before the save is made, so what it sets is saved; RETURN CANCEL refuses the save.
TURN_PROG (EVERY N) (MASK) - At the end of each turn: a party's turn in turn-based time, a
player's command that takes time in real time; every N turns if given. Heard by objects with
 the trigger in the leader's area, the area, and the world's scripts. $n is the leader, $g
the turns since the game began.
The files in world/scripts/ are scripts on one hidden object, WORLD (its variables are
WORLD's), that goes where the player goes and ticks every tick: GAME_PROG, QUEST_PROG and
TURN_PROG there hear the whole game.
VERB_PROG [VERB(,ALIAS...)] (P [PHRASE] / [KEYWORDS]) - When a player types the verb (whole,
 not a prefix) and the rest of the line names the object the script is on (or has the phrase
 or a keyword; a room or area needs no naming), before any command, skill or social of that
word; on items carried or here, mobs, exits, the room and the area. $t is the object, $g the
 rest of the line. RETURN CONTINUE hands the line back to the usual commands. Prop_Verbs
(VERBS=\"pull,yank\" MSG=\"...\" OTHERS=\"...\") does it without a script; LIST VERBS lists
a room's.
PARTY_PROG [JOIN/LEAVE/REST/LEAD/SWITCH/ANY] (MASK) - When a character joins the party,
leaves it, rests, takes the lead, or the player switches to a member; heard by every object
with the trigger. $n is the member, $t the leader, $g the event.
SEASON_PROG [SPRING/SUMMER/FALL/WINTER/ANY], MONTH_PROG [NUMBERS OR NAMES/ANY], YEAR_PROG
[YEAR/ANY], WEEKDAY_PROG [DAY NAMES/ANY] - When the area's clock comes to a new season,
month or year, or each new day of the week. $g is the new one, $0 the one before.
CLAN_PROG [JOIN/LEAVE/PROMOTE/DEMOTE/EXILE/RELATION/CONQUER/LOSEAREA/LEVEL/ALL] (CLAN/ALL) -
 When a member joins or leaves a clan (however it comes about), is promoted, demoted or
exiled, the clan's relation to another changes, it wins or loses an area, or changes level;
heard in the member's room, the clan's recall room and the area. $n is the member, $t the
area, $g the new rank, relation or level, $0 the event, $1 the clan, $2 the detail, $3 the
other clan or the area.
CRAFT_PROG [SKILL ID/*] [ITEM WORDS/ALL] (RUINED/SUCCESS) - When a crafter here makes
something with the skill (heard by the room, its area, and things and mobs around). $n is
the crafter, $o and $t the thing made, $g the skill.
RECIPE_PROG [SKILL ID/*] [RECIPE WORDS/ALL] - When a crafter here learns a recipe. $o is the
 thing it makes, $g the skill.
FACTION_PROG (@GLOBAL) [FACTION] [RANGE NAME/ANY/UP/DOWN] (MASK) - When a character's
standing changes (any, up, down), or comes into the named range; heard by the room and area,
 or anywhere with @GLOBAL. $g is the new range, $0 the change, $1 the range before, $2 the
faction.
COMBAT_PROG [START/END/FLEE/ANY] (MASK) - When the monster's fight (an item's owner's, or
any fight in a room) starts, ends with both sides alive, or an opponent flees. $n is the
opponent (the one fleeing), $g the event.
AREA_ENTER_PROG and AREA_LEAVE_PROG (ALL) (PCT/MASK) - When someone comes into the host's
area from another area (or into the world), or leaves it; with ALL, a move between it and an
 area inside it counts too. $n is the mover, $g the other area's name, $0 the other room's
ID. Prop_AreaEntry (ENTER, FIRST, LEAVE, TITLE or SHOWNAME, TEXT, DESC, ONCE, MASK, COLOR)
and Prop_AreaBanner show text on an area's border.
BOARD_PROG (MASK) and DISEMBARK_PROG (MASK) - When someone boards a vessel or leaves it;
heard by the vessel, its rooms and crew, and the room outside. $n is the one, $t the vessel,
 $g its name.
SAIL_PROG [COURSE/ANCHOR/STEER/ALL] - When one allowed to gives the vessel an order. $n is
the helmsman, $g the order, $0 its kind.
VESSEL_ARRIVE_PROG [ROOM ID/AREA/ALL] - On the vessel and its crew, when it comes into a
room. $g is the room's ID, $0 its area. VESSEL_GREET_PROG [VESSEL WORDS/ALL] - On a room a
vessel comes into, and what is there. DOCK_PROG - When the vessel's anchor drops; heard
aboard and in the room. $g is the room's ID.
READ_PROG [ITEM WORDS/P PHRASE/ALL] - When someone reads the thing (on a thing, only its own
 reading; on its holder, room or area, any that fits). $n is the reader, $o the thing. It
runs before the reading: RETURN CANCEL keeps the thing's own text back. CoffeeSUD: READ_PROG
 PAGE [N]/[TITLE] for a page of a GenTome (AHELP GENTOME).
GENERATED_PROG (PCT) - When a generator has made the area or room the host is in (the area,
its rooms, mobs and items hear it; EXECMSG_PROG GENERATED too). $g is the generator's ID. An
 AREA tag's onGenerate=\"...\" runs once.
FIRSTGREET_PROG (PCT) - When the mob first meets a character ever (sees them arrive).
REGREET_PROG [GAME DAYS] (PCT) - When a character it has met comes back after at least that
many game days. The meetings are kept in the save.
EVERY_PROG [N] (HOURS/DAYS/WEEKS/MONTHS) (CATCHUP) - Every N hours, days, weeks or months of
 the area's clock, its next time kept in the save; with CATCHUP, $g is how many times it was
 due while the host did not tick.
VAR_PROG [HOST/*/QUEST] [VAR] [==/!=/>/</>=/<=] [VALUE] - When a script variable's change
makes the condition come true; heard by every object with the trigger. $g is the new value,
$0 the old.
AFFECT_PROG [ADD/REMOVE/ANY] [ABILITY ID/NAME WORDS/*] - When an effect is put on something
or comes off it; heard by the thing, its room, and an item's owner. $t is the thing, $g the
effect's ID, $n its invoker.
DESTROY_PROG [REASON/WORDS/ALL] - When an item is destroyed, at once, on the item, its room
and its owner; $g is DECAY, JUNKED or empty. DECAY_PROG - When an item rots or runs out (its
 expiry).
ACHIEVE_PROG [ACHIEVEMENT ID/*] (MASK) - When an achievement is earned; heard by every
object with the trigger. $n is the earner, $g the achievement's ID.
SIGNAL_PROG [NAME/ALL] - When a script sends the signal to this thing, with MPSIGNAL. $g is
its arguments, $n who caused it, $t the thing that sent it.
PUTTING_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When matching something is put in
something, the words naming the thing put (PUT_PROG's name the container). On a mob, only
its own putting; on an item, when it is the thing put; on a room or area, anyone's. $n is
the one putting, $t and $o the container, $p the thing put.
SPEAK_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When the monster itself says the words
(SPEECH_PROG hears others); on an item, room or area, when anyone says them. $n is the
speaker, $t the one spoken to, $g what was said.
GIVING_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When the monster gives away a matching
thing (GIVE_PROG is when it is given one); on an item, when it is the thing given; on a room
 or area, any giving. $n is the giver, $t the one given it, $o the thing.
CAST_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When someone else uses a skill, spell or
other ability of that name (or ID) on the monster; on a room or area, anyone's. Speech in a
language other than Common counts too, as that language. $n is the user, $t the monster, $g
the trigger word that matched. Not on items.
CASTING_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When the monster itself uses a skill,
spell or other ability of that name (or ID), a language it speaks in too; on a room or area,
 anyone's. $n is the user, $t its target, $g the trigger word that matched. Not on items.
CMDFAIL_PROG [COMMAND] (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS]/ALL - When a command fails, or is
not known (Huh?), and the word typed starts the command given (OP for OPEN). ALL or nothing
for any words after it, P for exactly these. It runs before the failure is shown: RETURN
CANCEL keeps it back. $n is the one who typed it, $t the command's target, $g the rest of
the line.
GROUP_GREET_PROG [PCT CHANCE] - Same as ALL_GREET_PROG, but at most once a tick, so a group
coming in together sets it off once, for the first of them. In the host's room only, not on
areas.
DROPPING_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When the monster itself drops a matching
thing (DROP_PROG hears others). $t and $o are the thing. MPNOTRIGGER DROP_PROG stops it too.
GETTING_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When the monster itself gets a matching
thing (GET_PROG hears others). $t and $o are the thing. MPNOTRIGGER GET_PROG stops it too.
RIDE_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When someone else mounts a matching rideable:
 the host itself, or, on a room, area or mob, any rideable there. $n is the rider, $t the
rideable.
RIDING_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When the monster itself mounts a matching
rideable (RIDE_PROG hears others). $t is the rideable.
WEARING_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When the monster itself wears, holds or
wields a matching thing (WEAR_PROG hears others). $t and $o are the thing. MPNOTRIGGER
WEAR_PROG stops it too.
DISMOUNT_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - As RIDE_PROG, when someone else gets off
a matching rideable.
REMOVING_PROG (P) [A PHRASE]/[ONE OR MORE WORDS] - When the monster itself removes a
matching thing it wears (REMOVE_PROG hears others). $t and $o are the thing. MPNOTRIGGER
REMOVE_PROG stops it too.
Of these, SPEAK_PROG and the -ING triggers (PUTTING, GIVING, CASTING, DROPPING, GETTING,
RIDING, WEARING, REMOVING) are, on a mob, for its own doing; DROPPING, GETTING, RIDING,
WEARING and REMOVING work on mobs only. The words match a word of the thing's name, or its
ID; P a whole name. All but CMDFAIL_PROG run after the deed, on the host's next tick (at
once with MPSETINTERNAL NODELAY TRUE), so RETURN CANCEL cannot stop it.
*** NOTE Phrases for MASK_PROG, GIVE_PROG, GET_PROG, PUT_PROG, REMOVE_PROG, WEAR_PROG,
BUY_PROG, SELL_PROG, and SPEECH_PROG must group words and phrases together using the "'"
character, for instance 'a phrase' or 'multiple words'. The characteris unnecessary when put
 around single words 'word'.

*** NOTE If Scriptable is placed on an Item, triggers such as GET_PROG, DROP_PROG,
WEAR_PROG, and REMOVE_PROG will only trigger when the scripted item is involved.

*** NOTE MASK_PROG and ACT_PROG will check commands as they appear to the mob with this
behavior.  Consider perspective, vision, and word tense in light of this fact when wording
your masks.  For instance, the purchase of a sword in a dark shop may be seen as 'Someone
buys something from someone' instead of 'Bob buys a sword from Joe'.

Following this line is your script itself.  The commands are as follows:
IF/ENDIF/ELSE Conditional evaluations, separated by AND/OR.  The IF statement can group
conditions with () and use the following functions as part of its evaluation:
 - RAND([% CHANCE])    Random truth
 - HAS([CODE] [ITEM NAME])  if the given mob has the specified item.
 - HASNUM([CODE] [ITEM NAME] == [NUM])  the amount the given mob has of the item.
 - HASTITLE([CODE] [TITLE STR])  if the given mob has the give title.
 - WORN([CODE] [ITEM NAME])  if the given mob wears the specified item.
 - ISNPC([CODE])  if the given mob is a non-player.
 - ISPC([CODE])  if the given mob is a player.
 - ISPKILL([CODE])  if the given mob has playerkill flag on.
 - ISGOOD([CODE])  if the given mob is good.
 - ISNAME([CODE] [WORDS])  if the given item is named with given words.
 - CURRENCY([CODE] == [NAME])  if the native currency of the mob or coins is the name. Where
 == may be !=.
 - NUMMOBSINAREA([MOB NAME] == [NUM]) if comparison of number of mobs of that name in area.
Where == may be !=, >, <, <=, <=.
 - NUMMOBS([MOB NAME] == [NUM]) if comparison of number of mobs of that name in world. Where
 == may be !=, >, <, <=, <=.
 - NUMRACES([MOB NAME] == [NUM]) if comparison of number of mobs of that name in world.
Where == may be !=, >, <, <=, <=.
 - ISEVIL([CODE])  if the given mob is evil.
 - ISNEUTRAL([CODE])  if the given mob is neutral.
 - ISFIGHT([CODE])  if the given mob is fighting.
 - ISALIVE([CODE])  if the given mob is alive and available.
 - ISIMMORT([CODE])  if the given mob is an archon.
 - ISCHARMED([CODE])  if the given mob is charmed.
 - STRCONTAINS([STRING] [CODED WORDS])  is string contains coded words.  May use "" & | > <
().
 - STAT([CODE] [STAT] == [VALUE]) if the given mob/item has a stat of value, != is also
valid.
 - GSTAT([CODE] [STAT] == [VALUE]) like STAT, but player data accessible. See Generic.java.
 - DATETIME([TIME/DAY/ETC] == [VALUE]) like STAT, but player data accessible. Where == may
be >, <, !=, >=, or <=.
 - AFFECTED([CODE] [SPELL CLASS]) if the mob is affected by spell.
 - ISBEHAVE([CODE] [BEHAVIOR CLASS]) if the mob has a behavior.
 - ISFOLLOW([CODE])  if the given mob is following someone in the room.
 - ISSERVANT([CODE])  if the given mob is serving someone in the room.
 - HITPRCNT([CODE] == [% HITS])  if the given mob has the pct chance hit points.  Where ==
may be >, <, !=, >=, or <=.
 - HASTATTOO([CODE] [TATTOONAME]) whether the given mob has the given tattoo.
 - INLOCALE([ROOM CLASS]) if the mob is in the given room type.
 - ISBIRTHDAY([CODE]) if the mobs birthday is today.
 - INROOM([ROOM ID/MOB NAME] == [ROOM ID/MOB NAME]) if the mob is in the given room.
BEACON, MYPROPERTY, ANYPROPERTY and ANYSPECIAL may stand for the room; CoffeeSUD: with a mob
 on the left, BEACON and MYPROPERTY are that mob's (its start room, land it or its profile
owns), not the scripted mob's.
 - MOOD([MOB NAME] == [MOOD NAME]) if the mob has a mood, and it is the one specified.
 - ISRECALL([MOB NAME]== [ROOM ID/MOB NAME]) is the mob is from the given room.
 - ISHERE([CODE]) if the mob/item in the same room as the scripted one.
 - INAREA([NAME]) if the scripted mob/item in room named by the parameters.
 - ISLIKE([CODE] [MASK]) if the mob/item meets the given zapper mask.  See ZAPPERMASKS for
mask syntax
 - ISODD([AMT]) whether the given argument is an odd whole number
 - VAR([CODE] [VAR NAME] == [VALUE]) if the var for the given mob has value.  Where == may
be !=, >, <, >=, <=.
 - FACTION([CODE] [FACT] == [VALUE]) if the faction for the given mob has value.  Where ==
may be !=, >, <, >=, <=.
 - SEX([CODE] == [M/F/N]) evaluates sex.  Where == may also be !=.
 - POSITION([CODE] == [SLEEPING/STANDING/SITTING] Evaluates position.
 - LEVEL([CODE] == [LVL]) evaluates level.  Where == may be !=, <, >, >=, <=.
 - MATH([EXPR] == [EXPR]) evaluates expression.  Where == may be !=, <, >, >=, <=.
 - QUESTPOINTS([CODE] == [VAL]) evaluates questpoints.  Where == may be !=, <, >, >=, <=.
 - QVAR([QUEST] [CODE] == [VAL]) evaluates temp quest vars.  Where == may be !=, <, >, >=,
<=.
 - VARNAMES([HOST] [PREFIX] == [NAMES]) compares the names of the host's variables (* for
any host) starting with the prefix, sorted and separated by spaces.
 - ISDEV()  if this is a developer's game (started with DEV=1).
 - ISBUILDER()  if this is builder mode (started with BUILDER=1).
 - ISTURNBASED()  if time is turn-based (TIMEMODE TURNS).
 - ISPAUSED()  if the game is paused.
 - SAVESLOT(== [NAME]) compares the name of the save the game was last saved to or restored
from.
 - GAMETIME(> [MS]) compares the game's time, in game milliseconds since it began.
 - TURNS(> [N]) compares the turns since the game began (see TURN_PROG).

party and followers.

 NPC remembers of the character.

may be compared the same way, as LISTCOUNT($<WORLD SUSPECTS>) > 2.

 INPARTY([CODE]) if it is in the party of the character at the terminal ($u).
```
