```text
*** NOTES! The parenthesis are REQUIRED for the above!  The brackets should NOT be included,
 they are there to designate a parameter.  Where CODE above is one of the following:
$n=source of the action, $i=scripted mob, $t=target, $o=item1, $p=item2, $w=owner of item1,
$W=owner of item2.

Now we get to the executed commands.  They are as follows:
FOR $X = [START] to [FINISH] - loops. X must be 0-9.  End with NEXT by itself.
SWITCH/CASE/ENDSWITCH - act as a multiple if/elseif/elseif....
MPASOUND [TEXT] - a noisy emote that goes to all adjacent rooms.
MPECHO [TEXT] - an emote
MPSLAY [MOB NAME] - utterly kill the target.
MPJUNK [ITEM] - destroy the given item from the monsters inventory.
MPMLOAD [MOB NAME] - create an instance of the given mob name.
MPOLOAD [ITEM NAME] - create an instanceof the given item, give it to the mob.
MPOLOADROOM [ITEM NAME] - create an instanceof the given item, drop it in the room.
MPMLOAD FROMFILE [CMARE FILE] [MOB NAME] - create a given mob name from a file.
MPOLOAD FROMFILE [CMARE FILE] [ITEM NAME] - create an item from a file, give it to the mob.
MPOLOADROOM FROMFILE [CMARE FILE]  [ITEM NAME] - create an item from a file, drop it in the
room.
MPMLOAD CATALOG (FORCE) [NAME] (COUNT), MPOLOAD CATALOG (FORCE) [NAME] (INTO [CONTAINER]),
MPOLOADROOM, MPOLOADSHOP and MPMLOADSHOP CATALOG [NAME] - copies of the catalog's mob or
item, counted by the catalog; none is made past its cap unless FORCE. $b is the last copy.
With FROMFILE [FILE] ALL, all of the file's.  CATALOG:[NAME] is the same.
MPMLOAD ENCOUNTER [TABLE] - CoffeeSUD: rolls an encounter table (AHELP ENCOUNTER) here, for
$n if they are on the player's side (its masks and levels); $b is the leader of what came.
MPECHOAT [MOB/ROOM/AREA/WORLD] [TEXT] - emote to the given target.
MPECHOAROUND [MOB NAME] [TEXT] - emotes to everyone in the mob's room but the mob.
MPCAST [SPELL] [MOB NAME] - casts the given spell at the given target.
MPKILL [MOB NAME] - attack the given target.
MPEXP [MOB NAME] [EXP or TNL%] - grants amount of exp to mob.
MPQUESTPOINTS [MOB NAME] [QPS] - sets mobs amount of questpoints. Prefix QPS with ++ or --
to adjust only.
MPTRAINS [MOB NAME] [TRAINS] - sets mobs amount of trains. Prefix TRAINS with ++ or -- to
adjust only.
MPPRACS [MOB NAME] [PRACS] - sets mobs amount of pracs. Prefix PRACS with ++ or -- to adjust
 only.
MPPURGE [ITEM/MOB NAME] - destroy the given target item or mob.
MPUNAFFECT [MOB NAME] [ALL/SKILL NAME]- removes given affects from the mob.
MPGOTO [ROOM ID/NAME/DESC] - take the monster to the given room.
MPAT [ROOM ID/NAME/DESC] [COMMAND] - do a command at the given room.
MPSET [MOB/ITEM] [VAR NAME] [VALUE] - use with care! sets a stat for a mob or item.
MPGSET [MOB/ITEM] [VAR NAME] [VALUE] - like MPSET but player data accessible. See GSTAT.
MPTRANSFER [ALL/MOB NAME] [ROOM ID/NAME/DESC] - transfer mobs to the given room.
MPBEACON [ROOM ID/NAME/DESC] [ALL/MOB NAME] - Makes given room start room for players.
MPFORCE [MOB NAME] [COMMAND] - force the given mob to do the given command.
MPPROMPT [PC NAME] [VARIABLE NAME] [PROMPT].  Store user entered value in variable.  See
Guide.
MPCONFIRM [PC NAME] [VARIABLE NAME] [DEFAULT VALUE] [PROMPT].  Y or N.  See Guide.
MPCHOOSE [PC NAME] [VARIABLE NAME] [CHOICES] [DEFAULT VALUE] [PROMPT].  Hotkey choices.  See
 Guide.
MPMENU [PC NAME] [FUNCTION] "[PROMPT]" [KEY]:"[LABEL]"([IF CONDITION]) ... ([DEFAULT KEY]) -
 CoffeeSUD: a numbered menu that does not wait: the script goes on at once, and the
character's next line answers it, by number or key (Enter, or an answer that is none of
them, takes the default; with no default it asks again). Then FUNCTION_PROG [FUNCTION] of
the same script runs with the key as $0, the character as $n. A choice whose [IF ...]
condition fails is not shown. The answer is not a command, so it takes no time in turn-based
 play.
MPSCRIPT [MOB/ITEM] ([FLAGS]) [SCRIPT] - adds a quest Scriptable to the target, flags GLOBAL
 INDIVIDUAL SAVABLE EXECUTE.
MPSETVAR [MOB NAME] [VAR NAME] [VALUE] - set a variable for the given mob.  Value may be ++,
 --, or preceded by +,-,*,or /.
MPSETVAR [HOST] [VAR NAME] NOW - set the area clock's stamp, for ELAPSED().
MPSETVAR @[CODE] [VAR NAME] [VALUE] - a variable kept on that one thing, not on its name:
two guards of one name have their own, and a save keeps them with the thing; $<@[CODE] VAR>
and VAR(@[CODE] VAR == X) read them. MPSETINTERNAL VARHOST INSTANCE makes a bare [CODE] mean
 @[CODE]. A mob loses its own when it comes back to life, unless its variable PERSIST is
set.
MPSETVAR [HOST] [VAR NAME] %N or  - the remainder, or the power, of the number held; =VALUE
sets the value as it is, so =-5 is minus five.
MPENDQUEST [QUEST NAME/MOB NAME] - this command will shutdown the given quest, or remove
quest scripts from given mob.
MPSTARTQUEST [QUEST NAME] - this command will start the quest of the given name.
MPQUESTWIN [MOB NAME] [QUEST NAME] (OUTCOME [WORD]) (REWARD) - declares the mob a winner of
the given quest; CoffeeSUD: OUTCOME keeps a word of how it ended for that character, for
QUESTOUTCOME() and QUESTS WON; REWARD gives them the quest's SET REWARDS.
MPREWARD [MOB NAME] "[AWARDS]" - CoffeeSUD: gives a character a reward, in SET REWARDS'
words, with one message.
MPQUESTFAIL [MOB NAME] [QUEST NAME] ([REASON]) - CoffeeSUD: the quest fails for that
character: it is recorded (QUESTSTATUS, QUESTS FAILED), QUESTFAIL_PROG and QUEST_PROG FAIL
fire, and their quest scripts end and go, as MPENDQUEST [MOB NAME] does.
MPAFFINITY [NPC] [PC NAME] +[N]/-[N]/=[N] - CoffeeSUD: raises, lowers or sets the NPC's
opinion of the character (Prop_Affinity), kept in the game's variables.
MPTHREAT [NPC] [PC NAME] +[N]/-[N]/=[N]/*[X] - CoffeeSUD: raises, lowers, sets or multiplies
 a character's threat to an NPC (a taunt: MPTHREAT $t $n *3).  An NPC with CombatAbilities
turns on one who gets a clear lead.
MPQTIMER [MOB NAME] [QUEST NAME] [GAME TIME]/OFF - CoffeeSUD: the character's own deadline
for the quest, from now, as 6 MUDHOURS or 2 MUDDAYS or a number of ticks; OFF takes it away,
 and so does the quest's end for them. It is kept with the character (in saves too) and
counted on the game clock, so a pause or turn-based time holds it. QUESTS shows the time
left. When it comes: QUESTTIMEOUT_PROG, or, with none, the quest fails for them, EXPIRED.
MPSTOP [MOB NAME] - forces mob to stop fighting, or performing common skills.
MPCALLFUNC [FUNC NAME] [PARMS...] - executes a FUNCTON_PROG already declared.
With party windows off, MPECHOAT, MPPROMPT, MPCONFIRM and MPCHOOSE aimed at a party member
in the background go to the terminal, with the member's name before them.
MPCALLFUNC [TARGET] [FUNC NAME] [PARMS...] - executes a FUNCTION_PROG of another thing's
scripts.
LOAD=[FILE] [NAME]=[VALUE]... - in a script, reads the file in as part of it, with arguments
 the file reads as ARG([NAME]); ARGDEFAULT [NAME]=[VALUE] lines in the file give the
defaults.
MPALARM (NAME=[NAME]) [TICKTIME] [COMMAND] - executes COMMAND after time has elapsed.
CoffeeSUD: a named alarm replaces one of its name, is kept in a saved game, can be
cancelled, and goes when the mob it belongs to dies, sleeps, or is held or bound (stunned,
knocked out).
MPALARMCANCEL [NAME] - CoffeeSUD: cancels a named alarm (MPALARM NAME=) on all the thing's
scripts, and a telegraph of that name.
MPTELEGRAPH (NAME=[NAME]) [TICKS] "[WARNING]" [COMMAND] (INTERRUPT=STUN,DAMAGE>[N]%,MOVE)
(AVOID=LEAVE,HIDE,COMMAND:[WORD]) (INTERRUPTMSG="[TEXT]") - CoffeeSUD: the mob winds up an
attack: the warning shows now and each tick, LOOK at the mob shows that it is gathering
power, and after TICKS the command runs once for each foe in the room ($n each one) who did
not avoid it: those who left, hid (HIDE) or typed the word (COMMAND:brace).  It is a named
alarm (TELEGRAPH unless NAME=), so ALARM($i TELEGRAPH) and MPALARMCANCEL work on it; a stun,
 a sleep or a hold always stops it, DAMAGE>[N]% when it takes that share of its hit points
meanwhile, MOVE when it leaves the room.  Example: MPTELEGRAPH 2 "<S-NAME> rears back,
flames gathering in <S-HIS-HER> throat!" MPDAMAGE $n 30 60 INTERRUPT=STUN,DAMAGE>20%
AVOID=COMMAND:brace
MPWAVE START/NEXT/STOP/RESET - CoffeeSUD: starts the WaveSpawner of the room (START=CALL),
brings its next wave, ends it as a loss, or clears it to start again.
MPSETRESPAWN [CODE] [ROOM ID]/HERE/CLEAR - CoffeeSUD: sets or clears a character's respawn
point (Prop_Checkpoint; DEATH=CHECKPOINT wakes them there).
MPDOOR OPEN/CLOSE/LOCK/UNLOCK/TOGGLE [ROOM ID/HERE] [DIRECTION/CONTAINER]
(QUIET/"[MESSAGE]") - CoffeeSUD: changes a door on both sides from anywhere, as a character
would: the message (<T-NAME> the door; the default uses the door's own words) shows in both
rooms, and the door's relock timer starts.  A container in the room by its name works too.
MPTRANSFORM [ITEM] [CATALOG ITEM/ITEM CLASS/ITEM NAME]
(KEEP=STATE,TAGS,USES,CONTAINER,WORN/ALL/NONE) - CoffeeSUD: turns an item into another in
the same place: carried by the same one or in the same room, and by KEEP (CONTAINER,WORN
when none is given) in the same container and worn in the same place, with its script
variables and states, tags and uses.  What was in it stays in it.  The new item is $p for
the rest of the script.  JavaScript has transform(item, name, keep).
MPPARDON [CODE] ([CRIME]/ALL) - CoffeeSUD: takes a character's warrants away (those for the
crime, by its name or a word of it, or all), quietly, under the law of the host's room (else
 where the character is).
MPFINE [CODE] +[AMOUNT]/-[AMOUNT]/[AMOUNT] - CoffeeSUD: adds to, takes from or sets the
fines the character owes there (in base value; TaxCollector collects them).
MPRELEASE [CODE] - CoffeeSUD: a prisoner's time is up: the guards come to walk them to the
release room, and the warrants that jailed them are done; one being taken in is let go for
now.
MPSUPPRESSLAW [CRIME/ALL] [N] (TICKS/HOURS/DAYS/WEEKS/MONTHS)/OFF - CoffeeSUD: no warrants
for the crime (or any) under the law of the host's room for a while, on the game clock (a
bare number is ticks); OFF ends it.  A save keeps it.
MPSHOP [SHOPKEEPER] REMOVE [ITEM] ([N]/ALL) / STOCK [ITEM] [N] / PRICE [ITEM] [AMOUNT/-1] /
CLEAR / RESET / BUDGET [AMOUNT] - CoffeeSUD: changes a shop's stock: REMOVE takes some (one)
 or all of a product away, STOCK sets how many there are (an item not stocked, one the
script can find or the catalog's, is copied onto a new shelf), PRICE fixes its price (-1:
the usual), CLEAR empties the shelves, RESET puts the stock back as it was built (a generic
shopkeeper), BUDGET sets what is left of its buying budget.  A name with spaces is quoted.
MPBANK [CODE] [BANK CHAIN] +[AMOUNT]/-[AMOUNT] ([REASON]) - CoffeeSUD: pays into a
character's account at a bank chain (opening it, as a deposit would) or takes out of it, in
base value, with a dated line in its ledger; a chain name with spaces is quoted.
MPEXCHANGE [CURRENCY]/DEFAULT [PERCENT] - CoffeeSUD: what coins of a currency fetch at every
 money changer, in percent of their value (100: as they are, which ends it), on top of each
changer's own RATE and cut; a save keeps it.
MPGENERATE ITEM/MOB/ROOM/AREA/QUEST [FILE] [ID] ([VAR]=[VALUE] ...) (INTO [CONTAINER]/TO
[MOB]/HERE/AT [ROOM]/[DIRECTION]) (SEED=[N]) - CoffeeSUD: generates from a template file (as
 GENERATE, a fresh roll each time): an item here, into a container or to a mob; a mob here
or at a room; a room or an area off the host's room in a free direction; or a quest,
started.  $b is the first thing made.  PLAYER_LEVEL, PARTY_SIZE, AREA_LEVEL, AREA_THEME,
HOUR, SEASON, WEATHER and GAME_DAY are defined for the template unless given.
MPGRANT [ITEM] [MOB NAME]/NOBODY (PROFILE) (NAME=[NEW NAME]) - CoffeeSUD: gives property: a
deed (its land changes hands and the deed goes to them), a vessel (kept with that character
so it saves with them, renamed with no prompt, which fills the [NAME] in its name, and
docked near here if it is not in a room) or an item with Prop_PrivateProperty.  PROFILE
records the owner as @PROFILE, the whole profile.  NOBODY takes it back.
MPLEARNRECIPE [MOB NAME] [SKILL] [RECIPE NAME]/[RECIPE LINE] - CoffeeSUD: the mob knows that
 recipe for good: one of the skill's own by name (as one marked HIDDEN=1), or a whole recipe
 line, its fields joined with \    .
MPPERK [MOB NAME] [PERK]/-[PERK] - CoffeeSUD: gives the mob that perk of world/perks.ini,
with its rewards, or (-) takes it off; its rewards stay.
MPRECRUIT [NPC] [PLAYER] (PARTY/REST) (NAME=[NAME]) - CoffeeSUD: the NPC becomes a character
 of the player's profile, keeping its race, class and level, stats, abilities, effects,
inventory, factions, tattoos and description, and leaves the world as an NPC; it joins the
party (PARTY, the default) or rests (REST).  NAME= gives its name (else the first word of
the NPC's).  It refuses, telling the player, if the profile or party is full or the name is
taken.  From JavaScript: Packages.com.planet_ink.coffee_mud.core.Recruits.recruit(npc,
player, 'PARTY', name).
MPLEVELUP [MOB NAME] ([N]) - CoffeeSUD: the mob gains exactly N levels (1 if not given),
each by the experience it needs, wherever it is within its level.  MPLEVELDOWN [MOB NAME]
([N]) takes N levels away, its experience set back with them.  MPEXP [MOB NAME] NEXTLEVEL
gives exactly the next level.  From JavaScript:
Packages.com.planet_ink.coffee_mud.core.LevelUps.up(mob, n, 'SCRIPT:name'), .down(mob, n)
and .toNext(mob).
MPRANK [MOB NAME] [LADDER] (+N|-N|=N|CHECK) - CoffeeSUD: moves the character up (+1 if not
given) or down a rank ladder of world/ranks.ini, or to rank N (0: off it), with the rank's
effects, title and (once) rewards; CHECK raises them as far as the next ranks' REQUIRES let.
  RANK([MOB NAME] [LADDER]) (the one-word RANK([MOB NAME]) is still a mob's Prop_MobRank) is
 their rank on it, 0 for none: $%RANK($n GUILD)%.  AHELP RANKLADDERS.
MPRESPEC [MOB NAME] ([SKILLS|EXPERTISES|STATS|CLASS|ALL]) ([NAME]|ALL) - CoffeeSUD: undoes
what the character bought with trains and practices, of those kinds (by commas; ALL if not
given), the one named or ALL, and gives back what each cost, free (AHELP PROP_RESPEC).
Skills that come by themselves stay.  From JavaScript:
Packages.com.planet_ink.coffee_mud.core.Purchases.respec(mob, 'SKILLS', 'ALL').
MPDEED [ROOM ID/AREA/HERE] [MOB NAME]/@PROFILE ([PRICE]) - CoffeeSUD: the land (a room or
area with Prop_RoomForSale, Prop_LotsForSale or Prop_AreaForSale) belongs to them, or to the
 whole profile; its back taxes are cleared, the price set if given, and the room updated as
a sale does.  A room ID with spaces is put in single quotes.
MPUNDEED [ROOM ID/AREA/HERE] - CoffeeSUD: the land is for sale again, its room reset as a
lost lot is.
MPREGENERATE [AREA NAME]/HERE (SEED=[N]/SEED=SAME) - CoffeeSUD: re-rolls the area, as its
Regenerate behaviour would (AHELP BEHAVIOR_REGENERATE), with its KEEP and SEED unless a seed
 is given; once the party has left, if they are inside.  An area with no Regenerate
behaviour is re-rolled from its GENSOURCE at once, unless a player is inside.
MPWEATHER [AREA/HERE] [WEATHER] (NEXT) (FOR [N] HOURS/DAYS) (QUIET) - CoffeeSUD: changes an
area's weather now, with the usual end and start messages to everyone under the sky and the
WEATHER_PROGs (QUIET: no messages), or with NEXT only the weather that comes next; FOR holds
 it there for that much game time, each change of weather coming back to it, then the
weather goes its own way.  A save keeps the hold.
MPROOMSTATE [ROOM ID/HERE/AREA NAME] [STATE] - CoffeeSUD: the RoomStates of the room (or its
 area), or of the area named, changes to that state now.
MPPASSTIME [N] HOURS/DAYS/WEEKS / UNTIL DAWN/DUSK/HOUR [N]/... (INTERRUPTIBLE) (QUIET) -
CoffeeSUD: game time passes, the world going on as it would (the clock paused for it if it
runs), up to three game days, the player told each hour (QUIET: not); INTERRUPTIBLE ends it
if they are hurt, attacked or moved.
MPINTERRUPT [CODE] ([MESSAGE]) - CoffeeSUD: ends the wait (WAIT, MPPASSTIME) or journey of
that character or their party, with the message.
MPDEBT [CODE] [TO WHOM] +[AMOUNT]/-[AMOUNT] (INTEREST [PERCENT]) (DUE [N]
HOURS/DAYS/WEEKS/MONTHS) (FOR [REASON]) / CLEAR - CoffeeSUD: adds to what a character owes
someone (a bank chain, as its loans do, or anyone), with interest each month and a due date
on the game clock; a minus pays some off, CLEAR forgives it all.
MPNOTRIGGER [TRIGGER NAME] [MILISECS]- this command will prevent given trigger for given
miliseconds.
MPFACTION [MOB] [FACTION] [VALUE] - changes faction value for given mob. Value is number,
range, or +NUM, --NUM.
MPWHILE ([IF CONDITION]) [COMMAND] - repeatedly executes commmand.
MPDAMAGE [MOB/ITEM] [MIN] [MAX] (KILL)- does random damage to the target. Kills only when
KILL parm given.
MPREJUV AREA/ROOM/[ROOMID]/[AREAID] (ITEMS/MOBS) - rejuv dead mobs, lost items from area or
room
MPRESET AREA/ROOM/[ROOMID]/[AREAID] - reload an area or room from the database
MPLOG ERROR/INFO/DEBUG HEADER MESSAGE - add an entry to the coffeemud server log
MPDEBUG MESSAGE - in builder mode or DEV=1 only, the message to the developer log (DEVLOG)
as [debug host@room file:line] MESSAGE; nothing in a normal game. debug(x) in a <SCRIPT>
does the same.
MPLIST [HOST] [VAR] [ADD/ADDUNIQUE/DEL/CLEAR/SHUFFLE/SORT] [WORDS] - change a list kept in a
 variable (the host and name as MPSETVAR's). FOR $X IN LIST [TEXT] - loops over a list's
items, the text put in first.
MPSTATE [CODE] [NAME] [VALUE/CLEAR] - keep a value on that one thing, as MPSETVAR @[CODE]
does.
MPMSG VALUE [N/+N/-N/*X//X], MPMSG TEXT [S/T/O] [TEXT/NULL], MPMSG TARGET [CODE] - in
CNCLMSG_PROG, change the message: its value, a text, or its target.
MPSIGNAL [TARGET] [NAME] ([ARGS]) (DELAY [TICKS]) - fires SIGNAL_PROG [NAME] on the target's
 scripts, queued and silent; the target is a thing, a room's ID, a room's exit (ROOMID:NORTH
 or HERE:NORTH), TAG:[TAG] (in the area; TAG:[TAG]@WORLD anywhere), ROOM, AREA or WORLD.
MPWAIT [TICKS], MPWAIT [N] [HOURS/DAYS/WEEKS/MONTHS], MPWAIT UNTIL ([CONDITION]) ([MAX
TICKS]) - pause the body here and go on at the next line later: after so many ticks, so much
 game time, or once the condition is true (tested each tick, up to 1000 ticks unless a most
is given). $n, $t, $o, $0-$9 and the IF and SWITCH blocks it is in are kept, and a save
keeps the wait. Not in a FOR or MPWHILE loop, nor in a function another line called.
MPSETINTERNAL CANCELWAITS drops the waits.
MPTAG [CODE] [ADD/DEL/TOGGLE] [TAG] - give a thing a tag, take it off, or toggle it.
MPSTEPQUEST [QUEST NAME] (+N/=N/=NAME) - moves the quest on to its next step; +N moves it N
steps, =N to step N; CoffeeSUD: =NAME to the step STEP NAME named.
MPMONEY [MOB/ITEM/ROOM] [(-)AMOUNT] - gives money, or with - takes it: to or from the mob,
an item's holder, or else the room's floor (inside the item, if it is a container). The
amount is a number, or a number and a coin (10 gold).
MPHEAL [MOB/ITEM] [MIN] [MAX] - heals the mob a random MIN to MAX hit points, or mends an
item that wears by as much (to 100).
MPPOSSESS [PC NAME] [MOB NAME] - the player takes over the NPC, as POSSESS does; QUIT brings
 them back.
MPSPEAK [MOB NAME] [LANGUAGE] - the mob starts speaking the language (its ID or name); an
NPC at full proficiency.
MPSETCLAN [MOB NAME] [CLAN] [ROLE] - puts the mob in the clan (ID or name) with the role, a
number or the role's name; a player joins as a member does, with the clan's entry script and
 CLAN_PROG.
MPRLOAD - not a command: it is in the list of commands, but it only logs a script error.
MPACCTATTOO [PC NAME] (-)[TATTOONAME] - like MPTATTOO, on the player's account: in this game
 the player's profile, shared by all their characters (see HASACCTATTOO). A number of ticks
before the name makes one that wears off.
MPRPEXP [MOB NAME] [EXP or TNL%] - like MPEXP, but role-playing experience, the kind
RPAWARDS in coffeemud.ini sets up; while RPAWARDS is empty, as it starts, it does nothing.
MEA [MOB/ROOM/AREA/WORLD] [TEXT] - short for MPECHOAT.
MER [MOB NAME] [TEXT] - short for MPECHOAROUND: the text to all in the mob's room but the
mob. In MEA, MER, MPECHOAT and MPECHOAROUND, NOSOUND before the text makes it seen only.
MPCASTEXT [SPELL] [TARGET] [ARGS] - as MPCAST, at full proficiency, with the words after the
 target given to the skill as a player would type them.
MPLINK [DIRECTION] [ROOM ID] [EXIT CLASS] ([EXIT NAME]) - makes an unsaved one-way exit from
 the monster's room, in the direction, to a room of the same area, if there is no exit that
way; only while the host is in its home area.
MPUNLINK [DIRECTION] - takes away an exit MPLINK made from the monster's room (not a saved
one, nor one to another area).
MPPUT [ITEM/MOB] [CONTAINER/ROOM/MOB/RIDEABLE/NULL] - silently puts the item in a container
(moving it to the container's holder), a room or a mob's inventory, or the mob on a
rideable; NULL or NONE takes it out, or off.
MPHIT [MOB NAME] - the monster makes one attack at the mob, with the weapon it wields; no
one's fight target is left changed.
MPACHIEVE [PC NAME] [ACHIEVEMENT ID] [AMOUNT] - bumps the player's progress in the
achievement by the amount; with no amount, grants it outright, but only from a mob with the
CMDPLAYERS security flag.
MPACCUSE [MOB NAME] [VICTIM/''] [CRIME] - files a warrant against the mob under the law of
the host's room, for a crime of that law by its ID (a basic, tax or skill crime), or given
whole in five words: where, flags, name, sentence, warning.
MPLLM [HOST] [VAR NAME] [MESSAGE] - sends the message to this host's LLM chat (an LLM must
be set up, LANGCHAIN4J_ in coffeemud.ini) and sets the variable, as MPSETVAR does (but not @
 hosts), to the reply. MPSETINTERNAL LLMPROMPT [TEXT] sets the chat's instructions and
LLMMAXMSGS [N] how many messages it keeps (5); with no LLMPROMPT, the first MPLLM's message
becomes them, and its variable is set empty.
MPSETINTERNAL [SETTING] [VALUE] - changes how this host's scripts run: SCOPE
[GLOBAL/NAME/INDIVIDUAL] where its variables are kept (GLOBAL or nothing, the store all
share; a name, one shared by the scripts of that scope; INDIVIDUAL or *, its own); VARHOST
[INSTANCE/NAME], see MPSETVAR @; NODELAY TRUE, its triggers run at once, not on the next
tick; ACTIVETRIGGER(S) TRUE, they run even while the monster fights, follows someone or is
under half its hit points (not asleep or bound); MULTITRIGGER(S) TRUE, one event may set off
 more than the first of them; DEFAULTQUEST [QUEST], the quest * names; SAVABLE [TRUE/FALSE],
 whether the script is saved with the host; PASSIVE FALSE, while its area is not active it
does nothing and drops what is queued; NEEDPC TRUE, while no player is in its room only what
 is queued runs; TRACE [TRUE/FALSE], SCRIPTTRACE for the host; CANCELWAITS, drops the waits
MPWAIT left pending; LLMPROMPT and LLMMAXMSGS, see MPLLM.
ELSEIF [CONDITION] (or ELSE IF) - another test in an IF, before its ELSE or ENDIF.
WHILE ([CONDITION]) ([MAX PASSES]) ... ENDWHILE - loops while the condition holds, at most
1000 passes unless a most is given. CONTINUE goes on to the next pass of a WHILE or FOR,
BREAK leaves it.
MPLOCAL [NAME] [VALUE] - a named local, read as $([NAME]), for as long as the body runs.
FUNCTION_PROG [NAME] [PARAM] [PARAM]... binds the call's words to $([PARAM]), the last
taking the rest.
MPJSFILE [FILE] ([ARGS]) - runs a JavaScript file (under resources/, or world:path) as a
<SCRIPT> is, with args the rest of the line.  In a <SCRIPT> or such a file, cancel(), or a
last value of 'cancel', ends the prog as RETURN CANCEL does.
MPQOBJECTIVE [CODE] [QUEST] ADD [ID] [COUNT] [TEXT] - CoffeeSUD: gives a character an
objective in their quest journal (* is the script's quest); then SET [ID] [N], BUMP [ID]
([N]), DONE [ID], FAIL [ID], HIDE [ID], SHOW [ID], or CLEAR ([ID]). Reaching the count makes
 it DONE; QUESTS shows them, and the character is told of each change.  AT=[ROOM
ID/AREA/QUESTOBJ:N] after ADD's ID, or AT [ID] [WHERE] later (AT [ID] alone forgets it),
says where the objective is: QUESTS shows it as (area, room) and QUESTS WHERE gives the way
(QUESTTRACK in coffeemud.ini or world.ini: OFF, AREA, or PATH, the default); QUESTOBJ:N (or
QUESTMOB:, QUESTITEM:, by number or name) is wherever the quest's Nth mob or item is now.
MPQJOURNAL [CODE] [QUEST] [TEXT] - CoffeeSUD: an entry in the character's quest journal,
dated on the game calendar (QUESTS [QUEST], QUESTS LOG).
MPCHANNEL (!)[CHANNEL] MESSAGE - send a message to a channel
MPTRACKTO [MOB NAME] - forces the mob to track down the given mob.
MPWALKTO [MOB NAME] - forces the mob to track down the given mob, land surface only.
MPAFFECT [SPELL] [MOB NAME] [PARMS] - automatically casts a spell on a mob.
MPBEHAVE [BEHAVIOR] [MOB NAME] [PARMS] - adds a behavior to the mob.
MPUNBEHAVE [BEHAVIOR] [MOB NAME] - removes a behavior from a  mob.
MPTATTOO [MOB] (-)[TATTOONAME] - adds or removes the given tattoo for the mob.
MPPLAYERCLASS [MOB] [CCLASS ID] ([LVL])... - changes current char class & optionally level.
MPTITLE [MOB] (-) [TITLE] - adds or removes the given title string from the mob.
MPENABLE [MOB] [ABILITY NAME] [PROF] [STR] - adds a new skill to the mob, or mods prof.
w/++,--.
MPDISABLE [MOB] [ABILITY NAME] - removes a skill from the mob.
MPSAVEVAR [MOB NAME] [VAR NAME] - saves the variable set using MPSETVAR to the database.
MPLOADVAR [MOB NAME] [VAR NAME] - loads the variable from the database.
MPM2I2M [MOB/ITEM] - this strange command turns a mob into an item and back into a mob
MPHIDE [MOB/ITEM/EXIT] - makes the target undetectable by any means.
MPUNHIDE [MOB/ITEM/EXIT] - reverses the affects of MPHIDE -- does not affect Hide or other
skills.
MPOPEN [ITEM/EXIT] - opens a closed container or door: that one side only, silently, and
with no relock timer (MPDOOR changes both sides, with a message).
MPCLOSE [ITEM/EXIT] - closes an open container or door: that one side only, silently (MPDOOR
 does both).
MPLOCK [ITEM/EXIT] - closes and locks a lockable container or door: that one side only,
silently (MPDOOR does both).
MPUNLOCK [ITEM/EXIT] - unlocks a locked container or door, but does not open: that one side
only, silently (MPDOOR does both).
MPSETCLANDATA [CLAN] [VAR] [VALUE] - changes a datum about the given clan.
MPARGSET [$VAR] [VALUE] - changes internal $(i,n,t,0,1,..9) object to one specified by
value.
MPLOADQUESTOBJ [QUEST] [QVARNAME] [$VAR] - loads quest obj into internal $(i,n,t,0,1,..9)
object.
MPUNLOADSCRIPT [SCRIPT FILE NAME] - unloads a file script from the resources cache for
refreshing
MPQSET [QUEST] [QVARNAME] [VALUE] - set temp quest var to given value.
BREAK -- return/break out of the current if condition or program script.
RETURN [OPTIONAL STRING] - exits the existing script, returning the string given.
<SCRIPT> - embed Javascript in Scriptable event.  Must be closed with </SCRIPT>.
[COMMAND] [PARMS]- any valid coffee mud command!
** NOTES! For those commands which have multiple parameters (specifically MPAT, MPFORCE,
MPCAST, MPECHOAT, you must use "'" characters in order to group any words in the first
parameter of those commands.  Inside your command parameters, whether it be text, or even
when specifying MOB or ITEM names, you may use any of the following freely:
$a - name of the area the monsters in
$b - name of last item/mob loaded w/mmpload/mpoload
$B - display text of last item/mob loaded w/mmpload/mpoload
$c - random npc/pc inhabitants name
$C - random npc/pc inhabitants name
$i - monsters name
$I - monsters display text
$n - source of triggers name
$N - source of triggers name
$t - target of triggers name
$T - target of triggers name
$r - random pc inhabitants name
$R - random pc inhabitants name
$j - he/she of the monster
$e - he/she of the trigger source
$d - title of monsters room location
$D - long desc of monsters room location
$f - name of the person monster follows
$E - he/she of the trigger target
$F - he/she of the person monster follows
$g - lowercase form of the message from a MPCALLFUNC, MASK_PROG or SPEECH_PROG.
$G - uppercase form of the message from a MPCALLFUNC, MASK_PROG or SPEECH_PROG.
$u - the name of the character at the terminal, the one being played (U the same).
$J - he/she of a random pc inhabitant
$k - his/her of the monster
$l - list of all mobs (excluding monster). See "." syntax below.
$L - list of all Items in room. See "." syntax below.
$m - his/her of the trigger source
$M - his/her of the trigger target
$K - his/her of a random pc inhabitant
$y - sir/madam of the trigger source
$Y - sir/madam of the trigger target
$o - item1 name
$O - item1 name
$p - item2 name
$P - item2 name
$w - owner of item1s name
$W - owner of item2s name
$x - random valid exit's direction
$X - random valid exit's name
$xN- north exit's name
$0..$9- temporary variables set by other commands.

$<[CODE] [VAR NAME]> - the variable of the given name, of the given code.  Where code is $i,
 $n, $t, $o, or $p.  See MPSETVAR.

${[NUM] [QUEST NAME]} - a mob name from the given quest, if the quest is running. The number
 corresponds to the order in which mobs were designated in the quest script. Counting starts
 at 1.

$[[NUM] [QUEST NAME]] - an item name from the given quest, if the quest is running. The
number corresponds to the order in which items were designated in the quest script. Counting
 starts at 1.

$%FUNCTION(PARM1 PARM2..)% - replace this code with a value from one of the internal
functions.  While the names are the same as the eval functions above, their parameters will
be slightly different.  The functions which may be included in this code include the
following:
 - RAND() random number between 1 and 100.
 - HAS([CODE])  name of a random item in given mobs inventory.
 - HASNUM([CODE] [ITEM])  number of the given items in given mobs inventory.
 - WORN([CODE])  name of a random worn item in given mobs inventory.
 - ISNPC([CODE])  not implemented.
 - ISPC([CODE])  not implemented.
 - ISGOOD([CODE])  returns the alignment string of the given mob.
 - ISNAME([CODE])  Returns the real/full name of the given object.
 - CURRENCY([CODE])  Returns the native currency of the given object.
 - MATH([EXPR]) returns evaluated mathematical expressions. +-*\\
 - MOOD([MOB NAME]) the given mobs mood.
 - NUMMOBSINAREA([MOB NAME]) number of mobs in area matching mask.
 - NUMMOBS([MOB NAME]) number of mobs in world matching mask.
 - NUMRACES([MOB NAME]) number of mobs in world matching race.
 - ISEVIL([CODE])  alignment number of the given mob.
 - ISNEUTRAL([CODE])  short alignment string of the given mob.
 - ISFIGHT([CODE])  name of the mob the given mob is fighting.
 - ISALIVE([CODE])  health of the given mob.
 - ISIMMORT([CODE])  not implemented.
 - ISBIRTHDAY([CODE]) returns birthday of the mob
 - ISCHARMED([CODE])  name of the charm spell the mob is under.
 - STAT([CODE] [STAT]) value of the given stat for the given object.
 - DATETIME(DAY/TIME/MONTH/YEAR) displays the appropriate numberic value.
 - GSTAT([CODE] [STAT]) like STAT, but player data accessible. See Generic.java.
 - AFFECTED([CODE]) name of a random spell affect on the object.
 - FACTION([CODE] [FACTION]) name of the range the mob has in given faction.
 - ISBEHAVE([CODE]) class ids of the behaviors on the object.
 - ISFOLLOW([CODE])  name of the mob the given mob is following.
 - ISSERVANT([CODE])  name of the mob the given mob is serving.
 - HITPRCNT([CODE])  % of hit points remaining for given mob.
 - INLOCALE() name of the room type the monster is in.
 - INROOM() raw id of the room the monster is in.
 - ISODD([AMT]) echos AMT if AMT is an odd, whole number.
 - ISRECALL([CODE]) start room of the given mob.
 - INAREA() name of the area the monster is in.
 - ISHERE() name of the area the monster is in.
 - VAR([CODE] [VAR NAME]) Value of the given variable.
 - SEX([CODE]) sex of the given mob.
 - POSITION([CODE]) position name of the given mob.
 - LEVEL([CODE]) level of the given mob.
 - QUESTPOINTS([CODE]) questpoints of the given mob.
 - PRACS([CODE]) practices of the given mob.
 - TRAINS([CODE]) trains of the given mob.
 - CLASS([CODE]) class of the given mob.
 - BASECLASS([CODE]) base class of the given mob.
 - RACE([CODE]) race of the given mob.
 - RACECAT([CODE]) racial category of the given mob.
 - GOLDAMT([CODE]) number of gold coins the given mob has.
 - EXP([CODE]) number of experience points the given mob has.
 - VALUE([CODE] [CURRENCY]) base value the given mob has in given currency.
 - QUESTWINNER([CODE]) returns a list of all the quests the mob was won.
 - QUESTSCRIPTED([CODE]) returns a list of all the quests the mob is scripted for.
 - QUESTMOB([QUEST NAME]) returns a list of all the mobs desigated by this quest.
 - QUESTOBJ([QUEST NAME])  returns a list of all the items desigated by this quest.
 - QUESTROOM([QUEST NAME])  returns a list of all rooms desigated by this quest.
 - ISQUESTMOBALIVE([QUEST NAME]) returns a list of all live mobs desigated by this quest.
 - ISTIME() returns the approx time of day in words.
 - ISSEASON() returns the season.
 - ISWEATHER() returns the weather
 - ISMOON() returns the moon phase
 - ISDAY() returns word day or evening.
 - EVAL()  not implemented.
 - NUMBER([VALUE/CODE]) Returns the numberic value of the given argument.
 - RANDNUM([VALUE/CODE]) returns random number from 1..value/code.
 - RAND0NUM([VALUE/CODE]) returns random number from 0..value/code-1.
 - ROOMMOB([NUM]) returns the NUMth mob in the room's name.
 - ROOMITEM([NUM]) whether the NUMth item in the room's NAME.
 - NUMMOBSROOM([*/NAME]) returns the number of named mobs in the room.
 - NUMPCSAREA() returns the number of pcs in the area.
 - NUMPCSROOM() returns the number of pcs in the room.
 - EXPLORED([CODE] [AREA/WORLD]) displays % explored of code mob.
 - NUMITEMSROOM() returns the number of items in the room.
 - NUMITEMSMOB([NAME]) returns the number of items the mob has.
 - MOBITEM([MOBNAME] [NUM]) returns the NUMth item owned by mob mobname.
 - INCONTAINER([CODE]) returns container of an item, or the mount of a mob.
 - ISABLE([CODE] [SKILL NAME]) the mobs proficiency in the given skill/ability.
 - ISOPEN([CODE/DIRECTION]) "true" if the container item, or direction name is open.
 - ISLOCKED([CODE/DIRECTION]) the key name if the container, or direction has a lock.
 - STRIN([STRING] [STRING]) word number of the second string if it appears in the first.
 - CALLFUNC([FUNCTION] [PARM]..) the value returned by the FUNCTION_PROG named.
 - CALLFUNC([TARGET] [FUNCTION] [PARM]..) the value returned by a FUNCTION_PROG of another
thing's scripts.
 - DEITY([CODE]) returns a mobs deity.
 - CLAN([CODE]) returns a mobs clan.
 - CLANRANK([CODE]) returns mobs clan role/rank as a number.
 - CLANDATA([CLAN] [VAR]) returns the given clans data based on var.
 - IPADDRESS([CODE]) return ip address of player.
 - QVAR([QUEST] [CODE]) returns temp quest vars.
 - VARNAMES([HOST] ([PREFIX])) returns the names of the host's variables (* for any host)
starting with the prefix, sorted and separated by spaces.
 - ISTURNBASED() and ISPAUSED() return true or false.
 - SAVESLOT() returns the name of the save the game was last saved to or restored from.
 - GAMETIME() returns the game's time in game milliseconds; TURNS() the turns since the game
 began.
 - PARTYSIZE([CODE]), PARTYLEADER([CODE]) and PARTY([CODE]) return the size of the mob's
group, its leader's name, and the names in it, the leader first; INPARTY([CODE] [CODE]) true
 or false.
 - GENVAR([AREA] [VAR]) returns a variable the generator that made the area had.
 - MEMORY([NPC] [WHO] [MET/COUNT/LASTSEEN/DAYSSINCE/LASTTOPIC]) returns what the NPC
remembers of the character.
 - LISTCOUNT([LIST]), LISTGET([LIST] [N]) (from 0), LISTFIND([LIST] [WORD]) (-1 if not
there), LISTPICK([LIST]) and LISTJOIN([LIST] [SEPARATOR]) read a list: its words ("quoted
words" kept together), or the items between its commas if it has any.
 - DATETIME(STAMP) the area clock's hours since its year 0, DATETIME(DAYOFYEAR),
DATETIME(WEEKDAY) and WEEKDAY() the weekday's name; GAMETIME(HOURS/DAYS/MONTHS/YEARS) the
stamp in other units; ELAPSED([STAMP] [UNIT]) the time since a stamp; TICKS([N] [UNIT]) the
ticks in so much game time, for timed tattoos.
 - CATALOGCOUNT([NAME]) the copies of a catalog mob or item in the world.
 - STATE([CODE] [NAME]) the value MPSTATE keeps on that one thing.
 - MSG(TYPE/VALUE/SOURCE/TARGET/TOOL/TOOLID/STEXT/TTEXT/OTEXT/SMINOR/TMINOR/OMINOR) a part
of the message a CNCLMSG_PROG or EXECMSG_PROG reacts to (EXECMSG_PROG's is a copy): its
type, its value (damage, experience), the names of who and what, the tool's ID, its texts,
and the type each sees.
 - UPPER, LOWER, CAP, LEN, TRIM and ANAME([STRING]); SUBSTR([STRING] [START] ([LENGTH]))
from 0; REPLACE([STRING] 'OLD' 'NEW'); PADRIGHT([STRING] [N]); PLURAL([WORD] ([N]));
STRPOS([STRING] [PART]) (-1 if not there); STRSTARTS and STRENDS give true or false.
 - DICE(3d6+2); PICK([LIST]) one at random; WPICK(a:70 b:25) one by weight; ROLLNORMAL([N]
[DIE] ([PLUS])); CLAMP([N] [LOW] [HIGH]); ABS([N]). NUMBER() takes signs and decimals.
 - NUMTAGGED([TAG]) how many things have the tag, TAGGED([TAG]) true or false, TAGS([CODE])
the thing's tags, as a list.
 - ARG([NAME]) the value LOAD=[FILE] [NAME]=[VALUE] gave the script, or the file's
ARGDEFAULT [NAME]=[VALUE] line's.
 - PARM([NAME]) a generic behaviour's parameter: what its host was given, or the default
(AHELP GENBEHAVIOR).
 - AFFINITY([NPC] [CODE]) an NPC's opinion of a character, a number; AFFINITY([NPC] [CODE]
BAND) HOSTILE, COLD, NEUTRAL, FRIENDLY or DEVOTED (AHELP PROP_AFFINITY).
 - RANK([CODE]) a mob's rank (Prop_MobRank), or NORMAL (AHELP PROP_MOBRANK).
 - THREAT([NPC] [CODE]) a character's threat to an NPC; TOPTHREAT([NPC]) the one here with
the most; WEAKEST([NPC]) the enemy here with the least of their hit points left;
OPPONENT([NPC] 'MASK=[ZAPPER MASK]') the first enemy here the mask fits.  Each gives a name
for MPKILL, or nothing.
 - PHASE([CODE]) a boss's BossPhases phase, from 1 (0 for none).
 - ALARM([CODE] [NAME]) the ticks before a named alarm (MPALARM NAME=, MPTELEGRAPH) of the
thing's scripts goes off, or 0 for none.
 - RESPAWNROOM([CODE]) a character's respawn point's room id (Prop_Checkpoint,
MPSETRESPAWN), or nothing.
 - DOORSTATE([ROOM ID/HERE] [DIRECTION/CONTAINER]) open, closed or locked, or nothing when
there is no door: any room, from anywhere.
 - SWITCHSTATE([CODE/ROOM ID:DIRECTION/DIRECTION]) the state of its Prop_Switch, or nothing.
 - ROOMWEIGHT([ROOM ID/HERE/CODE]) what a room's mobs (with what they carry) and items
weigh.
 - CONTENTWEIGHT([CODE]) what is in or on a thing (and sits on it) weighs.
 - SETCOUNT([CODE] [SET]) how many pieces of an item set (Prop_ItemSet) count for one: worn,
 or carried.
 - WARRANTS([CODE]) how many warrants are out against a character, under the law of the
host's room (else where they are).
 - FINESOWED([CODE]) the fines they owe there, in base value; ISWANTED([CODE] ([CRIME]))
true or false.
 - MONEYSTR([AMOUNT] ([CURRENCY]) (LONG/SHORT)) an amount in base value in coin names: 36
CROWN gives 3 silver shillings (SHORT: as shops list prices); the host's currency when none
is given.
 - PRICE([ITEM] ([SHOPKEEPER])) what the shop asks the source ($n) for the item (a thing, or
 a name in its stock), in its coin names; the host, or the first shopkeeper in its room,
when none is given.
 - DENOMNAME([CURRENCY] [VALUE] ([COUNT])) a denomination's name: CROWN 12 3 gives 3 silver
shillings.  From JavaScript: MONEYSTR$(36, 'CROWN', 'LONG') and so on.
 - SHOPPRICE([SHOPKEEPER] [ITEM] ([CUSTOMER])) what the shop asks the customer (the source
when none is named) for the item, in base value; in an IF, SHOPPRICE([SHOPKEEPER] [ITEM] >
[N]).
 - SHOPBUDGET([SHOPKEEPER]) what is left of the shop's buying budget, or -1 for no limit.
 - BANKBALANCE([CODE] [BANK CHAIN] ([CURRENCY])) a character's coins at a bank chain, in
base value.
 - EXCHANGE([CURRENCY]) what its coins fetch at money changers, in percent of their value
(MPEXCHANGE; 100 as they are).
 - DEBT([CODE] [TO WHOM]) what they owe; DEBT([CODE] [TO WHOM] DUE) the game hours until it
falls due (below 0 when past due), or nothing when they owe nothing; in an IF, DEBT([CODE]
[TO WHOM] > [N]).
 - JS([EXPRESSION]) or JS$([EXPRESSION]) the value of a JavaScript expression, as text.
 - QOBJECTIVE([CODE] [QUEST] [ID]) a character's quest objective: its count, DONE or FAILED,
 or nothing if they have none such.
 - QUESTSTATUS([CODE] [QUEST]) how the quest stands for them: ACTIVE, WON, FAILED,
ABANDONED, EXPIRED, or nothing.
 - QUESTOUTCOME([CODE] [QUEST]) the outcome word MPQUESTWIN gave them, or why it failed.
 - QUESTWINS([CODE] [QUEST]) how many times the character won the quest; QUESTWINAGE([CODE]
[QUEST]) the game hours since they last did, or -1.
 - OBJTYPE([CODE]) the thing's class ID, in lower case.
 - NUMRACESINAREA([RACE NAME]) number of mobs in the area of that race.
 - ISSPEAKING([CODE]) the name of the language the mob is speaking, or Common.
 - ISCONTENT([CODE]) the names of the things in the container (at any depth), or of the
riders of the rideable.
 - WORNON([CODE] [LOCATION]) the names of the things the mob wears on the location.
 - CLANQUALIFIES([CLAN]) what it takes to join the clan, in words: its masks, whether only
family may, and how many clans of its category one may belong to.
 - HASACCTATTOO([CODE]) the tattoos on the player's account: the profile, shared by all
their characters.
 - SHOPITEM([SHOPKEEPER] [NUM]) the name of the NUMth thing the shop sells; $9 becomes its
price.
 - NUMITEMSSHOP([SHOPKEEPER]) the number of things the shop sells.
 - SHOPHAS([SHOPKEEPER]) the name of a random thing the shop sells; $9 becomes its price.
 - ISMONTH() the month on the area's clock, as a number.
 - ISYEAR() the year on the area's clock.
 - ISRLHOUR() the hour (0-23) on the computer's real clock: real-world time, not game time.
 - ISRLDAY() the day of the month on the computer's real clock (real-world time).
 - ISRLMONTH() the month (1-12) on the computer's real clock (real-world time).
 - ISRLYEAR() the year on the computer's real clock (real-world time).
 - HASTATTOOTIME([CODE] [TATTOONAME]) the ticks before the mob's tattoo wears off (0 if it
never does; nothing if none).
 - ISHOUR() the hour of the day on the area's clock.
 - ITEMCOUNT([CODE]) the count of things ITEMCOUNT() compares.
 - CANSEE([CODE] [CODE]) and CANHEAR([CODE] [CODE]) true or false, as the tests.
 - QUESTAREA([QUEST NAME]) the names of the areas the quest's rooms are in.
 - EXPERTISE([CODE] [SKILL] [KIND]) the mob's expertise of that kind in the skill.
 - ROOMPC([NUM/NAME]) the name, as a command takes it (2.bob), of the NUMth player in the
room.
 - AREAPC([NUM/NAME]) the name of the NUMth player in the area.
 - HASTAG([CODE]) the thing's tags, as TAGS() gives them.
 - FACTIONVALUE([CODE] [FACTION]) the mob's number in the faction; FACTIONBAND([CODE]
[FACTION]) the code of the range it is in. Nothing if it has no standing in the faction.

Any of the $ codes may be followed by a period and a literal number to designate a
particular word inside a string of many words.  For instance if $o evaluates to "a magic
wand", $o.1 would evalulate to "magic".  If $l evaluated to "orc bob hassan", $l.2 would
give "hassan".  This syntax can also be followed by ".." to grab substrings.  For instance,
if $o evaluates to "a magic wand", $o.1.. would evaluate to "magic wand".
```

<a id="behavior-sentry"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_SENTRY

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 2026.

```text
Behavior   : Sentry
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : (SPOT=[N]) (INTRUDERS="[MASK]") (ALARM="RADIUS=[N] MASK=[MASK] MSG=[TEXT]")
(ALERTTICKS=[N]) (ALARMITEM="[ITEM NAME]")
Example    : SPOT=30 ALARM="RADIUS=6 MASK=-NAMES +bandit MSG=Intruders! To arms!"
ALERTTICKS=40 ALARMITEM="a brass gong"
Description:
CoffeeSUD: a lookout.  It sees an intruder here or next door: a player's character or one
following them, or whoever INTRUDERS fits.  One hidden or sneaking it spots at SPOT% a tick
(25), less their Hide or Sneak proficiency, and half that next door.  Then, or when it is
attacked, it raises the alarm: a shout of MSG (a NOISE message, which EXECMSG_PROG can
catch), and every NPC within RADIUS rooms (6) that fits MASK wakes (a Sleeper stays up) and
is alert for ALERTTICKS (40): it heads for the alarm room, or for the intruder if they are
near, and attacks them or their party, while its Schedule or Patroller waits.  ALARMITEM is
an item in its room that anyone, a player too, may PUSH or PULL to raise the alarm.  It
raises it at most once in ALERTTICKS.  Silence the lookout first, and a camp can be taken
tent by tent.
```

<a id="behavior-sleeper"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_SLEEPER

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 2043.

```text
Behavior   : Sleeper
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : (ALWAYS/SLEEPS=[DAWN/DAY/DUSK/NIGHT/FROM-TO]) (BED="[ITEM]")
(WAKEON=[ATTACK,NOISE,ENTER,LIGHT,TOUCH]) (WAKECHANCE=[N]) (DEEP) (GRUMBLE="[TEXT]")
(AWAKEFOR=[TICKS]) (ALARM)
Example    : ALWAYS WAKEON=NOISE,ENTER WAKECHANCE=40 GRUMBLE="Who disturbs Grok?" ALARM
Description:
CoffeeSUD: a sleeping NPC that noise wakes.  It sleeps always (the default), or at SLEEPS= a
 time of day or hours on the area's clock (not TOD= or HOURS=, which would switch the whole
behaviour off), on BED= if it is there.  WAKEON says what may wake it (all of them, by
default) and WAKECHANCE (50) how likely each is: a fight in the room makes it likelier, one
next door less likely; someone entering sneaking or hidden takes off their Sneak or Hide
proficiency; one carrying a light adds to it; TOUCH is anything done to it but looking.
DEEP: only an attack wakes it.  Woken, it says GRUMBLE, stays up AWAKEFOR ticks (20) and
then sleeps again, and with ALARM shouts an alarm that wakes the NPCs round about: its
Sentry's ALARM= if it has one (AHELP BEHAVIOR_SENTRY), else six rooms and 'Intruders!'.
LOOK at it says it is sleeping soundly, or that it stirs when something nearly woke it.
```

<a id="behavior-sounder"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_SOUNDER

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 475.

```text
Behavior   : Sounder
Targets    : Room, MOBs, Items, Areas
Parameters : (Max/Min ticks;) ([EMOTE CODE] [EMOTE STRING];)
Example    : sound 80 wiggles his bottom.;sound 60 smiles evilly.;sound 20 burps!
Example    : min=20 max=20;wear $p looks good on you.;remove Now you don't look so
good.;remove_room $n doesn't look so good.

An alternative to the Emoter behavior, this allows you to create very simple emoting
triggers based on percent chances every tick, or based on event triggers such as getting an
item, or leaving a room.  Each emote trigger is semicolon (;) separated, and the first
trigger may instead be a set of ticks.  Valid emote codes include the following:
SOUND [PCT CHANCE] - every min/max ticks, this will be emoted % chance of the time.
GET - if an item is gotten (or THE item), this will emote to the getter.
GET_ROOM - if an item is gotten (or THE item), this will emote to the room (not the getter).
DROP - if an item is dropped (or THE item), this will emote to the getter.
DROP_ROOM - if an item is dropped (or THE item), this will emote to the room (not the
getter).
PUSH - if an item is pushed (or THE item), this will emote to the pusher.
PUSH_ROOM - if an item is pushed (or THE item), this will emote to the room (not the
pusher).
PULL - if an item is pulled (or THE item), this will emote to the pulled.
PULL_ROOM - if an item is pulled (or THE item), this will emote to the room (not the
puller).
EAT - if an item is eaten (or THE item), this will emote to the eater.
EAT_ROOM - if an item is eaten (or THE item), this will emote to the room (not the getter).
MOUNT - if an item is mounted (or THE item), this will emote to the mounter.
MOUNT_ROOM - if an item is mounted (or THE item), this will emote to the room (not the
getter).
DRINK - if an item is drunk (or THE item), this will emote to the drinker.
DRINK_ROOM - if an item is drunk (or THE item), this will emote to the room (not the
getter).
SIT - if an item is sat on (or THE item), this will emote to the sitter.
SIT_ROOM - if an item is sat on (or THE item), this will emote to the room (not the getter).
SLEEP - if an item is slept on (or THE item), this will emote to the sleeper.
SLEEP_ROOM - if an item is slept on (or THE item), this will emote to the room (not the
getter).
WEAR - if an item is worn (or THE item), this will emote to the wearer.
WEAR_ROOM - if an item is worn (or THE item), this will emote to the room (not the getter).
OPEN - if an item is opened (or THE item), this will emote to the wearer.
OPEN_ROOM - if an item is opened (or THE item), this will emote to the room (not the
getter).
CLOSE - if an item is closed (or THE item), this will emote to the wearer.
CLOSE_ROOM - if an item is closed (or THE item), this will emote to the room (not the
getter).
HOLD - if an item is held (or THE item), this will emote to the wearer.
HOLD_ROOM - if an item is held (or THE item), this will emote to the room (not the getter).
WIELD - if an item is wielded (or THE item), this will emote to the wearer.
WIELD_ROOM - if an item is wielded (or THE item), this will emote to the room (not the
getter).
REMOVE - if an item is removed (or THE item), this will emote to the remover.
REMOVE_ROOM - if an item is removed (or THE item), this will emote to the room (not the
getter).
PORTAL_ENTER - if the room is entered, this will emote to the one entering.
PORTAL_ENTER_ROOM - if the room is entered, this will emote to the others in the room.
PORTAL_EXIT - if the room is left, this will emote to the one leaving.
PORTAL_EXIT_ROOM - if the room is left, this will emote to the others in the room.
DAMAGE - if the object is hurt, or used to hurt, this will emote to the one hurting.
DAMAGE_ROOM - if the object is hurt, or used to hurt, this will emote to the others in the
room.
FIGHT - if the object is attacking, or used to attack, this will emote to the one attacking.
FIGHT_ROOM - if the object is attacking, or used to attack, this will emote to the others in
 the room.

The emote strings may be any text, and the following codes may be included:
$p - the name of the item with the behavior.
$n - the name of the source of the emote, or the source of the trigger.
$e - the he/she of $n.
$s - the his/her of $n.

CoffeeSUD: a bark table, entries EVENT: [CHANCE=N] [COOLDOWN=N] [ONCEPERPLAYER] line | line
..., among the codes above or one to a line in a file named by FILE=[PATH].  A line is
[WEIGHT] [{MASK}] [SAY|EMOTE|SOUND] text ("text is said, :text emoted, an emote by default),
 $n the one it is about; one line is drawn by weight with the game's dice, of those whose
mask fits $n.  CHANCE= is the percent chance it barks at all, COOLDOWN= the ticks before
that event barks again, ONCEPERPLAYER once for each character.  The events: GREET (a
character arrives), GREET_FIRST (the first time it sees them; GREET if it has none),
SEE_MOB(MASK) (anyone arriving who fits the mask or has the words in their name),
SEE_ITEM(MASK) (a character arrives carrying such an item), KILL (it kills $n), ALLY_DIES
(one of its group or race dies, $n the killer), FLEE (it flees), FIGHT (it is attacked),
HURT<N (below N% of its hit points, once until it heals), IDLE (each tick: give it a
CHANCE=), DAWN, DAY, DUSK and NIGHT, RAIN, SNOW and CLEAR (as each begins), SHOP_LIST,
SHOP_BUY, BRIBED (given money), and WIELD(MASK), WEAR, HOLD, GET and DROP (of an item, by
anyone in the room).  A saved game keeps whom it has greeted and its once-per-character
barks. Lines also accept Emoter's conditional prefixes (DAY/NIGHT, seasons, weather,
INDOORS/OUTDOORS, IFVAR name=value), MASK="...", ONCE and WEIGHT=n; idle ONCE lines are
selected for each reader. See AHELP BEHAVIOR_EMOTER.
Example    : GREET: COOLDOWN=20 2 SAY Move along. | 1 SAY Keep your blade
sheathed.;WIELD(+WEAPONCLASS SWORD): SAY Put that away in the city!;NIGHT: SAY Curfew's at
the bell.;HURT<30: SAY To me! Guards!
```

<a id="behavior-targetpriority"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_TARGETPRIORITY

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 3348.

```text
Behavior   : TargetPriority
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters :
PREFER=[HEALER/CASTER/LOWESTHP/LOWESTARMOR/LEADER/LASTHITME/STRONGEST/MASK:[ZAPPER
MASK]],... (SWITCH=[N]) (STICKY=[N]) (TAUNTABLE)
Example    : PREFER=CASTER,LOWESTHP SWITCH=50
Example    : PREFER=LASTHITME STICKY=4
Example    : PREFER="LOWESTHP,MASK:-CLASS +Cleric" TAUNTABLE
Description:
CoffeeSUD: which of its foes the monster attacks.  PREFER lists, in order, what it goes for:
 HEALER (the one with the most healing abilities), CASTER (the most spells, prayers, chants
or songs), LOWESTHP (the least of their hit points left), LOWESTARMOR (the worst protected),
 LEADER (the party's leader), LASTHITME (whoever hit it last), STRONGEST (the most
powerful), MASK: (the first a zapper mask fits; last in the list, and the list in quotes
when the mask has spaces).  The first that names someone here wins.  Its foes are those it
or they fight, whom it can see.  SWITCH is the percent chance each tick that it looks again
(30), STICKY the ticks after a switch before it may switch again (3).  TAUNTABLE: one with a
 clear lead in its threat (half as much again as the next: damage, healing, MPTHREAT, a
taunt) comes before the list.
```

<a id="behavior-taxibehavior"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_TAXIBEHAVIOR

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 3385.

```text
Behavior   : TaxiBehavior
Targets    : MOBs, Items, Rideables
Parameters : [ALL PRICE]/[AREA/ROOM]=[PRICE]/[PARAM]=[VALUE]; ... ;
Example    : 1.5
Example    : Midgaard#3001=1.5; Smurfville=2.0; 70 ; AREAONLY=true
Example    : Midgaard#3032; 100 ; INDOOROK=false; MAXRANGE=100
Description:
This behavior makes the mob a carrier of players to places.  The mob will charge for his
services if you specify a price in the parameters, or he will do it for free if you don't,
or if the last price specified was 0.  The parameters can include a comma delimited set of
room IDs, area names, or even short title descriptions for quickly entering rooms within
short range of the mob.

The parameters may also include certain other variables as part of the parameter list.
These include AREAONLY = true or false, to specify whether the taxi knows anything about
places outside his area.  MAXRANGE=number for the maximum number of rooms away from the taxi
 that is known.  GREETING=message will give a special taxi greeting message for all players
who enter the room its in. ENTERMSG will give a message to players after they mount the
taxi.  TALKERNAME=name will change the apparent name of the speaker, allowing you to turn a
mounted mob into a "driver" if you wish. PERROOM=number will set a per-room price for the
distance from the current room to the one sought. INDOOROK=true will allow the taxi to
traverse indoor rooms if convenient. NOWATER=true to prevent trails over water. NOAIR=true,
to prevent trails through the air. NOLOCKS=true to prevent trails through locked doors.
NOHOMES=true to prevent trails through private homes. NOCLIMB to prevent trails through
climbable exits. NOCRAWL to prevent trails through crawlable exits.
```

```text
Behavior   : TidalRoom
Targets    : Rooms
Parameters : (SPAN=[HOURS]) (TITLE=) (DESC=) (FLOODMSG=) (DEEP) (WASH=[WEIGHT])
Example    : SPAN=1 DESC="The sea fills the cove." WASH=2 DEEP
Description:
CoffeeSUD: a shore room the tide floods, made from RoomStates: at high tide (SPAN hours
either side) it is a swimming room with its own TITLE and DESC, and FLOODMSG for those who
come in; with DEEP its air is water at the spring tides; WASH washes away the loose things
there that weigh up to that much as the water comes.  At the ebb it is itself again.
ROOMSTATE() says ebb, flooded or deep.
```

<a id="behavior-transportline"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_TRANSPORTLINE

Source: [arc_travel.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_travel.ini), line 39.

```text
Behavior: TransportLine
Targets: Navigable vessels, rideables, mounted MOB drivers
Parameters: STOPS="[room IDs or port names separated by semicolons]" WAIT=[ticks]
DEPART=[game hours, comma separated] ROUND=LOOP|BACK FARE=[price] FARES="[stop:price,...]"
PARTY=LEADER|EACH PETS=[price] CARGO=[price per 100 lbs] PASSENGERONLY=true SIGN="[item
name]" BOARDCALL="[text]" DEPARTMSG="[text]" ARRIVEMSG="[text]"
Routes between stops with the ordinary movement system. DEPART replaces WAIT with calendar
departure hours. BACK reverses at endpoints; LOOP cycles. Messages substitute $stop and
$next. SIGN publishes the timetable at stops; TIMETABLE also shows it. Progress, direction,
departure and arrival count are saved.
Generated ticket and crew-only helm properties are temporary; explicit authored properties
take priority. PARTY=LEADER pays for the group, EACH uses individual fares. WAIT UNTIL
ARRIVAL stops at a line arrival.
```

<a id="behavior-veryaggressive"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_VERYAGGRESSIVE

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 3420.

```text
Behavior   : VeryAggressive
Targets    : MOBs
Parameters : aggression flags (message=[msg]) aggression masks
Example    : -race +elf message="die! You!"
Example    : -race +elf
Example    : mobkill misbehave -race +elf
Description:
Makes the mob attack any player mob it can detect in the same room, from the moment the new
mob enters.  In addition, this behavior will detect any mobs in adjacent rooms, and move to
attack those as well, but only if those players meet all the other criteria, and are within
16 levels of the mob. Mobs will not be aggressive towards Archons and builders with the
CMDMOBS security flag. Horribly wounded mobs are not aggressive. If no other parameters are
given, the mob will attack anyone within 8 levels. Valid aggressive masks include:
message=[msg] something for the mob to say whenever he's fixing to attack
delay=x (makes the mob delay x ticks before looking for a victim)
mobkill (makes this behavior attack mobs as well as players)
nogang (makes this behavior pass over players already in combat)
misbehave (makes this mob attack even when wounded or a follower)
BRIBE=[AMOUNT],[TICKS OF PEACE],[TICKS TO PAY] - this is a comma-delimited
BRIBEPAYMSG=x, BRIBEPAIDMSG=x, (see also ahelp on AGGRESSIVE BRIBE)
See AHELP ZAPPERMASK, where allowed is attacked, and disallowed is spared.
```

<a id="behavior-wavespawner"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_WAVESPAWNER

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 3445.

```text
Behavior   : WaveSpawner
Targets    : Rooms
Parameters : WAVE1="[WAVE]" WAVE2="[WAVE]"... (NEXT=CLEAR/TICKS=[N]) (START=ENTER/CALL)
(LOCKEXITS=true) (ONWIN=[FUNCTION]/UNLOCK) (ONLOSE=RESET/SPARRING(:[ROOM ID]))
(REWARD="[ITEM]") (RESETAFTER=[N])
Example    : WAVE1="catalog:goblin*3" WAVE2="goblin*2+goblin archer*2"
WAVE3="encounter:goblin_boss" LOCKEXITS=true REWARD="a laurel" ONLOSE=SPARRING:Arena#2
Description:
CoffeeSUD: an arena of waves.  Each wave is name*dice joined with + (from the catalog,
catalog: being optional, or a mob class), or encounter:[TABLE], a roll of an encounter table
 (AHELP ENCOUNTER).  START=ENTER (the default) starts when the party walks in, CALL when a
script runs MPWAVE START.  The next wave comes when the last is dead (NEXT=CLEAR) or after N
 ticks (NEXT=TICKS=N).  LOCKEXITS keeps the party in until it is done.  When the last wave
is dead, the winner gets REWARD, ONWIN's FUNCTION_PROG of the room's scripts runs ($n the
winner), and after RESETAFTER ticks it may start again.  If the party leaves or falls, what
is left of the wave leaves; ONLOSE=SPARRING puts Prop_SparringRoom on the room while it
runs, so a defeat is not death (the room ID is where the loser wakes).  WAVE_PROG [N],
ARENAWIN_PROG and ARENALOSE_PROG run on the room's scripts and its NPCs' (an arena
master's), and the wave is kept in a saved game.
```

<a id="behavior-when"></a>

## BEHAVIOR_WHEN

Source: [arc_behaviors.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_behaviors.ini), line 9.

```text
Behavior   : (any)
Targets    : MOBs, Items, Rooms, Areas, Exits
Parameters : (WHEN="[ZAPPER MASK]") (TOD=[DAWN,DAY,DUSK,NIGHT]) (HOURS=[FROM]-[TO])
Example    : MobileAggressive TOD=NIGHT -NPC
Example    : Aggressive WHEN="+WEATHER -THUNDERSTORM"
Example    : Emoter HOURS=22-4 min=5 max=10 chance=50;howls at the moon.
Description:
CoffeeSUD: these parameters go with any behaviour, beside its own.  WHEN is a zapper mask
tested on the behaviour's host (the mob, item, room, area or exit), such as +HOUR, +SEASON
or +WEATHER; TOD is a time of day, or several with commas; HOURS is a range of hours on the
host's clock, which runs round midnight when the first is past the second.  While the
condition fails, the behaviour neither acts nor reacts.  For the opposite case, give the
host a second copy with the opposite condition: a werewolf with MobileAggressive TOD=NIGHT
and Mobile TOD=DAY.  STAT BEHAVIORS says whether each is on now.  Scripts (Scriptable) do
not take them.
```

<a id="blacksmithing"></a>

## BLACKSMITHING

Source: [common_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/common_help.ini), line 225.

```text
<ABILITY>Usage    : BLACKSMITH (LIST/LEARN/INFO) (BUNDLE [NUM]) [ITEM TYPE]
Usage    :   ... (FROM [RESOURCE NAME])
Example  : blacksmith pot
:        : blacksmith bundle 100 iron
:        : blacksmith list
:        : blacksmith list pot
:        : blacksmith list 5-10
:        : blacksmith list all
:        : blacksmith learn pot
This skill allows a player to craft metal items, such as pots and pans.  The extent of the
items which can be crafted expands as the player goes up in level.  To begin smithing, the
player must be in a room with an open fire burning, and must have placed the metal he or she
 wishes to make the item from on the ground. The player may also learn how to smith an item
he or she has found, so long as he or she has a blank recipe page or a recipe book with
blank pages in his or her inventory. The raw metal for blacksmithing can be obtained using
the Mining skill, and better metals through the Smelting skill.
```

Source: [common_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/common_help.ini), line 247.

```text
<ABILITY>Usage    : BOATWRIGHT (LIST/INFO/MEND/SCAN) [ITEM NAME]
Usage    :   ... (FROM [RESOURCE NAME])

:        : boatwright list 5-10
:        : boatwright list all
:        : boatwright mend canoe
:        : boatwright scan
:        : boatwright scan bob
:        : boatwright learn boat
This skill allows a player to craft wooden boats.  The extent of the items which can be
crafted expands as the player goes up in level.  This command also allows the player to
repair any damaged small wooden boats.  To begin carving a new item, the player must have
placed the wood he or she wishes to make the item from on the ground. Items crafted with
balsa can be done with half the required wood listed, while items crafted with ironwood will
 require twice the required wood listed. The raw wood for building is found using the
Chopping skill.
```

<a id="buildermode"></a>

## BUILDERMODE

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 2223.

Help alias for **BUILDING**.

```text
Topic    : BUILDING
Short(s) : BUILDERMODE
The creator handbook is docs/creator/README.md in the developer checkout: workflows, a
cookbook, runnable examples and current tool references.
Building in CoffeeSUD, with BUILDER=1.  The world lives in its folder (WORLDDIR, world/ by
default): areas/*.cmare, quests/*.quest, the catalog, custom objects, templates, clans and
the world's own resources/.  The database is a cache of those files; SAVE writes the files
from it, and so does QUIT.

1. A mob or item you CREATE is only in the room until SAVE ROOM, which saves each mob into
its own start room; this is the first trap.  LIST UNSAVED lists the rooms with mobs or items
 not saved, SAVE CHANGED saves them all, QUIT asks, and %U in a prompt counts them.  MODIFY
ROOM and the room's exits are saved as you make them.
2. UNDO puts back what the last building commands changed (UNDO LIST).  SAVE keeps a copy of
 each world file it writes over in world/.backup/ (WORLD BACKUPS, WORLD RESTOREFILE).
3. A world file edited outside the game while it runs is not written over: WORLD STATUS
lists such files, WORLD DIFF shows one against the game's, WORLD RELOAD loads it (or
CHANGED, all of them; DEVWATCH ON does it as they change), and SAVE FORCE writes the game's
over it.
4. To make: CREATE ROOM, WORLD DIG and WORLD PATH for rooms, COPY, the catalog and templates
 for things, GMODIFY and MODIFY UPDATE: (MQL) for many at once, IMPORT and GENERATE for
whole areas (GENERATE ... SANDBOX to try one out first), RUNFILE for a file of commands and
JRUN with its builder object for scripts.  EDIT SCRIPT and EDIT DESC open the line editor.
5. To look: WORLD MAP, WORLD CHECK (and sud.sh CHECK=1), SCRIPTCHECK, PROPCHECK, QUESTCHECK,
 ORGCHECK, VALIDATE RECIPES, LIST CONTENTS, LIST LINKAGES, WORLD PROBLEMS for files that did
 not load whole, DEVLOG and SCRIPTTRACE for what runs, PAUSE AREA to freeze one.  PLAYTEST
plays as a player, BUILD runs one builder command meanwhile.
6. Not in the world folder: the characters (the database's), the game's own resources/
unless a world copy is made (builder mode writes changes to the world's copy), and
coffeemud.ini; ERRMSGS=BOTH and JSCRIPTS=2 there help while building.
```

<a id="calendar"></a>

## CALENDAR

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 2595.

```text
CoffeeSUD: MODIFY AREA CALENDAR [KEY=VALUE ...] gives an area, and its child areas, a
calendar of its own, kept in the area's data (so in its .cmare), in place of the global
clock's: HOURS= (hours in a day), DAYS= (days in a month), MONTHS="Leafwake,Bloomtide" (the
months' names), WEEK="..." (the weekdays'), YEARS="year #" (the years'), DAWNHR=, DAYHR=,
DUSKHR=, NIGHTHR= (the hours each begins), and START=YEAR/MONTH/DAY/HOUR, where a new game
starts its clock (months and days count from 1; the hour left out is dawn).  What it leaves
out comes from the parent area's clock, else the global one.  A saved game goes on from its
own date. MODIFY AREA CALENDAR alone shows it, NONE takes it away; the area editor's
calendar screen writes it too. STARTDATE=YEAR/MONTH/DAY/HOUR in coffeemud.ini (or world.ini)
 is the global clock's START. Seasons, day length and moons: SEASONS="the
Burn:SUMMER:1-2,the Rains:SPRING:Flood-Silt" names each season, the built-in season it
counts as for the weather, VARIES and the like, and its months (numbers from 1, or the
months' names); SEASONOFFSET=[MONTHS] is the area's own, its seasons that many months on, on
 its parent's clock (a southern land); DAYLIGHT="WINTER:2-4,the Burn:0-5" gives a season's
dawn and night hours (or all four, DAWN-DAY-DUSK-NIGHT); MOONS="Selune:24,Ember:9:3" names
each moon, its cycle in days and its offset in days, the first being the moon the tides and
ISMOON(FULL) follow.  ISSEASON(the Burn), ISMOON(Ember full), -SEASON "+the Burn", <the
Burn>...</the Burn> in VARIES text and TIME know them.
Example    : MODIFY AREA CALENDAR HOURS=10 DAYS=30
MONTHS="Leafwake,Bloomtide,Highsun,Frostfall" DAWNHR=0 DAYHR=1 DUSKHR=8 NIGHTHR=9
START=812/2/3
```

<a id="carpentry"></a>

## CARPENTRY

Source: [common_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/common_help.ini), line 407.

```text
<ABILITY>Usage    : CARVE (LIST/INFO/MEND/REFIT/SCAN/LEARN) (BUNDLE [NUM]) [ITEM TYPE]
Usage    :   ... (FROM [RESOURCE NAME])
Example  : carve small table
:        : carve bundle 100 maple
:        : carve list
:        : carve list table
:        : carve list 5-10
:        : carve list all
:        : carve mend club
:        : carve refit club
:        : carve scan
:        : carve scan bob
:        : carve learn club
This skill allows a player to craft wooden items, such as chairs and wooden shields.  The
extent of the items which can be crafted expands as the player goes up in level.  This
command also allows the player to repair any damaged wooden weapons or armor, get info on a
list item, refit any armor which may be the wrong size, or learn how to carve a found item,
provided a blank recipe page, or recipe book with blank pages is in his or her inventory. To
 begin carving a new item, the player must have placed the wood he or she wishes to make the
 item from on the ground.  The player may also scan the room or other players for equipment
that may be mended by this skill, using the scan parameter. Items crafted with balsa can be
done with half the required wood listed, while items crafted with ironwood will require
twice the required wood listed. The raw wood for carpentry can be obtained using the

 of the crafted item, and some material types require smaller amounts to make the same
items.
```

<a id="catalog"></a>

## CATALOG

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 113.

```text
Command  : CATALOG
Usage    : CATALOG LIST (MOBS/ITEMS/CATEGORIES/) [NAME MASK]
Usage    : CATALOG (DELETE) [ITEM/MOB NAME]
Usage    : CATALOG (ROOM/AREA/WORLD) (MOBS/ITEMS/)
Usage    : CATALOG EDIT [ITEM NAME]
Usage    : CATALOG CATEGORY [CATEGORY NAME]
Usage    : CATALOG SCAN/DBSCAN (ROOM/AREA/WORLD) (MOBS/ITEMS/)
Usage    : CATALOG OVERLOOK/DBOVERLOOK (ROOM/AREA/WORLD) (MOBS/ITEMS/)
Example  : catalog list
Example  : catalog list mobs the st
Example  : catalog list mob categories
Example  : catalog the waiter
Example  : catalog delete the waiter
Example  : catalog edit the sword
Example  : catalog room mobs
Example  : catalog scan area
Example  : catalog dboverlook area mobs
Short(s) :
This command is used to manage your muds global catalog of generic mobs and/or items. The
catalog is a place where you can store templates of mobs and items for reuse, or for quick
global modification and analysis.  Mobs and items in your catalog can be changed globally
simply by creating and then changing any instance of one of them.  You can create new
instances of a cataloged object simply by entering CREATE <cataloged object name>. Your
catalog is keyed by name, so once the name of a cataloged item or mob is set, it should not
be changed.

Cataloged items can be placed into categories by issueing the catalog category command
before adding or modifying catalog entries.  Mobs and items so cataloged must still have a
unique global name, but flagging them this way can make listing them must easier.

You may review the objects in your catalog using the catalog list command. You can also
check the catalog synchronicity of the objects in your live rooms with scan, or your saved
rooms with dbscan.  You can check for uncataloged objects in live rooms with the overlook
parameter, or in your saved rooms with dboverlook.

You may delete an object from your catalog to stop using it as a global template. Deleting
an object from the catalog only detaches instances of a cataloged object from all others,
but does not destroy any actual instances.

The catalog is also used to manage a global random item-drop table.  Items can be set to
randomly appear in the inventories of selected mobs when those mobs are brought to life, or
at the moment of their death. Use CATALOG EDIT <item name> to change drop settings.

CoffeeSUD: an item may also be found in containers (C)ontainer: when a matching container is
 first opened, on a timer, or both), have several rules sharing its cap, and be unique at a
time, once ever, or once for a while; every copy in the game counts, those from a save too.
See AHELP UNIQUES.
```

```text
For NPCs that talk (MudChat).  CHATTEST shows what the NPC would make of what you would say,
 without anyone speaking: its base and active chat groups, anything that would stop it
answering (it cannot hear or see you, it answered you last, another NPC spoke, three or more
 players are here), each entry the words lead to and whether it matches, and the replies of
the first that does, with their weights and their variables filled in ($n is the NPC's own
name).  CHATLINT checks a chat file as the parser reads it: patterns that do not parse,
malformed ${} lines, @ links to groups not defined above them, replies with no pattern,
patterns with no replies, files that cannot be read and lines the parser skips, each with
its line number.  CHAT RELOAD reads a chat file again (or all of them) for every NPC that
talks from it; in builder mode an edited chat file is read again by itself.
```

## CHECKTEXT

Help alias for **PREVIEW**.

```text
Command  : PREVIEW
Usage    : PREVIEW (ROOM) ([CONDITION]...)
Usage    : CHECKTEXT (ROOM/AREA/WORLD)
Example  : preview night winter snow
Example  : preview from north visited
Example  : preview dusk as Bob var BRIDGE=1
Example  : checktext area
Short(s) : CHECKTEXT
PREVIEW shows this room's title and description as they read under the conditions given, the
 rest as they are, and changes nothing: a time of day (DAY, NIGHT, DAWN, DUSK), a season
(SPRING, SUMMER, FALL, WINTER), a weather (RAIN, SNOW, CLEAR, FOG, THUNDERSTORM, BLIZZARD,
WINDY, CLOUDY...), FROM a direction or FROM UNKNOWN, VISITED or FIRSTVISIT, AS a character
(for MASK parts and what they are doing) and VAR NAME=VALUE (a script variable of the
reader, put back after).  Only rooms' texts vary (<VARIES>).  CHECKTEXT lists what in rooms'
 titles and descriptions would print as text instead of varying: variation tags in a text
that does not start with <VARIES>, tags that are none (<nigth>), tags in small letters
(their end is found only in capitals), tags opened and not closed or closed and not opened,
a MASK whose mask has a > in it (write &gt;), and a colour code left open at the end.
<FROMUNKNOWN> is the same as <FROMUNKOWN>, as the code long spelled it.
```

```text
This skill allows a player to craft clan items.  The clan items from this skill require that
 the clan have a certain amount of experience in order to make the item.  For this reason,
only clan members who have the rank of Enchanter (or the equivalent privileges), may use
this skill even if they have the skill.  The majority of items crafted using this skill
serve the CONQUEST system, and only work on mobs in conquered areas.  See the help on
CONQUEST for more information on how to use the items. The extent of the items which can be
crafted expands as the player goes up in level.  To begin crafting, the player must have
placed the materials he or she wishes to make the item from on the ground.   Using better
materials will increase both the strength and the required level of the crafted item, and
some material types require smaller amounts to make the same items.
```

<a id="compose"></a>

## COMPOSE

Source: [help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/help.ini), line 3198.

```text
Ability : Ability composition (Skill_Compose)
Usage   : COMPOSE (LIST)
Usage   : COMPOSE LEARN/SHOW/FORGET [skill ID]
Usage   : COMPOSE LINK/UNLINK [skill ID] [support ID]
Usage   : COMPOSE CAST [skill ID] [target]
Requires the optional abilities.composition module and the learned Skill_Compose ability.
Installing the module does not grant it. LEARN selects an eligible authored skill version;
LINK adds a compatible support. SHOW explains the compiled values and each modifier's
source. UNLINK removes one support. FORGET removes a chosen skill; neither it nor LEARN
resets cooldowns.
Up to four chosen skills and three supports per skill are supported; the creator may lower
limits. Each character keeps separate choices. Existing skills retain their selected
versions across save/restore and content upgrades. LEARN explicitly adopts the latest
version and clears supports. A missing or changed version suspends its binding until
repaired or removed.
The world controls available skills, prerequisites, support compatibility, costs, timing,
chain limits and secondary effects. Existing native abilities keep their ordinary behavior.
See AHELP WORLD_COMPOSITIONS for creator tools.
```

<a id="craftquality"></a>

## CRAFTQUALITY

Source: [arc_misc.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_misc.ini), line 1281.

```text
CoffeeSUD: quality tiers for what players craft, in resources/skills/craftquality.txt (a
world's own copy, world/resources/skills/craftquality.txt, first).  The shipped file has its
 tiers in comments, so nothing rolls until a world gives some.  One tier a line, the fields
between tabs: NAME, CHANCE, VALUE, ARMOR, DAMAGE, USES, LEVEL, EFFECTS.  NAME is the word
put in the item's name.  CHANCE is a percent, as a formula: @x1 is the crafter's level less
the item's, @x2 their proficiency in the skill, @x3 the QUALITY of the best workstation
helping them (AHELP PROP_WORKSTATION); a formula is worked left to right, so put brackets
round each part.  VALUE, ARMOR, DAMAGE and USES multiply the item's value, armour (armour
only), damage (weapons only) and uses; LEVEL is added to its level; EFFECTS are put on it,
as Prop_HaveResister(fire 10);Prop_WearAdjuster(dex+1).  When a player's craft succeeds the
tiers are tried from the first, and the first that rolls under its chance is the item's; if
none does, it is plain.  A data skill with QUALITY false (AHELP GENCRAFTSKILL), or a recipe
with NOQUALITY=1 (AHELP RECIPEKEYS), rolls none.  Example line, with tabs where the commas
are: masterwork, (@x2/25)+(@x1/4)+(@x3*3), 1.5, 1.1, 1.1, 1.2, 3
```
