<a id="creationsteps"></a>

## CREATIONSTEPS

Source: [arc_misc.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_misc.ini), line 1169.

```text
CoffeeSUD: the steps of character creation and the world's own questions, in
world/creation.ini.  STEPS=RACE,GENDER,STATS,CLASS,ORIGIN,KIT,TRAITS,FACTIONS,DEITY is the
default.  RACE, GENDER, STATS, CLASS, FACTIONS and DEITY keep that order (each needs the one
 before; a STEPS line with them otherwise is logged); ORIGIN, KIT, TRAITS (AHELP PERKSINI)
and questions go wherever STEPS puts them.  A step STEPS leaves out is not asked: race,
gender, stats and class are then picked at random (as DISABLE=CHARCRRACE and the like do),
the others skipped.  RACE=RANDOM (SKIP, ASK), GENDER=..., FACTIONS=RANDOM, ORIGIN=RANDOM,
KIT=RANDOM: a step listed but not asked.  REVIEW is for P27.  A question is a [NAME]
section: PROMPT (the question), INTRO (a text file, in world/ or resources/), SHOWIF (a
zapper mask; others are not asked), MODE=RANDOM, and CHOICE lines, each NAME="..."
HELP="..." MASK="..." EFFECTS="..." (achievement rewards, as 1 CHARISMA 50 XP) FACTION="ID
amount" START="room ID" SCRIPT="ONCE_PROG 100;...;~" (or LOAD=file); quote values with
spaces.  The answer is the tattoo CHARCR_[NAME]_[CHOICE] (spaces as _), for masks and
scripts; its EFFECTS, FACTION, START and SCRIPT (run in the start room) come at the end of
creation, with the origin's and the kits'.  Example: [UPBRINGING] PROMPT=Where were you
raised?, CHOICE=NAME="Noble" EFFECTS="1 CHARISMA" START="Manor#1", CHOICE=NAME="Street
urchin" EFFECTS="25 Thief_Swipe" START="Docks#3"; HASTATTOO(CHARCR_UPBRINGING_STREET_URCHIN)
 in the cooper's script.  REVIEW in STEPS (it is always last) shows the character before
creation ends: race, class, stats, standing, deity, origin, kits, answers and start room;
BACK [step] puts the character back as it was when that step began and asks it and the steps
 after it again (BACK CLASS keeps the stats), and DONE ends creation.  At the profile menu,
NEW [name] QUICK takes every step at random with no review, and NEW [name] QUICK [template]
makes that ready-made character (AHELP PLAYERTEMPLATES).
```

<a id="currency-file"></a>

## CURRENCY_FILE

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 2577.

```text
CoffeeSUD: a world's currencies, in world/resources/currencies.ini (the stock
resources/currencies.ini is read when the world has none).  Each line CODE=[DEFINITION]
makes a currency, as an area's CURRENCY would: denominations with semicolons between, each
its value in the lowest coin, its name with (s) for the plural, and its short form in
brackets, as CROWN=1 copper penny(s) (cp);12 silver shilling(s) (ss);240 gold crown(s) (gc);
 notrade first makes coins no shop takes.  Areas then name it by its code alone (MODIFY
AREA, CURRENCY CROWN), and an area that defines the code again, differently, keeps the
file's (the log says so).  DEFAULT=CROWN is the currency of every area with none of its own,
 in place of the gold coins and Archon notes; GOLD, COPPER, CREDIT, DOLLAR and VICTORY are
built in.  coffeemud.ini or world.ini may set CURRENCY_[CODE]=[DEFINITION] and
DEFAULTCURRENCY=[CODE] as well.

A denomination may end in braces, in any currency definition (an area's too): 12 silver
shilling(s) (ss) {MATERIAL=SILVER WEIGHT=0.01 DESC="A thin disc stamped with the crowned
stag."}. MATERIAL is what its coins are made of (else the first material word of the name;
note, bill and dollar are paper), WEIGHT what one coin weighs (else a hundred to the pound),
 DESC their look, shown before the "Equal to" line.
```

<a id="devlog"></a>

## DEVLOG

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 1760.

```text
Command  : DEVLOG
Usage    : DEVLOG ON (ERROR/WARN/INFO/DEBUG) (MODULE [MASK])
Usage    : DEVLOG OFF
Usage    : DEVLOG LAST ([NUMBER]) (ERROR/WARN/INFO/DEBUG) (MODULE [MASK])
Usage    : DEVLOG CLEAR
Usage    : DEVLOG WINDOW (ERROR/WARN/INFO/DEBUG) (MODULE [MASK])
Usage    : DEVLOG WINDOW OFF
Example  : devlog on warn module Scripting,Quest*
Example  : devlog last 30 error
Short(s) :
In builder mode or a DEV=1 game, tells you each line the engine logs as it is logged,
whatever mud.log is set to keep: script errors, JavaScript errors, MPLOG, MPDEBUG and
debug() lines (told you whatever you watch), quest failures, what the world files' loader
skipped.  ON takes the level (ERROR, WARN, the default, INFO or DEBUG, each with those above
 it) and a mask of modules (names separated by commas, * for any letters).  Each line comes
as one coloured line with its level and module; a line repeated is told once, and how many
more times when something else comes.  LAST replays the last lines kept (500), the repeats
counted, by level (DEBUG, all, by default) and module; CLEAR forgets them.  In builder mode
the setting is kept beside the database for the next time; the DEVLOG= key in coffeemud.ini
(DEVLOG=WARN Scripting,Quest*) gives it otherwise. WINDOW opens a separate display-only log
with its own filters and recent history; WINDOW OFF closes it. Without a display, ON and
LAST show the log in this terminal.
```

<a id="devwatch"></a>

## DEVWATCH

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 2152.

Help alias for **WORLD**.

```text
Command  : WORLD
Usage    : WORLD (LIST)
Usage    : WORLD SET [KEY]=[VALUE]
Usage    : WORLD PROBLEMS
Usage    : WORLD MODULES ([ID])/CHECK/PLAN/RELOAD/ADOPT/CONFIGURE/STATE
Usage    : WORLD TEST ([FILE.play/FILE.test/FILE.js])
Usage    : WORLD CHECK (AREA ([NAME])) (LOG) (ONLY=[PART],[PART]...)
Usage    : WORLD DEV (([AREA]) ON/OFF)
Usage    : WORLD STATUS
Usage    : WORLD DIFF [FILE]
Usage    : WORLD RELOAD ([AREA]) [NAME] (FORCE)
Usage    : WORLD RELOAD SCRIPT [FILE]/ALL (RESET)
Usage    : WORLD RELOAD QUEST [NAME]/QUESTS/CATALOG/ASSETS/CHANGED
Usage    : WORLD BACKUPS ([FILE])
Usage    : WORLD RESTOREFILE [FILE] ([TIME])
Usage    : WORLD DIG ON/OFF (TYPE=[LOCALE/TEMPLATE]) (LINK=TWO-WAY/ONE-WAY)
Usage    : WORLD PATH [DIRECTIONS] (TYPE=..) (NAME="..") (DESC="..") (LINK=..)
Usage    : WORLD MAP (RADIUS [N]) (AREA) (IDS) (FLAGS) (HTML=[FILE])
Example  : world
Example  : world check only=exits,keys
Example  : world diff castle
Example  : world reload castle
Example  : world path e,e,n,ne type=forestpath name="A forest trail"
Example  : world map area ids flags
Example  : world reload script progs/innkeeper.script reset
Example  : world set START=Emberfall#0
Example  : world set HOURSINDAY=12
Short(s) : LIST WORLDINI
WORLD lists the world settings: the keys a world may set in world.ini in its folder, each
with its value in effect and where that came from (coffeemud.ini, world.ini or the command
line).  In builder mode, WORLD SET KEY=VALUE changes the key's line in world.ini, or adds
one, and a blank value takes it out; it takes effect the next time the game starts.  Keys
that are not world settings, such as the database's, stay in coffeemud.ini.  WORLD PROBLEMS
lists what did not load from the world files: an object of an unknown class (a misspelled
ability, say) is skipped, and its file loaded only in part, so builder mode does not write
that file until it is fixed (and the world loaded again from it), or SAVE FORCE writes it as
 the world has it.  WORLD CHECK, in builder mode or a DEV=1 game, checks the whole world (or
 one area) and lists errors, then warnings, each with its part and room: EXITS (exits to
nowhere, doors with no way back), REACH (start rooms that do not exist, rooms nothing leads
to from them, by area), KEYS (locked doors and containers whose key is nowhere: in rooms,
carried, in shops or the catalog), TEXT (the new room's description, rooms, generic mobs and
 items with their class's text), SHOPS (shopkeepers with nothing to sell), DATA (WORLD
PROBLEMS), SCRIPTS (SCRIPTCHECK), PROPS (PROPCHECK), JS (the world's JavaScript classes),
VOCAB (languages, glossary, lists and help), LORE (entries/files), TEMPLATES (presentation
text/options), ROUTES (travel and route references) and IDS (stable author identities);
ONLY= picks parts, LOG writes the report to the log too.  sud.sh CHECK=1 loads the world as
a new game would, on a scratch copy, runs it with no player, prints it and exits 1 if it
found errors: for a script or a commit hook.  WORLD DEV lists the dev areas: those in
world/dev, for building and testing only, which builder mode and DEV=1 games load and a
normal game never does (DEVSTART= in coffeemud.ini can start new characters in one, such as
a hub with portals and test gear).  In builder mode, WORLD DEV [AREA] ON makes an area one
(SAVE writes it to world/dev) and OFF a shipped one again; WORLD CHECK warns of an exit from
 a shipped area into a dev area, which leads nowhere in a normal game.  In builder mode,
SAVE does not write over or delete a world file changed outside the game (edited, added or
deleted since the game loaded or last wrote it): what it would write goes beside it, as
NAME.builder, and SAVE FORCE writes over it.  WORLD STATUS lists the files changed outside
the game, and what SAVE would write, delete and leave; WORLD DIFF [FILE] shows a file
(castle, areas/castle.cmare, quests/hunt.quest) against what SAVE would write, - for its
lines on disk and + for SAVE's.  WORLD RELOAD loads world files again into the running game:
 an area (by its name or its file's), whose players and their followers wait outside it and
come back, and whose exits from other areas are linked again (refused while rooms of it have
 unsaved mobs or items, as LIST UNSAVED lists them, unless FORCE); SCRIPT, the scripts that
name a file (or ALL), their triggers reset with RESET; QUEST, a quest stopped, read again
from its file in world/quests and started again at its step; QUESTS, each of them; CATALOG,
the catalog's entries from its file; CHANGED, each file WORLD STATUS lists as changed
outside the game.  In a normal game it saves the game as world-reload and restores it, which
 builds the world from its files again.  DEVWATCH ON ([SECONDS]) looks at the world files
and resources' scripts every few seconds and runs the reload that matches what changed, each
 noted in DEVLOG; DEVWATCH OFF stops it.  Before SAVE writes over or deletes a world file it
 keeps a copy in world/.backup/ (the last BACKUPS= in coffeemud.ini of each, 5 if not set):
WORLD BACKUPS lists the files with backups, WORLD BACKUPS FILE the times of one's, and WORLD
 RESTOREFILE FILE (TIME) puts the newest (or that one) back, changed outside the game, for
WORLD RELOAD to load.  WORLD DIG ON makes a room, as CREATE ROOM does (of the room's own
kind, or TYPE=, a locale or a builder template), wherever you walk and there is no exit, and
 goes into it, linked back unless LINK=ONE-WAY; WORLD DIG OFF stops it.  WORLD PATH lays out
 a chain of rooms, one for each direction, following the exits there already, each with
NAME= and DESC= if given, and leaves you where you are.  Rooms made so are saved and tagged
TODO, which WORLD CHECK lists until EDIT DESC gives them their own text.  WORLD MAP draws
the rooms around you (5 steps out, or RADIUS N) or the whole area (AREA), north up, laid out
 by walking their exits from your room (*); a room above or below, or where another is, is
listed instead.  IDS numbers the rooms and lists them; FLAGS marks what to look at: > < v ^
an exit that does not lead back, + a locked door, @ an exit to another area, s a room with
scripts, and lists the rooms of the area nothing leads to from here.  HTML=FILE writes the
area's map to world/maps/FILE.html, each room with its exits as links.
```

<a id="difficulty"></a>

## DIFFICULTY

Source: [help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/help.ini), line 1082.

```text
Command : DIFFICULTY
Usage   : DIFFICULTY ([NAME])
Example : difficulty
Example : difficulty story
Short(s):
Says how hard the game is, and with a name changes it (not in the middle of a fight).
STORY: enemies deal 60% of their damage and have 80% of their hit points, and your side
deals 125%.  EASY: enemies deal 80% and have 90%, and your side deals 110%.  NORMAL: as the
game was made.  HARD: enemies deal 130% and have 120%, and you gain 110% of the experience.
  Your side is your characters and those who follow them.  The world may set the numbers
differently, or offer more; DIFFICULTY lists them.  The game remembers it in your saves.
```

<a id="edit"></a>

## EDIT

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 2106.

```text
Command  : EDIT
Usage    : EDIT SCRIPT [TARGET] ([NUMBER])
Usage    : EDIT DESC [TARGET]
Example  : edit script the innkeeper
Example  : edit script here 2
Example  : edit desc the old sword
Short(s) : EXTRACT
In builder mode or with CMDMOBS, CMDITEMS or CMDROOMS: EDIT SCRIPT opens a thing's script
(the first, or the number given: its Scriptable behaviours', then its scripts) in the line
editor, a statement to a line.  The editor's menu lists (L), edits (E), inserts (I) and
deletes (D) lines, adds them (A), replaces text (R), and saves (S) or quits (Q).  On save
the script is checked as SCRIPTCHECK does: edit it again, keep it, or cancel.  A script that
 is only LOAD=file opens the file, which every LOAD= of it shares, and is read again.  EDIT
DESC opens the description.  The target is a mob or item here or carried, HERE, AREA, or
name@room.  A room or area is saved; SAVE ROOM keeps a mob or item.  EXTRACT SCRIPT [TARGET]
 ([NUMBER]) ([FILE]) moves an inline script to resources/progs/NAME.script (the world's own
copy, in builder mode), a statement to a line, and puts LOAD= of it in its place, for others
 to share.  MODIFY's script fields (GenAbility and GenTrap's Scriptable Parm, GenCommand's
Script), a Scriptable behaviour added, a quest's script and a description of more than one
line open the same editor, and + at a description's prompt opens it for any.  EDITOR=WINDOW
in coffeemud.ini edits in a window instead, and EDITOR=EXTERNAL in the program
EDITORCOMMAND= names (or $VISUAL or $EDITOR), on a temporary file.
```

<a id="encounter"></a>

## ENCOUNTER

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 1997.

```text
Command  : ENCOUNTER
Usage    : ENCOUNTER LIST | SHOW [TABLE] | ADD [TABLE] [ENTRY] | DEL [TABLE] [N] | ROLL
[TABLE] | CHECK ([TABLE]/ALL) | RESET [TABLE]
Example  : encounter add darkwood MOBS "grey wolf*2d3" LEADER="dire wolf" WEIGHT=4
MASK="-HOUR +20 +21 +22" AMBUSH
Example  : encounter roll darkwood
Short(s) :
In builder mode, a DEV=1 game or with CMDMOBS: the encounter tables of world/encounters,
which RandomEncounters, MPMLOAD ENCOUNTER and the quests' LOAD ENCOUNTER roll.  A table is a
 text file, one entry a line (# for a comment): its kind, what, and options.  MOBS
"name*dice,name*dice" brings mobs from the catalog (or a class), as many as the dice say
(2d3, 1d4+1, 3, 2-5), with LEADER="name" one more that the others follow; MERCHANT "name"
the same, for a pedlar; ITEM "name*dice" leaves things in the room; EMOTE "text" is shown to
 the room; TRAP [TRAP ID] is set off on the one who came in; FUNC [FUNCTION] runs a
FUNCTION_PROG of what rolled the table (the area's or room's scripts), $n the one who came
in.  Options: WEIGHT=N (1); MASK="[ZAPPER MASK]" on the one who came in (-HOUR, -SEASON,
-LEVEL, +GROUPSIZE...); LEVEL=LO-HI the party's highest level (8- for 8 and up, -5 for up to
 5); ONCE (once a game); COOLDOWN=N (N encounters of the table before it comes again);
FROM=HERE (the default), HIDDEN (hidden in the room) or ADJACENT (they walk in from next
door); AMBUSH (they strike first).  SHOW lists a table with what ONCE and COOLDOWN hold
back, ADD checks an entry before it goes in, ROLL rolls the table for you where you are, and
 RESET lets ONCE and COOLDOWN entries come again.
```

<a id="farming"></a>

## FARMING

Source: [common_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/common_help.ini), line 782.

```text
<ABILITY>Usage    : PLANT (BUNDLE [NUM]) [RESOURCE NAME]
Example  : plant berries
Example  : plant bundle 10 berries
This skill allows the player to plant a resource into the ground.  The player must place a
sample of the resource on the ground first to use as seed.  After planting is completed, the
 resource will be ready to harvest some time later, after the plants have grown. There will
be no need to forage them, as the new crop will simply appear in the fields.  Most foods
with seeds can be grown from the food source, but others may require seeds, such as cotton
or hemp, etc. You can also bundle multiple resources together using this skill.  The GET
command can be used to unbundle such resources.  See also the Composting skill.
```

```text
<ABILITY>Usage    : FISH (BUNDLE [NUM]) [TARGET])
Example  : fish

the fish are biting.  Fishing is best done in the water. You can also bundle multiple
resources together using this skill.  The GET command can be used to unbundle such
```

<a id="fletching"></a>

## FLETCHING

Source: [common_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/common_help.ini), line 827.

```text
<ABILITY>Usage    : FLETCH (LIST/INFO/LEARN) [ITEM TYPE] (FROM [RESOURCE NAME])
Example  : fletch short bow
:        : fletch list
:        : fletch list bow
:        : fletch list 5-10
:        : fletch list all
:        : fletch learn crossbow
This skill allows a player to craft ranged wooden weapons, such as bows, crossbows,
blowguns, slings, and the necessary arrows and bolts. The extent of the items which can be
crafted expands as the player goes up in level.  The player may also learn how to fletch
found items, provided a blank recipe page, or recipe book with blank pages is in his or her
inventory. To begin fletching, the player must have placed the wood he or she wishes to make
 the item from on the ground. The raw wood for fletching is obtained by using the Chopping
skill.
```

<a id="formula-npcarmor"></a>

## FORMULA_NPCARMOR

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 203.

Help alias for **NPCFORMULAS**.

```text
Topic   : NPCFORMULAS
Short(s):
CoffeeSUD: the combat numbers a mob gets from its level, when it is made, by RESET
MOBCOMBATSTATS, Prop_Doppleganger, summons and hirelings, are formulas in coffeemud.ini (or
a world's world.ini): FORMULA_NPCHITPOINTS, FORMULA_NPCARMOR (lower is better; a half rounds
 down), FORMULA_NPCATTACK, FORMULA_NPCDAMAGE, FORMULA_NPCSPEED (attacks a round),
FORMULA_NPCREJUV (game minutes before a dead mob comes back) and FORMULA_NPCMONEY.  In each,
 @x1 is the level, @x2 LASTPLAYERLEVEL and @x3 the mob's ABILITY (its hit point modifier);
in FORMULA_NPCATTACK @x4 is the attack bonus a level from its attack attribute, and in
FORMULA_NPCMONEY @x5 is a roll of 1d(level) and @x6 a roll of 1d10.  The defaults are what
CoffeeMud always did, so nothing changes until they are edited; then RESET MOBCOMBATSTATS
WORLD brings the mobs already made into line.  Operators are worked left to right, so use
brackets; < is the smaller of two, > the larger, ? a random number between.  A formula that
does not work out is logged once and gives 0.  In the attack, armor, damage and crit
formulas, @xP is 1 when the one the number is for (the attacker, or whose armor it is) is a
character or follows one, and @xD is the difficulty's D (STORY 0.5, EASY 0.75, NORMAL 1,
HARD 1.25), so a curve can treat the player's side apart or follow the difficulty.
DIFFICULTY=NORMAL in coffeemud.ini or world.ini is a new game's difficulty, and
DIFFICULTY_[NAME]="NPCDAMAGE=n NPCHP=n PLAYERDAMAGE=n PLAYERXP=n D=x" changes a preset or
adds one; the player's DIFFICULTY command changes it in play, and the save keeps it.
Example: a low-magic world where mobs hit harder and are easier to hit:
FORMULA_NPCDAMAGE=@x1*1.3 and FORMULA_NPCARMOR=110-(@x1*1.8), then RESET MOBCOMBATSTATS
WORLD.
```

<a id="genability"></a>

## GENABILITY

Source: [arc_misc.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_misc.ini), line 1080.

```text
CoffeeSUD: a generic ability (CREATE ABILITY [ID], MODIFY ABILITY [ID]) is a spell, skill or
 property made as data.  Cast, it does what its fields say (target, cast messages, saving
throw, damage, HERESTATS, POSTCASTAFFECT...).  Added as a plain effect instead, as a
property on a room, item or mob (through the target's effects editor, or effect lists in
world files), it works as a property: its HERESTATS (stat adjustments, as dex+2) and its
MOCKABILITY (another ability it acts as, with MOCKABLETEXT) take hold at once, and its
SCRIPT runs as the thing's own script.  Its own text, given where it is added, reaches the
script: EFFECTPARM(KEY) is the value of KEY=VALUE in it, EFFECTPARM(*) all of it, and $PARMS
 all of it too; so one ability serves many settings (as with every script function, a
comparison goes inside the brackets: effectparm(LOUD == yes)).  A worked example, a
haunting: CREATE ABILITY Prop_Haunted, with the SCRIPT   RAND_PROG 10   if effectparm(LOUD
== yes)    mpecho Something moans behind the walls!   else    mpecho A cold draft slips
through the room.   endif   ~ then on each room that needs it: MODIFY ROOM, then add
Prop_Haunted in its effects editor with LOUD=no, or LOUD=yes for a loud one.  It is kept in
world/custom.cmare like any generic ability.  LIST ABILITYFLAGS shows the flag values.
Named hooks: its SCRIPT may have FUNCTION_PROG CANCAST (before any cost is paid; RETURN
false refuses the cast), ONCAST (once it is cast, $t the target), ONTICK (each tick it is on
 something), ONEXPIRE (when it wears off) and ONLEARN (when a mob gains it), each with $n
the caster or learner, $t the target and $0... the words given.  CASTMASK sees the target as
 $t in its +IF and -IF (a condition in quotes, as -IF "isname($t wolf)"), and CASTFAILMSG is
 what a caster who fails it is told (<T-NAME> the target), in place of "You do not meet the
requirements".  Example: Moonblade's   FUNCTION_PROG CANCAST   if !istime(night)    mpecho
The moon is hidden.    return false   endif   ~ and an ONEXPIRE that echoes "the moonlight
fades".  A GenTrap has ONTRIGGER and ONDISARM (AHELP GENTRAP).  TARGETMODE makes it an area
ability: SINGLE (the usual), ALLENEMIES (all the caster would fight there), ALLALLIES (the
caster's group there), ALLINROOM (all there, the caster too unless it is malicious) or
GROUPANYWHERE (the caster's group wherever they are).  The caster's mask, CANCAST and the
cost come once; then each target is cast at in turn, with its own target mask (a target it
turns away is passed over), cast message, saving throw, damage or healing, HERESTATS,
effects, extra castings and script event (ONCAST with $t).  MAXTARGETS, a formula (@x1 the
caster's level, @x2 how many there are), keeps only that many; AOEMSG is shown once, before
them.  Example: Thunderclap, TARGETMODE=ALLENEMIES, damage 2d6+@x1/2 and Spell_Deafness for
3 ticks after; Marching Cadence, TARGETMODE=ALLALLIES with HERESTATS for movement.
ACTIONCOST and COMBATACTIONCOST are what it takes in actions out of a fight and in one (or
when it is malicious), -1 for the default (DEFABLETIME and DEFCOMABLETIME in coffeemud.ini).
  COMPONENTS is a components.txt line kept in the ability's own record, as
(inventory:consumed:1:pinch of salt:), and takes the place of a line for this ID there
(AHELP COMPONENTS).  Data craft and gather skills and TWEAK abilities have the same three
fields.  Example: Greater Ward, COMBATACTIONCOST=2.0,
COMPONENTS=(inventory:consumed:1:salt:).  SUMMON, a catalog mob's name or a mob class,
brings that mob when the cast works: SUMMONCOUNT of them (a formula, @x1 the caster's level;
 1 when blank) at SUMMONLEVEL (a formula; blank keeps the mob's own level).  SUMMONFLAGS:
FOLLOW (it follows the caster, so it takes party turns and goes along), ASSIST (it fights
the caster's foes), NOSAVE (a save leaves it out), DISMISSONEXPIRE (it goes when the
ability's effect ends, or after the ability's duration when it has no effect) and BIND (it
goes when the caster dies or leaves the game).  A summon carries Prop_Summoned, gives no
experience and does not come back.  Example: Call the Pack, SUMMON=a grey wolf,
SUMMONCOUNT=1+(@x1/10), TICKSOVERRIDE=20, SUMMONFLAGS=FOLLOW ASSIST DISMISSONEXPIRE.
```

```text
CoffeeSUD: a building skill as data, as Construction or Masonry are in code: CREATE
```

## GENCRAFTSKILL

Source: [arc_misc.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_misc.ini), line 970.

```text
CoffeeSUD: what a data crafting skill (CREATE CRAFTSKILL, MODIFY CRAFTSKILL) has besides its
 name, trigger, recipe file, materials and verbs.  STATION: a workstation every recipe of it
 needs in the room (AHELP PROP_WORKSTATION).  CANLEARN: true lets a crafter LEARN [ITEM]: an
 item the skill could make (its material, and a recipe whose name fits) is taken apart, and
its recipe written into a recipe book they carry with blank pages.  LEARNMASK: an item mask
narrowing what it learns from, as -TAGS +rune for items tagged rune.  QUALITY: false keeps
```

<a id="gendisease"></a>

## GENDISEASE

Source: [arc_misc.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_misc.ini), line 988.

```text
CoffeeSUD: a disease as data, as the Disease_ ones are in code: CREATE DISEASE [ID] makes
one (or one in place of a coded disease of that ID, starting from its spread and
difficulty), MODIFY DISEASE [ID] changes it and DESTROY DISEASE [ID] removes it; it is kept
with the world like the other data skills, and cures, immunities and every check for a
disease know it as one.  Its fields: NAME and DISPLAY; TICKS, how long it lasts, and DELAY,
the ticks between its effects (formulas: @x1 the giver's level, @x2 its expertise, @x3 the
sufferer's level); SPREAD, by commas: STD (mating), CONTACT (touch), PROXIMITY (someone in
the room, each delay), CONSUMPTION (eaten or drunk), DAMAGE (bites and blows), GET (picked
up), HEARING (spoken to) and INHERITED; CATCHCHANCE (0-100, a formula), the chance a spread
goes ahead before the disease save; DIFFICULTY, which a cure (Prayer_CureDisease) cannot
beat when it times 10 is over the healer's level; STARTMSG, AFFECTMSG (each delay) and
DONEMSG; DAMAGE each delay (a formula, 1?4 is 1d4); ADJUSTMENTS (Prop_Adjuster's, as con-2)
and EFFECTS (Prop_SpellAdder's) while it lasts; IMMUNEMASK, who never catches it (-RACE
+Dwarf); MALICIOUS; HELP; and SCRIPT, a script run with it, whose functions ONAFFECT
(caught), ONTICK (each delay) and ONEXPIRE (run its course or cured) are called.  Example:
Ash Lung, SPREAD=PROXIMITY ADJUSTMENTS=con-2 DELAY=5 DAMAGE=1?4 DIFFICULTY=2
IMMUNEMASK="-RACE +Dwarf".
```

<a id="generate"></a>

## GENERATE

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 323.

```text
Command : GENERATE
Usage   : GENERATE [OBJ TYPE] [ID] (FROM [FILENAME]) ([VAR]=[VAL]...) ([DIR]/[TARGET])
Example : generate area maze_dungeon from randareas/example.xml areasize=50 "areaname= the
test" level_range=10?20 aggrochance=50 theme=kobolds south
Usage   : GENERATE CHECK [FILENAME]
Example : generate area maze_dungeon from randareas/forest.xml areaname=Woods areasize=20
level_range=5 aggrochance=0 theme=forest SEED=13 up
Example : generate string list
Example : generate check randareas/example.xml

CoffeeSUD: SEED=[N] builds the same thing each time (the same seed, the same area, rooms,
mobs and items); with no SEED it picks one and says it, and an area keeps it as its GENSEED
flag.  The game's own rolls go on as if nothing had been built.  In a template,
seed="[MATH]" on an AREA, ROOM, MOB or ITEM tag seeds just that one (seed="$[$GAME_DAY]" for
 one a day); $GEN_SEED is the seed in use.  An autogen instance's or AutoGrid's SEED
variable is a number, GAME (the save's own seed, so the same dungeon each visit) or ENTRY (a
 new one each time).

GENERATE FILL [ROOM ID] (FROM [FILENAME]) ([VAR]=[VAL]...) ROOM/AREA (KEEPTEXT) (SEED=[N])
runs a ROOM template on rooms that are already there: the room you are in, or every room of
its area.  Each room gets the tags a layout would give it, from its real exits:
ROOMTAG_NODETYPE (leaf for one exit, street for two, square for more), ROOMTAG_NODERUN (ns,
ew, ud, nesw or nwse for a straight street), ROOMTAG_NODEEXITS (,n,e,), ROOMTAG_NODEFLAGS
(corner, tee, intersection, gate), the neighbours' NODETYPE_x, ROOMTITLE_x and ROOMLINK_x,
ROOMTAG_NODEGATEEXIT and ROOMTAG_GATEEXITROOM for an exit out of the area, and the depth
tags from a walk from the entrance.  The template sets the title and description (unless
KEEPTEXT, or the room is GENLOCK) and adds its mobs, items, effects and behaviours; the
exits are left alone.

GENERATE PREVIEW [TYPE] [ID] (FROM [FILENAME]) ([VAR]=[VAL]...) (SEED=[N]) ([DIR]) builds an
 AREA (unlinked), a ROOM (in a free direction, or the one given), a MOB or an ITEM as
GENERATE would, with the database left out, lists it with the seed (each room's ID, title,
node type, exits, mobs with their levels and items; a mob's race, class and gear; an item's
level and value) and destroys it again.  GENERATE PREVIEW KEEP then runs the real GENERATE,
with the same words and seed (an area unlinked, unless a direction was given).  GENLAYOUT
draws a layout without building anything.

The layouts are APARTMENT, BOXCITY, BOXCITYSQUARE, BRANCH, CROSS, GRIDCITY, MAZE, MESH,
SPOTTEDMESH, TREE and MAP, and with CoffeeSUD: CAVE (smoothed random blobs and winding
passages), CLUMP (a square block with dead ends off it), LINEAR (a road with side spurs),
RING (a loop with spokes, for wall walks) and ISLANDS (clusters joined by single bridges).
layout="TREE,CAVE" picks one at random.  levels="N" on an AREA (or a ROOM with a layout)
splits its size over N floors of the layout, each joined to the next by a stair at rooms
that are not leaves: DOWN to the next floor and UP back, or the other way with
levelsdir="UP".  Rooms get ROOMTAG_LEVEL (1 for the entrance's floor) and ROOMTAG_STAIRS
(up, down, or up,down), and the area AREA_LEVELS.

layout="MAP" on an AREA lays its rooms out as drawn, in a MAP tag inside it or the file its
MAPFILE="world/maps/keep.txt" names (the size is the number of rooms drawn).  Each character
 that is not a link or a space is a room: . a street, o an interior room, L a leaf, @ the
entrance, ^ and v stairs, and any other a room built from the ROOM template its <GLYPH
char="B" room="boss_room"/> names (else from the AREA's rooms, as the others are).  Rooms
side by side are joined, - and | join rooms a space apart, + does so with a door, / and \\
on the diagonal; a line of = starts the floor above, and a ^ is joined to the v in the same
column there.  The rooms get the usual ROOMTAG tags, with ROOMTAG_GLYPH (the character) and
ROOMTAG_DOORS (,e,n,), so the themes fill a drawn plan as they fill a made one, and
re-rolling keeps the plan.

An AREA's ENSURE tags run once its rooms are laid out and filled.  <ENSURE NAME="[WORDS]" or
 VAR="[COUNTER]" MIN="[N]" MAX="[N]" FALLBACK="[ITEM OR MOB ID]" WHERE="..."
IN="MOB|CONTAINER|ROOM"/> makes sure of a thing: with NAME, the mobs and items whose names
hold the words are counted where they may be, and one in the wrong place is moved to a right
 one; with VAR, the counter is read; then the FALLBACK tag is built until MIN is reached,
and with NAME, MAX removes the extras (those in the wrong place first).  WHERE is ANY (the
default), REACHABLE (from the entrance) or REACHABLE-WITHOUT:KEYNAME=[KEY] (from the
entrance without going through a door locked to that key), so a key is never behind the door
 it opens; IN says whether an item goes on a mob, in a container or in the room there (ROOM
by default).  <ENSURE ROOM="[ROOM ID]" COUNT="[N]" REPLACE="[ROOM ID]"/> makes sure that
many rooms came from that ROOM template: the deepest rooms (of the REPLACE template, if
given) are emptied and made from it, keeping their exits.

UNLINKED as the last word (GENERATE AREA ... [DIR] UNLINKED) builds the area with no gate,
for LINK later; it says the entrance's room ID.  The area keeps a GENSOURCE flag, how it was
 made (the file, the AREA id, the seed and the variables given), saved in its .cmare:
REGENERATE AREA builds it again from it.  GEN_BACKTICKS=false in coffeemud.ini keeps real
apostrophes in what GENERATE makes (names and texts), rather than the engine's backticks.

Room templates in a generated area also see ROOMTAG_DEPTH (rooms from the entrance),
ROOMTAG_DEPTHPCT (0 to 100), ROOMTAG_ISDEEPEST (true or false), ROOMTAG_INDEX, ROOMTAG_X and
 ROOMTAG_Y, and AREA_MAXDEPTH and AREA_NUMROOMS; an AREA's order="depth", "reverse-depth" or
 "random" is the order its room groups are built in after the entrance.

GENERATE CHECK loads a file as GENERATE would, with its LOAD and FROM includes, generates
nothing, and lists its mistakes by line and tag id: what loading it complains of (duplicate
ids, includes that are missing), INSERT ids that are not defined, LIKE ids that are not
defined or not of the same tag, CLASS values that are no class of their kind, unknown
layouts and SELECT modes, and js: conditions and ${js:...} that do not compile.

A template can run JavaScript: ${js:expr} in a value puts in what it gives, and
condition="js:expr" or validate="js:expr" keeps a tag when it gives a true value.  The
expression sees defined (the variables, by any case; setting one defines it), obj (what is
being built), test(condition) (a condition in the template's grammar), and cm, gen and
require() from world/js/lib.  Math.random is the game's dice, so a seed covers it;
JSCRIPTS=0 turns it off.  The RandomAreas guide has the rest.

This command uses an xml file to generate random content for your mud.  This content can be
anything from whole areas, to rooms, mobs, items, or simple strings. By default, the content
 is built from the file in resources/randareas/example.xml, though the builder may specify
his or her own xml file path as one of the many arguments.  The arguments, briefly, are:

OBJ TYPE: One of the following: AREA, ROOM, MOB, ITEM, SCRIPT, or STRING.

ID      : one of the "id" xml attributes defined on any tag in the XML file. Use GENERATE
STRING LIST for a list of all "id" attributes defined in your file.

FROM "F": An optional argument to specify your own xml file, with the resources directory
being the default root.

VAR=VAL : One or more variables and their definitions.  Many tags will have a specific set
of required variables which must be defined in order for the content to be generated.
Failing to specify one of the required variables will cause an error message listing the
variables which must be defined, and the type of data required for the variable.  Variable
types which list numbers as their data types may also have math expressions values (so you
can use random numbers).  See the help on MATH EXPRESSION for more information on this.  In
addition to required variables, you may also use the space to enter one or more "override"
values.  Many object fields (such as LEVEL for mobs and items, or NAME, etc) as well as the
XML id tags, can have their "random" values overridden by defining them using the generate
command.  If you need to use a space in a variable value, enclose the ENTIRE definition in
quotes, such as "areaname=the dungeon" instead of areaname="the dungeon".

DIRECTION: This applies only to ROOM and AREA object types.  The object, if successfully
generated, will be linked to the current room that the player is standing in, in the
direction they specify.

TARGET: This applies only to SCRIPT object types.  The script, if successfully generated,
will be added to the target.

In closing, the GENERATE command is an interesting way to deliver large amounts of dynamic
content for your world, though it can never replace the caring touch of a real, creative
builder.  If anyone is interested in writing their own xml content, please open up the
/resources/randareas/example.xml file and begin reading. Use that file as an example on how
to construct your own.
```

<a id="gengatherskill"></a>

## GENGATHERSKILL

Source: [arc_misc.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_misc.ini), line 1133.

```text
CoffeeSUD: what a data gathering skill (CREATE GATHERSKILL, MODIFY GATHERSKILL) finds.  Each
 item in its ITEMXML may carry, inside its ITEM tag, <FREQ>[N]</FREQ> (its weight; 1 when
not given, 0 never), <MASK>[ZAPPER MASK]</MASK> (found only when the gatherer or their room
passes it, as -SEASON +WINTER, -HOUR +20, -WEATHER +THUNDERSTORM, -AREA +Frostmere or -LEVEL
 +>20; angle brackets written &lt; and &gt;) and <YIELD>[FORMULA]</YIELD> (how many, in
place of the skill's YIELDFORMULA).  NOTHINGFREQ is the weight of finding nothing.
YIELDFORMULA and YIELD take @x1 (the gatherer's level), @x2 (their proficiency), @x3 (their
expertise bonus) and @x4 (the percent of the room's yield left, 100 when it is fresh); a
formula is worked left to right, so use brackets, as 1+(@x2/40).  Example: driftwood
<FREQ>60</FREQ>, shells <FREQ>30</FREQ>, amber <FREQ>5</FREQ><MASK>-WEATHER
+THUNDERSTORM</MASK>, a message in a bottle <FREQ>1</FREQ>, and YIELDFORMULA 1+(@x2/40).
ACTIONCOST, COMBATACTIONCOST and COMPONENTS: as on a generic ability (AHELP GENABILITY).
```

## GENLANGUAGE

Help alias for **LANGUAGE_AUTHORING**.

```text
World languages and vocabulary
GenLanguage supports WORDFILE, SUFFIXES, SYLLABLES, KEEPWORDS, KEEPNAMES, WRITTENNAME and
TRANSLATESCRIPT. WORDFILE loads WORD=translation lines from world/vocab/languages/. Inline
HASHEDWORDS wins over the file. SUFFIXES uses S:en,ED:ka; SYLLABLES uses comma-separated
banks separated by /.
INTERPRETS=Elvish(60),Sylvan(30) grants partial understanding at the language's proficiency
times the percentage. Hearing, reading, scripts and inline LANG inscriptions share
comprehension, including translators on the listener, carried items and room. WRITTENNAME
names its script.
TRANSLATESCRIPT defines translate(word,language), optionally garble(text,count). Return null
 to use dictionaries. Normal JSCRIPTS approval and runtime limits apply.
See also: PROP_MONOLINGUAL, PROP_LANGUAGEIMMERSION, PROP_LOCALLISTS, PROP_WEAPONMESSAGES,
WORLD_VOCABULARY, LANGUAGE_SCRIPTING.
```

<a id="gentome"></a>

## GENTOME

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 2626.

```text
CoffeeSUD: a GenTome (CREATE ITEM GenTome) is a book whose pages are kept in it, so that
they go into the world files and every new game.  Its readable text holds the pages, <PAGE
TITLE="The Fall of Ost" LANG=Elvish LORE=ost.fall>text</PAGE> one after another, or
FILE=world/texts/ost.txt, a file in which a line "=== The Fall of Ost ===" (or "=== The Fall
 of Ost | LANG=Elvish LORE=ost.fall ===") begins each page.  READ BOOK lists the pages; READ
 3 BOOK, READ NEXT BOOK, READ PREV BOOK and READ [TITLE] BOOK read one.  A page in a
language (LANG) is read only by one who knows it; <VARIES> works in a page; LORE gives the
reader the tattoo LORE:[KEY].  READ_PROG PAGE 7 (or PAGE [TITLE]) fires for that page.  TEAR
 PAGE 3 FROM BOOK gives a page of its own (tagged PAGE:3; the book is tagged TORN:3).

Books and boards that keep their pages in the game's journals (GenBook, GenJournal) are
filled, when empty, from world/journals/[NAME].txt the first time they are read: [NAME] is
their name, lower case, spaces as _; "=== subject ===" begins each entry, and an AUTHOR:
line before the first names the writer.
```

<a id="gentrap"></a>

## GENTRAP

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 2642.

```text
CoffeeSUD: a GenTrap (CREATE ABILITY GenTrap, MODIFY ABILITY [ID]) has, besides its
messages, damage, ability and script:
TRIGGERS: what springs it, instead of its class's (entering a room, opening or unlocking an
exit or container, getting an item): message types, commas between, such as SIT, READ, LOOK,
 EXAMINE, OPEN, CLOSE, WEAR, HOLD, PUT, DROP, GET; on a room ENTER, LEAVE:[DIRECTION] and
the others, by anyone there.
DISARM: verb:[PHRASE], typed there, disarms it (until it resets), besides the usual skills.
ONCE: it springs once and is gone.
Its script (the Scriptable Parm) runs when it springs, with or without an ability: ACT_PROG
[TRAP ID], $t the one who sprang it.  CoffeeSUD: its FUNCTION_PROG ONTRIGGER runs then too,
$n the one who sprang it, and ONDISARM when it is disarmed (its DISARM verb or a thief's
skill), $n the one who did, if known.
```

<a id="gentweak"></a>

## GENTWEAK

Source: [arc_misc.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_misc.ini), line 1014.

```text
CoffeeSUD: a tweak (CREATE TWEAK [ID], MODIFY TWEAK [ID]) is a coded ability (its ORIGINAL)
under a new name, with its words, range, cost, cooldown and messages changed (STRING),
keeping all it does.  Cast, it casts the original with the caster's proficiency.  More it
can have: CASTMASK, who may cast it, and where (-LOCALE +OUTDOORS); TARGETMASK, whom or what
 it works on; POSTCASTAFFECT, effects put on the target after a cast that worked, and
POSTCASTABILITY, abilities cast on it after (Prop_SpellAdder's form: 20%;Fighter_Trip);
DURATIONMULT, times how long the effects it leaves last, and DAMAGEMULT, times the damage
the cast and those effects do (1 for none); and SCRIPT, a script whose functions are called:
 CANCAST before (return false or CANCEL to stop it, $t the target), ONCAST after a cast that
 worked, and ONEXPIRE when the effect it left wears off.  Example: Stormcall, a tweak of
Spell_Lightning, CASTMASK="-LOCALE +OUTDOORS", POSTCASTABILITY= "20%;Fighter_Trip".
```

```text
This skill allows a player to craft glass items, such as cups and flasks.  The extent of the
 items which can be crafted expands as the player goes up in level.  The player may also
learn how to make found items, provided a blank recipe page, or a recipe book with blank
pages is in his or her inventory. To begin blowing glass, the player must be in a room with
```

<a id="gmodify"></a>

## GMODIFY

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 2655.

```text
Command : GMODIFY
Usage   : GMODIFY (AREA/ROOM/WORLD/PLAYERS/#TAG) [FIELD=VAL](&&/||[...])
Usage   :         (CHANGE=[FIELD=VAL])
Example : gmodify area class=genmob&&name=the cityguard change=name=the guard
Example : gmodify world class=[cs]GenMob&&name=[ss]city change=name=[ss]
Example : gmodify world class=[cs]GenItem&&name=a rusty sword change=destroy=true
Example : gmodify players charclass=Fighter
Example : gmodify #mytag change=ability=12
Example : gmodify ?
Short(s):
A command to select objects in a an area, some rooms, or the whole world based on the
specified field values, and optionally change some of those specified fields.

Searching the entire WORLD is implied, but the first parameter may be the word AREA or ROOM
to narrow the search.  You may also enter a hash mark and the name of a TAG to only search
tagged objects.

The next parameter is the search criteria.  The key phrase WHEN= may optionally precede it
to make explicit that you are specifying the search criteria.  The search criteria fields
may be separated by && strings to specify that all of the preceding criteria AND the next
single criteria must be true.  The criteria fields may also be separated by || strings to
specify that all of the preceding criteria OR the next single criteria may be true.  One of
those strings must be present when specifying more than one criteria.

Each field in the search criteria must be of the form FIELD=VALUE, FIELD!=VALUE,
FIELD$VALUE, FIELD>VALUE, FIELD<VALUE, FIELD>=VALUE, or FIELD<=VALUE.  Where FIELD must be a
 valid search field.  Enter GMODIFY ? for a complete list of all valid fields.  Not all
fields will apply to all object types, so take this into account especially when using < or
!= operators.  The operators are all normal except for the new one, $, which means that the
value is really a regular expression. The VALUE portion of the criteria may be prefixed with
 modifiers, which include:
[ss] to specify that the value refers to a substring of the fields whole value.
[cs] to specify that the search is case sensitive (case insensitive is implied).

The last parameter is the optional change specifications.  These specifications must be
prefixed with the key phrase CHANGE=.  If these specifications are not included, GMODIFY
will display the results of the search.  The change specifications are similar to the search
 criteria in that they consist of groupings of FIELD=VALUE separated by && strings.  Unlike
search criteria, however, operators other than =, and strings other than || have no special
meaning.  The fields, like in the search criteria, must be valid fields for the options
selected by the search criteria.  A special field name "DESTROY", when set to true, will
obliterate the item in question.  Otherwise, the ordinary fields on the object will be
changed to the specified value UNLESS the following conditions are met: the VALUE portion of
 a field is prefixed with the modifier [ss], and the VALUE portion of an identical field in
the search criteria was also prefixed with the modifier [ss].  Under those special
conditions, instead of substituting the entire field value on the object with the new value,
 ONLY the portion of the string selected in the search criteria will be substituted.

* Be very careful with this command! It is wise to try the command WITHOUT change= ...
first, to make sure you are matching Exactly what you expect, before doing a change pass.

Exits are matched and changed too, with their own fields (CLOSEDTEXT, KEYNAME, DOORNAME and
the like), each room's saved with it; an area's own fields (AUTHOR, CURRENCY, PLAYERLEVEL
and the like) are known as well: gmodify area name$wooden change=name=stone
```

<a id="god"></a>

## GOD

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 2737.

```text
Command  : GOD
Usage    : GOD
Usage    : GOD [CHEAT/POWER/ALL] ([CHEAT/POWER]...) (ON/OFF)
Usage    : GOD RESET
Example  : god noclip noaggro on
Example  : god nodamage
Example  : god immort off
Example  : god all off
Short(s) :
A developer's cheats, in a DEV=1 game or in builder mode.  GOD alone lists them, and whether
 each is on.  The cheats are NOCLIP (walk through closed and locked doors and past the
Prop_Req* entry checks, and walking costs no movement), NOCOST (skills cost no mana,
movement or hit points, and need no wait), NODAMAGE (take no damage), NODEATH (hit points
stop at 1), SEEALL (see in the dark, the hidden, the invisible and those who sneak, and
never be blind) and NOAGGRO (aggressive creatures leave you be).  A cheat's name with ON or
OFF turns it on or off; with neither, it turns over.  Some sysop powers give a part of a
cheat already (GOTO walks through doors, ALLSKILLS skips the wait, IMMORT keeps you alive,
ORDER or CMDROOMS keep the aggressive away); turning the cheat OFF takes that away too.  A
sysop power's name (IMMORT, GOTO, ALLSKILLS...) with OFF suspends that power for you, and
with ON gives it back.  ALL is every cheat: ALL OFF plays as a mortal would.  RESET forgets
them all.  The cheats are kept with the character (Prop_DevCheats).
```

<a id="hazards"></a>

## HAZARDS

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 1830.

```text
Command  : HAZARDS
Usage    : HAZARDS ([AREA NAME])
Usage    : WEATHER SET [WEATHER] (FOR [N] HOURS/DAYS) (AREA [NAME]) (NEXT)
Usage    : WEATHER FORECAST
Usage    : WEATHER NEXT
Usage    : TIME SET [HOUR/DAWN/DAY/DUSK/NIGHT]
Usage    : TIME SEASON [SPRING/SUMMER/FALL/WINTER]
Usage    : LOOK AS [CONDITION]...
Example  : weather set thunderstorm
Example  : time set dusk
Example  : look as night fog
Short(s) : WEATHER SET,WEATHER FORECAST,WEATHER NEXT,TIME SET,TIME SEASON,LOOK AS
For builders (builder mode, a DEV=1 game, or CMDAREAS).  HAZARDS lists what an area holds
that acts on those in it: the area's own behaviours and effects (spawners such as
RandomMonsters, weather), and in its rooms, exits and items their behaviours, traps,
Prop_InstantDeath, Prop_NarrowLedge and Prop_Weather, each with its state (as STAT BEHAVIORS
 gives it) or its parameters.  WEATHER SET changes the area's weather now, as a change of
weather comes, with its messages and the scripts that wait on it, or with NEXT only the
weather that comes next (CLEAR, CLOUDY, WINDY, RAIN, THUNDERSTORM, SNOW, HAIL, HEAT, SLEET,
BLIZZARD, DUST, DROUGHT, COLD, FOG); FOR holds it there, each change coming back to it, for
that much game time. WEATHER FORECAST shows the weather now, what comes next, a hold, and
the odds of each weather the step after, from the area's season and climate; WEATHER NEXT
makes the next change now. TIME SET runs the area's clock forward, hour by hour as TICKTOCK
does (so its events happen), to an hour or the start of DAWN, DAY, DUSK or NIGHT; TIME
SEASON runs it forward a month at a time to the season.  LOOK AS shows this room under
made-up conditions, as PREVIEW does.
```

```text
Usage   : Shows you the formal usage information.  Words in

Usage   : thing to type in.
```

<a id="holidays"></a>

## HOLIDAYS

Source: [arc_misc.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_misc.ini), line 922.

```text
Holidays are a special/reserved quest defined by file
/resources/quests/holidays/holidays.quest. They are very simple Scriptless quests that can
be started at random intervals, or on certain mud dates, or real-life dates.  The holidays
will only impact the areas specified by the holiday settings, and only the mobs in those
areas specified in the settings, and only with the features you specify.  Use LIST HOLIDAYS
to see a list of all defined holidays and the areas hey are defined for.  By default, 3
special-case weather related holidays are included which impact any area that meets their
criteria.  You can use MODIFY HOLIDAY <name> to change the settings for a holiday, DESTROY
HOLIDAY <name> to delete one, or CREATE HOLIDAY name to create a new one that will
automatically apply to the area the creator is standing in.  CoffeeSUD: a holiday (any
quest) may start, besides SET MUDDAY m-d, on SET WEEKDAY [NAME] (each week), SET EVERY [N]
DAYS FROM [Y/M/D], SET SEASONSTART [SEASON] (its first day; a calendar's own season by name
too, AHELP CALENDAR) or SET MOON ([MOON]) [PHASE] (the first day of that phase: SET MOON
FULL, SET MOON Ember FULL).  SET DATE m-d follows the game's calendar, and DAYS and HOURS in
 a SET DURATION are game ones (2 DAYS is 2 MUDDAYS).  SET HOLIDAY [NAME] has a quest run
exactly while that holiday is on.  Scripts see them by name: ISHOLIDAY(name), HOLIDAY() (the
 names on now), the masks +HOLIDAY [NAME ...] and -HOLIDAY [NAME ...], <HOLIDAY
name>...</HOLIDAY> in VARIES text; JavaScript's cm.holiday(name) and cm.holidays(). CALENDAR
 HOLIDAYS lists each game-dated one, on now or in how many game days.  A quest may also run
in a game-time window: SET SCHEDULE "[RULES]", every rule holding: HOUR a-b, WEEKDAY [NAME],
 EVERY [N] DAYS (AT DAWN, AT HOUR h), SEASON [NAME], MONTH [NAME or N], MOON ([MOON])
[PHASE], HOLIDAY [NAME], WEATHER [STATE] (in the quest's area).  It starts as its window
opens, once each time; SET DURATION UNTIL DUSK, UNTIL HOUR h or UNTIL END ends it at dusk,
at that hour, or as the window closes (a DURATION of ticks or game days counts down as
ever).
```

<a id="home"></a>

## HOME

Source: [help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/help.ini), line 1627.

```text
Command : HOME
Usage   : HOME (SET)
Example : home
Example : home set
Short(s):
CoffeeSUD: takes the whole party home: to the leader's home, the room where they last slept
in a home (or set it with HOME SET).  It takes a few turns (HOMERECALL in the ini, 3 by
default; 0 turns it off), and a fight in the party stops it.  A home is a room with
Prop_HomeBeacon, or, where the world says so (HOMEBEACONS=true), any room you own; sleeping
in it, or HOME SET there, makes it the start room of every character of the party with
privileges there, so RECALL brings them there too.  (HELP HOMES is about owning property.)
```

```text
<ABILITY>Usage    : HUNT

With this common skill, a player checks carefully for the tracks of any game which may be
nearby.  When the tracks are found, the player needs to check nearby rooms for the animal
and attack it to complete the hunt. Hunting can be done almost anywhere, though Forests,
Jungles, and Plains are best.
```

<a id="instancearea"></a>

## INSTANCEAREA

Source: [arc_properties.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_properties.ini), line 229.

```text
Property   : InstanceArea
Targets    : Mobs, Items, Area
Parameters : TYPEID or instance modification arguments (see areainstancetypes.txt)
Example    : Triumph
Example    : ID=ANYTHING
Example    : LIKE=Triumph AREAMATCH=Midgaard
Description:
This misc property, when applied to an area, will put anyone who enters the area into a
group instance of the area, as per StdThinInstance.  Modifications to the mobs, items, and
levels of the area will be applied according to a TYPEID given in the arguments, which
matches a type from resources/skills/areainstancetypes.txt. If no modifications are desired,
 then at least an ID= parameter is required.

When the property is applied to a player or item directly, then it will also require an
AREAMATCH argument to specify which area(s) will be instanced when entering them.
```

<a id="instrumentmaking"></a>

## INSTRUMENTMAKING

Source: [common_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/common_help.ini), line 1027.

```text
<ABILITY>Usage    : INSTRUMENTMAKE (LIST/INFO/LEARN) [ITEM TYPE]
Example  : instrumentmake piccolo

:        : instrumentmake list piccolo
:        : instrumentmake list 5-10
:        : instrumentmake list all

This skill allows a player to craft musical instruments, such as flutes and guitars.  The
extent of the items which can be crafted expands as the player goes up in level.  The player
 may also learn to make new found instruments, provided a blank recipe page or a recipe book
 with blank pages is in his or her inventory. To begin making a new item, the player must
have placed the material he or she wishes to make the item from on the ground. Instruments
crafted with balsa can be done with half the required wood listed, while instruments crafted
 with ironwood will require twice the required wood listed.
```

<a id="jconsole"></a>

## JCONSOLE

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 448.

```text
Command : JCONSOLE
Usage   : JCONSOLE (@[TARGET]) ([STATEMENT])
Example : jconsole ([statement])
Short(s):
When entered with a statement, this command will execute the single javascript statement and
 exit.  When entered alone, it will enter a console where the user can enter as many
javascript statements as they want, and the system will even remember any variables or
functions they've defined later one (does NOT survive reboots!).

All the Scriptable/MOBPROG commands and functions are also available, though the commands
and functions must be entered in ALL UPPERCASE, and commands must have their parameters
separated by commas instead of spaces, be put into quotes, and surrounded by parenthesis
like javascript function calls.

For multi-line data, you can enter multi-line mode by entering < by itself, and exiting by
entering > by itself.  If you have GMCP, you might see a pop-up too.

JCONSOLE @[NAME] (a mob or item), @HERE, @AREA or @ME binds the console to that thing: its
MOBPROG calls run as it, with you as the source, and me, here and cm are its.  Lines that
start with a dot are the console's own: .trigger GREET|SPEECH [TEXT]|GIVE [ITEM]|LOOK|TICK
fires that event on it, .inspect [EXPR] shows a thing's name, class, room and stats, .load
[FILE] runs a file, .reset clears the console, .time ON|OFF shows each line's time, .history
 lists the lines before and !N runs line N again.  In builder mode the history is kept from
one game to the next.
```

<a id="jewelmaking"></a>

## JEWELMAKING

Source: [common_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/common_help.ini), line 1068.

Help alias for **JEWEL_MAKING**.

```text
<ABILITY>Usage    : JEWEL (LIST/INFO/MEND/REFIT/LEARN/MOUNT (GEM)/ENCRUST (GEM)) [ITEM TYPE]
Usage    :   ... (FROM [RESOURCE NAME])
Example  : jewel ring
:        : jewel list

This skill allows a player to craft jewelry, such as rings, earrings, necklaces, and
bracelets, or to mount or encrust bits of precious jewels onto other items.  The extent of
the items which can be newly crafted expands as the player goes up in level.  The player may
 also learn to make new found jewelry, provided a blank recipe page, or a recipe book with
blank pages is in his or her inventory. To begin crafting, the player must be in a room with
 an open fire burning, and must have placed the metal he or she wishes to make the item from
 on the ground, along with any precious gems. which may be mounted in the jewelry. The raw
gems for jewel making are found using the Digging skill.  The metal is obtained using the
Mining skill.
```

```text
Short(s) :
Runs the given file as Javascript.  See the Programming Guide for more information on how to
 write Javascript for CoffeeMud.  A script run this way may take up to JSTIMELIMIT_JRUN
seconds (30 unless the ini says otherwise); other scripts up to JSTIMELIMIT seconds (2).
See JS ERRORS.  A JRUN script has a builder object too: builder.here(), room(id), dig(dir,
type) (a room made as WORLD DIG makes one), link(fromId, dir, toId), create('mob' or 'item',
 catalog name or class, roomId), saveRoom(id), forEachRoom(area, function) and cmd('a
command'), each as you.
```

<a id="js"></a>

## JS

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 3032.

```text
Command  : JS ERRORS
Usage    : JS ERRORS ([NUMBER]), JS STATE ([KEY] (= {VALUE}/DELETE)), JS RELOAD
([FILE]/ALL), JS WATCH ON/OFF, JS HELP [EXPR]
Example  : js errors 20
Short(s) :
Lists the most recent JavaScript errors since the game started (10, or the number given):
when, where the script is (its host, room and trigger, or the JRUN file, quest or cron job),
 the line, and what went wrong.  A script that runs past its interpreted instruction limit
(JSTIMELIMIT in the ini) is stopped, and listed here too. Blocking Java calls and compiled
classes cannot be preempted safely on the game thread. Use cm.background(worker, data,
timeoutMs, callback) for blocking work: JSON data enters a fresh worker scope, and
callback(error, result) runs on the game thread. The returned job has cancel(), done(),
error() and resultJSON(). Workers have no cm, closure or game objects; callbacks and jobs
are cancelled by a new game/restore and are not saved. In builder mode each error is also
shown as it happens.
Every JavaScript (a script's <SCRIPT>, JRUN, JCONSOLE, a quest's, cron's, world/js/init.js,
a JS class) may require('name') a library: world/js/lib/name.js, or else
resources/js/lib/name.js, gives what it puts in exports.  Each is compiled once, and read
again when its file changes.  Random-area templates require() them too, in ${js:...} and js:
 conditions (AHELP GENERATE).
A world keeps its JavaScript classes in world/js/[kind]/ (behaviors, abilities, properties,
items, mobs, races, charclasses, commands, common, locales, exits, areas), loaded as the
game starts; resources/js/templates/ has commented templates for a behaviour and a property.
  A room's or area's behaviour may extend
com.planet_ink.coffee_mud.Behaviors.JSWorldBehavior and define onEnter, onLeave, onWeather
and onDaypart.  A script's LOAD=world:scripts/name.script reads a file of world/scripts/.
WORLD CHECK's JS part lists the classes that do not compile or extend nothing.
Every JavaScript scope also has cm, the game's objects (cm.here(), cm.room(id),
cm.findMob(name), cm.loadMob(catalogName, room), cm.say(mob, text), cm.mp('MPECHO hi'),
cm.var(host, name), cm.clock(), cm.weather(), cm.law(), cm.shop(mob), cm.bank(mob), cm.lib
for CMLib...); cm.on(event, fn) for the clock, the weather and the game's course (a save
listener that returns false refuses the save); sud (sud.time, sud.party, sud.save, sud.find,
 sud.vars); include('path') or include('world:path'); debug(x); and importPackage.  JCONSOLE
 has here, area and target.  guides/JavaScriptSUD.html lists it all.
cm.store(key) is a plain JavaScript object kept with the game: key is 'world', 'quest:name',
 any string, or a room, mob, item or area. Mobs/items use persistent instance IDs, so names
and locations can change and copies have independent stores. Unambiguous old name keys
migrate; ambiguous legacy data stays available under its explicit string key. A save writes
it as JSON, a restore puts it back, and a new game starts from world/js/state.json if the
world has one.  JS STATE lists the stores, JS STATE key shows one, JS STATE key = {gold: 5}
replaces it and JS STATE key DELETE takes it away (in builder mode).
cm.on also hears the world, wherever it happens: death(victim, killer), beforeDeath (false
keeps the victim alive), levelUp(mob, level), questWin(mob, quest), questEnd(quest, mob,
why), enterRoom(mob, room, from), beforeEnterRoom (false keeps the mover out),
enterArea(mob, area, from), itemGained(mob, item), itemLost(mob, item), factionChange(mob,
faction, change) and turn(leader, count); cm.off(event, fn) takes one away.  Register them
in world/js/init.js's onBoot.
The property Prop_JScript and the behaviour JSBehavior run a JavaScript file:
SCRIPT=world:js/props/x.js and parameters, which the file has as parms (see AHELP
PROP_JSCRIPT and AHELP BEHAVIOR_JSBEHAVIOR).
JS RELOAD migrates declared STATE/ACTIVITY, effect duration, proficiency and invoker.
Incompatible live instances keep their old class and are counted in the reload report. JS
RELOAD puts the world/js files changed since the game started (or since their last reload)
into the running world; JS RELOAD file reloads one, JS RELOAD ALL every one.  A file that
does not compile is shown with its line, and left as it was.  init.js is read again and its
onReload(old) called; a library is read again where it is required from then on; a class is
compiled again, and its behaviours and effects in the world replaced; a Prop_JScript or
JSBehavior file is read again by each one running it, which calls its onReload(old) with the
 old scope.  JS WATCH ON ([SECONDS]) does it by itself as files change; JS WATCH OFF stops
it.  Builder mode only.
The behaviour JScriptable scripts a mob, item, room, exit or area wholly in JavaScript, with
 handlers as onSpeech(who, text) and onGive(who, item) (see AHELP BEHAVIOR_JSCRIPTABLE).
Math.random() in every JavaScript scope is the game's own dice, so a game started with
RANDOMSEED= rolls the same, and a save keeps where the dice were.  cm.now() and cm.ticks()
are the game's time, which stands still while it is paused; cm.realNow() is the real time.
Date is the real date and time.
A zapper mask may have -JS "expr" (only what the JavaScript expression is true for) and +JS
"expr" (what it is true for, whatever else the mask says): the expression sees mob, item,
room, target and cm, cm.store included; an error counts as false.
JS HELP [expression] shows the methods of what an expression gives, and its stats: JS HELP
cm.room('Town#1'), JS HELP cm, JS HELP cm.store('world').  guides/JavaScriptSUD.html says
where JavaScript runs, what each place has, and how to do common things.
A quest may have JavaScript handlers, in SET JSFILE world:js/quests/x.js or a <JSQUEST> ...
</JSQUEST> block: onStart(state), onStep(n, state), onTimeUp(state), onWin(player),
onAccept(player) and onStop(), with state cm.store('quest:name') and a quests helper; the
JScriptables of its mobs and items may have onQuestAccept, onQuestStep, onQuestWin,
onQuestFail and onQuestEnd.
Timers on the game's clock, which wait while it is paused and step with its turns:
cm.every(10, fn), cm.every('6 hours', fn), cm.at('day 7 hour 8', fn) and cm.after(ticks, fn,
 data); an after() is kept in the save. cm.stopTimer(key) takes one away, cm.timers() lists
them.
cm.command('dig', {help: 'DIG [DIRECTION]', cost: 1, combatCost: 2, words: ['excavate']},
function(mob, args) {...}) makes a command of the world's (DIG ? shows its help);
cm.verb(thing, 'pull lever', function(mob, rest) {...}) makes a phrase that works near that
room, item or mob only.  Register them in init.js's onBoot.
world/scripts/progression.js: onCreated(mob), onCreationStep(mob, step, answer), xpGain(mob,
 source, amount) (returns the experience), onLevel(mob, level), practicesForLevel(mob) and
trainsForLevel(mob) (return the numbers), onLearn(mob, abilityId), onTrain(mob, what,
amount), and statRoll(mob, bonus) when STARTSTAT=SCRIPT.
```

<a id="kit"></a>

## KIT

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 1828.

Help alias for **TESTCHAR**.

```text
Command  : TESTCHAR
Usage    : TESTCHAR [NAME] (KIT=[KIT]) (PARTY)
Usage    : KIT [KIT] ([CHARACTER OR MOB])
Example  : testchar Tank KIT=act3-warrior PARTY
Example  : kit act3-cleric Heals
Short(s) : KIT
In builder mode or a DEV=1 game, TESTCHAR makes a character of your profile with no
questions: an average human apprentice of level 1, or as the kit says, levelled as CHARGEN
levels, starting where you are or in the kit's room.  PARTY brings them into the world and
the party (as PARTY ADD); without it they rest in the profile.  KIT gives a character, a
follower or a mob here (you, by default) a kit.  Kits are kept with the world,
world/kits/NAME.kit, one setting a line (# for comments): race, class, gender, alignment
(good, neutral, evil...), level, gold, room, item (a class, or catalog:NAME; worn if it can
be; as many as wanted), ability ID PROFICIENCY, faction ID VALUE and var NAME VALUE (a
global script variable of the character).  An item may have a count first (item 2 catalog:a
ration) and may be a plain catalog name.  Starting kits: a kit with a starting line
(starting all, or starting and a zapper mask, as starting -BASECLASS +Fighter or starting
-TATTOO +ORIGIN_NOBLE) is given to every new character it lets in, its items, gold (added),
abilities, factions and vars (not its race, class, level or room).  Kits with the same
choose GROUP are a menu in the KIT step of creation, after the origin (AHELP ORIGINS): one
is taken (one alone is taken with no question).  title names it in the menu; wear no keeps
its items in the pack.
```

<a id="law"></a>

## LAW

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 1861.

```text
Command  : LAW
Usage    : LAW
Usage    : LAW CRIMES ([TEXT])
Usage    : LAW WARRANTS ([NAME])
Usage    : LAW PARDON [NAME] ([CRIME]/ALL)
Usage    : LAW ACCUSE [NAME] [CRIME]
Usage    : LAW TEST [CRIME] (AS [CHARACTER]) (AGAINST [VICTIM])
Usage    : LAW SET KEY=VALUE
Example  : law
Example  : law accuse Bob ASSAULT
Short(s) :
In builder mode, a DEV=1 game or with ABOVELAW: the law of the area you are in, as it found
its people and places by name: the legal behaviour and its law file, the officers and judges
 it found among the area's mobs (or that it found none, so that a misnamed guard shows at
once, and a mob named as one but not one, and why: an officer must wander, a judge stay
put), the jail and release rooms each name found (or FOUND NOWHERE), the taxes, and how many
 crimes and warrants there are.  CRIMES lists the crimes, with their names, sentences,
places and circumstances, or those holding the text.  WARRANTS lists the warrants out, or a
person's.  PARDON takes a person's warrants away, or those for one crime. ACCUSE makes one,
as a witness would. TEST checks the actual warrant eligibility rules and explains refusal
without changing warrants or campaign dice. It uses a fixed roll for random ignore flags.
SET copies a shared law into this area's custom law before editing it; in builder mode, the
custom definition is exported with the world.
```

<a id="learn"></a>

Source: [help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/help.ini), line 2861.

```text

Example : learn stealthy ii
Example : learn magic missile Horice
Example : learn strength from Horice
Short(s):
If your character has the necessary training sessions and/or practice points, this command
will allow you to request training in the specified skill, spell, chant, prayer, attribute,
or expertise.  In addition to specifying the ability to learn, you may also specify a MOB
who is present in the room who can teach you in that skill.  See also help on TRAIN, GAIN,
```

```text
Command : MODULES

Usage   : MODULES DEMO [MODULE ID]
Lists this campaign's optional modules and any suspension reason. New modules are default
off; the world's MODULES setting selects roots and their declared dependencies. Existing
campaigns keep their saved selection and effective settings. Installing a manifest alone
does not enable it.
The optional example.counter module provides MODULES DEMO example.counter, which advances a
character-owned practice counter without changing combat or rewards. It must be installed
and selected by the creator.
Creators can use WORLD MODULES in builder mode or DEV=1 to inspect, validate, plan/reload
definitions, explicitly adopt a world-selected module, configure a campaign setting or
inspect saved state. See AHELP WORLD_MODULES.
```

<a id="namestyles"></a>

## NAMESTYLES

Source: [arc_misc.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_misc.ini), line 1295.

```text
CoffeeSUD: random names by culture, one file per style: world/namegen/STYLE.ini, else
resources/namegen/STYLE.ini (or the world's own copy).  Lines are KEY=value (# a comment; a
key given twice adds to the first).  VOWELS= and CONSONANTS= are the syllables, taken in
turn, each followed by a digit: 4 it may be in the middle, 2 first, 1 last (7 anywhere).
START=VOWEL|CONSONANT|EITHER, SYLLABLES=2-4 (when none are asked for), PREFIXES= and
SUFFIXES= (comma lists) with PREFIXPCT= and SUFFIXPCT= (25), MALE=, FEMALE= and NEUTER=
given names used GIVENPCT= (50) percent of the time, FAMILY= or FAMILYSTART= with FAMILYEND=
 joined, and TITLES= with TITLEPCT= (20) for the full form.  RACES= and LANGUAGES= name the
races (ID, name or category) and languages that use the style; a GenRace's or GenLanguage's
own NAMESTYLE (MODIFY RACE, the language editor) comes first.  default.ini is the old table:
 a world's own default changes every name that names no style.  elvish, dwarvish and goblin
ship.  Templates write $SYSTEM_RANDOM_NAME:2-4:elvish (a style, race or language; :FULL adds
 the family name and title); with no style, a NAMESTYLE the template or its theme defines,
else the mob's race's.  Scripts use RANDNAME(), JavaScript CM.core.NameStyles.make(style,
min, max, gender, full).  NEW * dwarf at the profile menu offers a dwarvish name, as does
True Name on a dwarf.
```

<a id="note"></a>

## NOTE

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 1902.

```text
Command  : NOTE
Usage    : NOTE (HERE) [TEXT]
Usage    : NOTES (ALL)
Usage    : NOTES DONE/UNDONE/GOTO [NUMBER]
Example  : note the miller mentions a dog that is not in the room
Example  : notes goto 4
Short(s) :
In any game: a playtest note, kept in notes/playtest.txt (NOTESFILE= in coffeemud.ini),
outside the world and the saves, so that a note made in play reaches builder mode, where the
 fix is made.  Each note has the date, the save, the character, the room's ID and name, the
game time and the text.  NOTE HERE adds the room as it is: its exits, mobs, items, effects
and behaviours.  NOTES lists those to do, numbered (ALL with those done), NOTES DONE marks
one done and UNDONE takes that back, and NOTES GOTO, in builder mode or a DEV=1 game, takes
you to the note's room.
```

<a id="npcformulas"></a>

## NPCFORMULAS

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 178.

```text
Topic   : NPCFORMULAS
Short(s):
CoffeeSUD: the combat numbers a mob gets from its level, when it is made, by RESET
MOBCOMBATSTATS, Prop_Doppleganger, summons and hirelings, are formulas in coffeemud.ini (or
a world's world.ini): FORMULA_NPCHITPOINTS, FORMULA_NPCARMOR (lower is better; a half rounds
 down), FORMULA_NPCATTACK, FORMULA_NPCDAMAGE, FORMULA_NPCSPEED (attacks a round),
FORMULA_NPCREJUV (game minutes before a dead mob comes back) and FORMULA_NPCMONEY.  In each,
 @x1 is the level, @x2 LASTPLAYERLEVEL and @x3 the mob's ABILITY (its hit point modifier);
in FORMULA_NPCATTACK @x4 is the attack bonus a level from its attack attribute, and in
FORMULA_NPCMONEY @x5 is a roll of 1d(level) and @x6 a roll of 1d10.  The defaults are what
CoffeeMud always did, so nothing changes until they are edited; then RESET MOBCOMBATSTATS
WORLD brings the mobs already made into line.  Operators are worked left to right, so use
brackets; < is the smaller of two, > the larger, ? a random number between.  A formula that
does not work out is logged once and gives 0.  In the attack, armor, damage and crit
formulas, @xP is 1 when the one the number is for (the attacker, or whose armor it is) is a
character or follows one, and @xD is the difficulty's D (STORY 0.5, EASY 0.75, NORMAL 1,
HARD 1.25), so a curve can treat the player's side apart or follow the difficulty.
DIFFICULTY=NORMAL in coffeemud.ini or world.ini is a new game's difficulty, and
DIFFICULTY_[NAME]="NPCDAMAGE=n NPCHP=n PLAYERDAMAGE=n PLAYERXP=n D=x" changes a preset or
adds one; the player's DIFFICULTY command changes it in play, and the save keeps it.
Example: a low-magic world where mobs hit harder and are easier to hit:
FORMULA_NPCDAMAGE=@x1*1.3 and FORMULA_NPCARMOR=110-(@x1*1.8), then RESET MOBCOMBATSTATS
WORLD.
```

```text
Short(s) :
In builder mode, a DEV=1 game or with CMDFACTIONS: reads faction files again from their

counts), bands that overlap or leave a gap, CHANGE triggers that match nothing, REACTION and
 AFFBEHAV IDs that are no ability, behaviour, command or social, a REACTION range that is no
 band's code, and a RELATION faction that does not exist.  CLANS lists the world files' mobs
```

```text
CoffeeSUD: character origins (backgrounds), in world/origins.ini.  Each starts with [ID] and
 has KEY=VALUE lines (a line ending in \\ goes on to the next; # starts a comment): NAME,
DESCRIPTION, MASK (a zapper mask of who may take it, as -RACE +Human +Half-Elf), UNLOCK (a
tattoo the profile or the character must have, as one a profile achievement gives), START (a
 room ID, the start room), ITEMS (catalog item names or item classes, a count before one for
 more, as 2 a worn prayer book, a torch), ABILITIES (an ID and a proficiency each, as
Prayer_Bless 25), FACTIONS (a faction ID or name and an amount added each), TATTOOS, MONEY
and SCRIPT (a ONCE_PROG, lines between semicolons, as ONCE_PROG 100;mpecho Welcome home.;~).
  When any origin is open to a character, creation asks for one after the class (by number
or name); the choice is kept as the tattoo ORIGIN_[ID], for masks and scripts (-TATTOO
+ORIGIN_ORPHAN), and what it gives comes as the start room is set, after the class's outfit.
  CHARCREATIONSCRIPTS=ORIGIN:LOAD=... runs scripts just after.  Example: [ORPHAN]
NAME=Temple Orphan, MASK=-RACE +Human +Half-Elf, START=Ashford#12, ITEMS=a worn prayer book,
 ABILITIES=Prayer_Bless 25, FACTIONS=faithofash.ini 1000, TATTOOS=ORPHAN.
```

<a id="party"></a>

## PARTY

Source: [help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/help.ini), line 33.

```text
Command : PARTY
Usage   : PARTY (ADD/REMOVE/REST [NAME]) (or PARTY RULES)
Usage   : PARTY MEET (ON/OFF)
Usage   : PARTY FIGHT (ON/OFF)
Usage   : PARTY ORDER [NAME] [NAME]...
Usage   : PARTY LEAD/DISABLE/ENABLE [NAME]
Usage   : PARTY MORTAL/ARCHON [NAME] (builder mode)
Example : party
Example : party add bran
Example : party rest bran
Short(s):
Several of your characters (see PROFILE) can be in the world at once, and those who follow
one leader are a party.  PARTY lists them: your party, the rest of your characters in the
world, and those resting in your profile, out of the world.  PARTY ADD NAME brings one into
your party; one who was resting comes back into the world.  PARTY REMOVE NAME takes one out
of the party, leaving them in the world, and PARTY REST NAME sends one back to rest.  You
play one character at a time: SWITCH NAME plays another of those in the world, and the one
you were playing stays where they are.  AS NAME COMMAND has one of them do a command, and
shows you what comes of it.  Who follows the leader also helps them fight, unless AUTOASSIST
 is off.  PARTY MEET ON has a character you add stay where they are, or come back where they
 last were, for you to go and meet them; PARTY MEET OFF, as a game starts unless PARTYMEET
is set, has them come to you.  PARTY FIGHT ON lets your characters fight each other, and
PARTY FIGHT OFF, as a game starts unless PARTYFIGHT is set, does not.  For turn-based time
(see PARTYTURNS), PARTY ORDER sets the order your party acts in, PARTY LEAD NAME hands the
lead to another member, and PARTY DISABLE NAME has a member act on their own, as followers
do, so that the turn does not wait for orders for them; PARTY ENABLE NAME undoes it.

PARTY RULES shows this world's size and joining rules. Worlds can limit the party and
profile, cap all active characters, and require you to meet companions or summon them only
in certain places. PARTY MEET OFF cannot override those rules. REMOVE leaves a character
active elsewhere; REST takes them out of the world. To make another character, LOGOFF opens
your profile, then NEW name. Use PARTY ADD name to bring them along, SWITCH name to play
them, or AS name command to give an order. PARTY CLANS lists memberships and ranks; FACTIONS
 PARTY compares standings. See also PROFILE, SWITCH, PARTYTURNS and WINDOWS.
```

```text
Short(s):

services in the entire mud.  It can be a quick and easy way to discern locked up threads, or

objects, or specify room, area, or an object name to suspend the ticking of just that
object.
```

<a id="perksini"></a>

## PERKSINI

Source: [arc_misc.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_misc.ini), line 1199.

```text
CoffeeSUD: perks, traits and flaws, in world/perks.ini.  A perk is a line: its ID, then
NAME="...", POOL=GENERAL (or any pool name), MASK="..." (a zapper mask, as -LEVEL +>=3),
REQUIRES=PERK_X,PERK_Y (perks, or tattoos, it needs first), COST=1, REWARDS="..."
(achievement rewards, as 1 CHARISMA 50 XP) and HELP="...".  PICKS= gives the picks each pool
 has, ; between them: GENERAL every 3 levels; CLASS:Fighter at 1,5,10 (a CLASS:name pick
counts that class's own levels).  A character's picks are the picks of their levels less the
 COST of the perks they took of that pool; a level-up with one to spend says so.  PERKS
shows what they have, can take and cannot yet, and why; PERK [name] takes one: its ID
becomes a tattoo (HASPERK(), -TATTOO masks) and its rewards are given.  POOL=TRAIT perks are
 traits and flaws, bought in the TRAITS step of creation (after KIT, AHELP CREATIONSTEPS)
with TRAITS=[N] points; a flaw has a COST below 0 and gives points back.  Their rewards come
 at the end of creation.  MPPERK gives or takes one from a script.  Example: PERK_PACKMULE
NAME="Pack mule" POOL=GENERAL REWARDS="50 MAXCARRY"; TRAIT_LUCKY POOL=TRAIT COST=2;
FLAW_BADBACK POOL=TRAIT COST=-1.
```

```text
(the default), ONLY (no making your own) or NO.  Picking one gives the character the
```
