<a id="vars"></a>

## VARS

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 3153.

```text
Command  : VARS
Usage    : VARS LIST ([SCOPE]) ([HOST]) ([MASK])
Usage    : VARS SCOPES
Usage    : VARS SET [HOST] [NAME] [VALUE] (SCOPE [SCOPE])
Usage    : VARS CLEAR [HOST] ([NAME]/*) (SCOPE [SCOPE])
Usage    : VARS WATCH ([HOST] [NAME]) / VARS UNWATCH
Usage    : VARS DUMP [FILE]
Example  : vars list * Hero QUEST_*
Example  : vars set Hero ACT 3
Example  : vars watch * DRAGONMOOD
Short(s) :
Shows and changes the variables scripts keep (MPSETVAR, $%VAR()%).  LIST gives each one's
scope, host, name and value: the scope is * for all of them, GLOBAL, QUEST and a quest's
name, a scope's name (MPSETINTERNAL SCOPE), or INDIVIDUAL for the scripts that keep their
own; the host and the name may hold * as a wild card.  SCOPES counts the hosts and variables
 of each scope. SET sets one as MPSETVAR would (so ++, +5 and the like add), in the global
scope unless SCOPE is given; CLEAR clears one, or all a host has.  WATCH tells you of each
change to a variable (* for any host or name), with the script file that made it and the
room it ran in; WATCH alone lists yours, UNWATCH stops them.  DUMP writes the list to a
file, to compare two runs. Scripts can list names too: $%VARNAMES(host prefix)%.
```

```text
This skill allows a player to craft wagons and carts.  The extent of the items which can be
crafted expands as the player goes up in level.  To begin carving a new item, the player
must have placed the wood he or she wishes to make the item from on the ground. The player
may also learn to how to make a found cart, provided a blank recipe page, or recipe book
with blank pages is in his or her inventory. Items crafted with balsa can be done with half
```

<a id="wait"></a>

## WAIT

Source: [help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/help.ini), line 2774.

```text
Command : WAIT
Usage   : WAIT ([TICKS])
Usage   : WAIT [N] HOURS/DAYS/WEEKS
Usage   : WAIT UNTIL DAWN/DAY/MORNING/DUSK/NIGHT/HOUR [N]/DAY [N]/ARRIVAL/STOP/DOCK
Example : wait
Example : wait 10
Example : wait 8 hours
Example : wait until dawn
While time is turn-based or the game is paused, lets one tick, or the given number of ticks
(up to 100), pass.  A wait of several ticks ends early if you are hurt, attacked or moved,
so in a fight WAIT 10 lets the fight go on until the next blow lands, and when someone
speaks to you.  In real time, time passes on its own. In a party (see PARTYTURNS), only the
leader's WAIT lets time pass, once the others have carried out their orders; another
member's WAIT has them sit out the leader's next turn.  CoffeeSUD: WAIT [N] HOURS, DAYS or
WEEKS, or WAIT UNTIL a time of day, an hour, a day of the month, or (on a vessel or mount)
ARRIVAL, STOP or DOCK, lets up to three game days pass, in turn-based or real time (the
clock stops for it and starts again after): the world goes on as it would, you are told each
 hour, and it ends early as a long WAIT does. In an inn's room a wait of an hour or more
ends with a full rest.  Builders may also WAIT UNTIL VAR [HOST] [NAME] [OP] [VALUE] or QUEST
 [NAME] STEP [N] or DONE.
```

```text
 which can be crafted expands as the player goes up in level.  To begin crafting, the player
```

```text
This skill allows a player to craft weapons from metal.  This skill requires Blacksmithing
in order to learn it.  It also requires specialization in the weapon type the player wishes
to make.  The extent of the weapons which can be crafted expands as the player goes up in

have placed the metal he or she wishes to make the weapon from on the ground.  The player
may also scan the room or other players for equipment that may be mended by this skill,
using the scan parameter, or learn how to smith a found item, provided a blank recipe page,
or recipe book with blank pages is in his or her inventory. The metal for weaponsmithing is
obtained using the Mining skill, or better metals from the Smelting skill. Using better
materials will increase both the strength and the required level of the crafted item, and
some material types require smaller amounts to make the same items.
```

```text
CoffeeSUD: MODIFY AREA WEATHERPROFILE [NAME] (NONE takes it away) gives an area, and its
child areas, the climate of world/climates/[NAME].ini (or resources/climates/[NAME].ini) in
place of the built-in one.  Its lines: SPRING=, SUMMER=, FALL= and WINTER= (or ALL= for
every season not given) weigh each weather, as CLEAR 40, CLOUDY 30, RAIN 20, FOG 10 (the
area's wet, cold, hot, dry and windy bits still add theirs); TRANSITION=RAIN->FOG=30,
CLEAR->RAIN=10 sets the chance of a change from one weather to another in place of the
built-in one (a minus number all but forbids it); HOLD=[HOURS] is the fewest game hours a
weather lasts before it changes on its own; ALLOW=FOG,CLEAR is the only weathers it has;
TEXT_[WEATHER]= the weather's description and STOP_[WEATHER]= its ending line, alternatives
between |, NONE for nothing, in place of lists.ini's.  WEATHER FORECAST names an area's
climate and shows its odds; a file that is missing, or a line it cannot read, is logged.
```

```text
followed by a name can be used to label weaved containers.  The extent of the items which
```

```text
Command : WINDOWS

Usage   : WINDOWS PANEL (ON/OFF/[SECTIONS])
Example : windows on
Example : windows panel status,party
Short(s):
With WINDOWS ON, each of your characters in the world (see PARTY), but for the one you play
here, has a window of their own: it shows what they see, and what you type into it is their
command, so that you can play several of them at once without switching.  In turn-based
time, what takes time still waits for the leader's turn (see PARTYTURNS).  SWITCH swaps the
one played here with the one in the window.  Closing a window sends that character to rest.
  WINDOWS OFF closes them all, leaving the characters in the world.  A game starts with
windows if WINDOWS=1 is set, and only where there is a display.

WINDOWS PANEL ON gives each window a panel beside its text, drawn again at each prompt;
WINDOWS PANEL OFF takes it away.  Give the sections to show, in their order, in place of ON:
 STATUS (the world's text/panel.txt, with the codes of PROMPT, or the character's points,
room and area), MAP (the rooms about the character) and PARTY (each of the party with a bar
of their hit points).  WINDOWPANEL=STATUS,MAP,PARTY in coffeemud.ini or world.ini starts a
game with it.
```

<a id="world"></a>

## WORLD

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 3177.

```text
Command  : WORLD
Usage    : WORLD (LIST)
Usage    : WORLD SET [KEY]=[VALUE]
Usage    : WORLD PROBLEMS
Usage    : WORLD MODULES ([ID])/CHECK/PLAN/RELOAD/ADOPT/CONFIGURE/STATE
Usage    : WORLD TEST ([FILE.play/FILE.test/FILE.js])
Usage    : WORLD CHECK (AREA ([NAME])) (LOG) (ONLY=[PART],[PART]...)
Usage    : WORLD DEV (([AREA]) ON/OFF)
Usage    : WORLD STATUS
Usage    : WORLD DIFF [FILE]
Usage    : WORLD RELOAD ([AREA]) [NAME] (FORCE)
Usage    : WORLD RELOAD SCRIPT [FILE]/ALL (RESET)
Usage    : WORLD RELOAD QUEST [NAME]/QUESTS/CATALOG/ASSETS/CHANGED
Usage    : WORLD BACKUPS ([FILE])
Usage    : WORLD RESTOREFILE [FILE] ([TIME])
Usage    : WORLD DIG ON/OFF (TYPE=[LOCALE/TEMPLATE]) (LINK=TWO-WAY/ONE-WAY)
Usage    : WORLD PATH [DIRECTIONS] (TYPE=..) (NAME="..") (DESC="..") (LINK=..)
Usage    : WORLD MAP (RADIUS [N]) (AREA) (IDS) (FLAGS) (HTML=[FILE])
Example  : world
Example  : world check only=exits,keys
Example  : world diff castle
Example  : world reload castle
Example  : world path e,e,n,ne type=forestpath name="A forest trail"
Example  : world map area ids flags
Example  : world reload script progs/innkeeper.script reset
Example  : world set START=Emberfall#0
Example  : world set HOURSINDAY=12
Short(s) : LIST WORLDINI
WORLD lists the world settings: the keys a world may set in world.ini in its folder, each
with its value in effect and where that came from (coffeemud.ini, world.ini or the command
line).  In builder mode, WORLD SET KEY=VALUE changes the key's line in world.ini, or adds
one, and a blank value takes it out; it takes effect the next time the game starts.  Keys
that are not world settings, such as the database's, stay in coffeemud.ini.  WORLD PROBLEMS
lists what did not load from the world files: an object of an unknown class (a misspelled
ability, say) is skipped, and its file loaded only in part, so builder mode does not write
that file until it is fixed (and the world loaded again from it), or SAVE FORCE writes it as
 the world has it.  WORLD CHECK, in builder mode or a DEV=1 game, checks the whole world (or
 one area) and lists errors, then warnings, each with its part and room: EXITS (exits to
nowhere, doors with no way back), REACH (start rooms that do not exist, rooms nothing leads
to from them, by area), KEYS (locked doors and containers whose key is nowhere: in rooms,
carried, in shops or the catalog), TEXT (the new room's description, rooms, generic mobs and
 items with their class's text), SHOPS (shopkeepers with nothing to sell), DATA (WORLD
PROBLEMS), SCRIPTS (SCRIPTCHECK), PROPS (PROPCHECK), JS (the world's JavaScript classes),
VOCAB (languages, glossary, lists and help), LORE (entries/files), TEMPLATES (presentation
text/options), ROUTES (travel and route references) and IDS (stable author identities);
ONLY= picks parts, LOG writes the report to the log too.  sud.sh CHECK=1 loads the world as
a new game would, on a scratch copy, runs it with no player, prints it and exits 1 if it
found errors: for a script or a commit hook.  WORLD DEV lists the dev areas: those in
world/dev, for building and testing only, which builder mode and DEV=1 games load and a
normal game never does (DEVSTART= in coffeemud.ini can start new characters in one, such as
a hub with portals and test gear).  In builder mode, WORLD DEV [AREA] ON makes an area one
(SAVE writes it to world/dev) and OFF a shipped one again; WORLD CHECK warns of an exit from
 a shipped area into a dev area, which leads nowhere in a normal game.  In builder mode,
SAVE does not write over or delete a world file changed outside the game (edited, added or
deleted since the game loaded or last wrote it): what it would write goes beside it, as
NAME.builder, and SAVE FORCE writes over it.  WORLD STATUS lists the files changed outside
the game, and what SAVE would write, delete and leave; WORLD DIFF [FILE] shows a file
(castle, areas/castle.cmare, quests/hunt.quest) against what SAVE would write, - for its
lines on disk and + for SAVE's.  WORLD RELOAD loads world files again into the running game:
 an area (by its name or its file's), whose players and their followers wait outside it and
come back, and whose exits from other areas are linked again (refused while rooms of it have
 unsaved mobs or items, as LIST UNSAVED lists them, unless FORCE); SCRIPT, the scripts that
name a file (or ALL), their triggers reset with RESET; QUEST, a quest stopped, read again
from its file in world/quests and started again at its step; QUESTS, each of them; CATALOG,
the catalog's entries from its file; CHANGED, each file WORLD STATUS lists as changed
outside the game.  In a normal game it saves the game as world-reload and restores it, which
 builds the world from its files again.  DEVWATCH ON ([SECONDS]) looks at the world files
and resources' scripts every few seconds and runs the reload that matches what changed, each
 noted in DEVLOG; DEVWATCH OFF stops it.  Before SAVE writes over or deletes a world file it
 keeps a copy in world/.backup/ (the last BACKUPS= in coffeemud.ini of each, 5 if not set):
WORLD BACKUPS lists the files with backups, WORLD BACKUPS FILE the times of one's, and WORLD
 RESTOREFILE FILE (TIME) puts the newest (or that one) back, changed outside the game, for
WORLD RELOAD to load.  WORLD DIG ON makes a room, as CREATE ROOM does (of the room's own
kind, or TYPE=, a locale or a builder template), wherever you walk and there is no exit, and
 goes into it, linked back unless LINK=ONE-WAY; WORLD DIG OFF stops it.  WORLD PATH lays out
 a chain of rooms, one for each direction, following the exits there already, each with
NAME= and DESC= if given, and leaves you where you are.  Rooms made so are saved and tagged
TODO, which WORLD CHECK lists until EDIT DESC gives them their own text.  WORLD MAP draws
the rooms around you (5 steps out, or RADIUS N) or the whole area (AREA), north up, laid out
 by walking their exits from your room (*); a room above or below, or where another is, is
listed instead.  IDS numbers the rooms and lists them; FLAGS marks what to look at: > < v ^
an exit that does not lead back, + a locked door, @ an exit to another area, s a room with
scripts, and lists the rooms of the area nothing leads to from here.  HTML=FILE writes the
area's map to world/maps/FILE.html, each room with its exits as links.
```

<a id="worldmaterials"></a>

## WORLDMATERIALS

Source: [arc_misc.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_misc.ini), line 1255.

```text
CoffeeSUD: a world's own materials (resources), in world/materials.txt, one a line, the
fields between tabs: NAME, FAMILY (CLOTH, LEATHER, METAL, MITHRIL, WOODEN, GLASS,
VEGETATION, FLESH, PAPER, ROCK, LIQUID, PRECIOUS, ENERGY, SYNTHETIC...), VALUE, FREQUENCY
(1-10, how common), HARDNESS (1-10), BUOYANCY, CATEGORY (FISH, BERRY or WOODY, or blank),
SMELL, EFFECTS (on the raw resource, as Spell_Light;Prop_HaveResister(fire 5)), DESCRIPTION
(of the raw resource) and CODE.  A # starts a comment, and a first line starting NAME is a
heading.  A row named as a built-in resource (IRON, OAK...) changes it.  The others come
after the built-ins (0-209; there is room for 256 in all): at their CODE when they have one,
 the rest sorted by name, so adding one moves only those after it; and an item made of one
keeps its name (MTRALN) next to its number, so it finds it again when the numbers move.
Crafting skills take a resource by its family, so Blacksmithing works starsteel of METAL;
ResourceOverride(starsteel) puts it in a room to be mined.  It is read when the game starts,
 before the ini's ADDMATERIAL_ entries, which it takes the place of for the same name.
Example line, with tabs where the commas are: starsteel, METAL, 300, 1, 6, 9000, , ,
Prop_HaveResister(fire 5), A sliver of metal that never cools.
```

## WORLDRULES

Source: [arc_misc.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_misc.ini), line 1212.

```text
CoffeeSUD: the world's rules for the profile and the party, in coffeemud.ini or world.ini.
PROFILEMAX=[N]: the most characters in the profile (1 for a world of one character).
NEWCHARS: ALWAYS (the default), FIRSTONLY (only the first character), CHEAT (more only with
CHEAT ON) or MASK (NEWCHARMASK, a zapper mask, must pass on the character played last, as
-LOCATION +ROOMSTR(Adventurers)); the first character is always made, and NEWCHARMESSAGE
says where to go when one is refused.  PARTYMAX=[N]: the most characters in the party at
once (PARTY ADD refuses more; one coming into the world is also held to MAXCONNSPERACCOUNT,
and the refusal is now said to you).  PARTYROLES="healer:-BASECLASS +Cleric +Druid;
scout:-BASECLASS +Thief": PARTY, and NEW at the profile menu, say which roles no character
fills.  CHEAT ON/OFF (HELP CHEAT) is kept in the save and shown in SAVES.  Example: a
lone-wolf world, PARTYMAX=1 NEWCHARS=FIRSTONLY; a dungeon crawler, PARTYMAX=4 NEWCHARS=MASK
NEWCHARMASK="-LOCATION +ROOMSTR(Guild)" NEWCHARMESSAGE="New heroes sign on at the
Adventurers' Guild."  NEWCHARLEVEL: the level a new character starts at, 1 (the default), a
number, PARTYMIN, PARTYAVG (of the profile's other characters) or LEADER (the one played
last), each with +N or -N (PARTYMIN-1); it is reached by real level-ups as creation ends, so
 hit points, practices, trains and the skills levels bring are earned.  NEWCHARXP=FLOOR sets
 their experience to the least of that level; KEEP (the default) leaves what the level-ups
gave.  FORMULA_PRACTICESPERLEVEL and FORMULA_TRAINSPERLEVEL: what each level gives, as
formulas (AHELP MATHFORMULA) of @x1 the new level, @x2 WIS, @x3 INT, @x4 the class's bonus
(LVLPRAC, or LVLTRAIN for trains) and @x5 the race's; blank (the default) gives WIS/6 plus
both LVLPRACs practices and 1 plus both LVLTRAINs trains.  TRAINSATLEVELS="1:3, 5:2" gives
more trains at those levels (level 1's as creation ends).  A GenRace's FSTTRAN and FSTPRAC
are more at creation; its LVLPRAC and LVLTRAIN, and a GenCharClass's LVLTRAIN, are more each
 level.  A lost level takes back what it gave.  A world's JavaScript practicesForLevel and
trainsForLevel, when set, have the last word.
```

## WORLD_COMPOSITIONS

Source: [arc_help.ini](../../CoffeeMud/resources/help/arc_help.ini), line 3349.

```text
Command : WORLD COMPOSITIONS
Usage   : WORLD COMPOSITIONS CHECK/RELOAD
Builder/DEV tools for the optional abilities.composition module. CHECK validates flat
world/compositions/<id>.v<version>.json files without changing the live library; WORLD CHECK
 ONLY=COMPOSITIONS also includes these findings. RELOAD atomically accepts a valid library
and its file provenance. Existing character bindings keep their selected versions and
hashes; missing or changed pins suspend.
The module is default off and is selected/adopted using WORLD MODULES. Grant Skill_Compose
through normal progression or creator tools; then COMPOSE lets players select skills and
link compatible supports. Data definitions control typed damage, tags, prerequisites,
modifiers, costs, timing, bounded chaining and burning. SAVE preserves hand-authored files
and character-owned choices.
See docs/creator/15-ability-composition.md and its runnable example pack.
No arbitrary scripts execute inside the modifier compiler. Existing abilities are unaffected
 unless explicitly integrated into an opt-in adapter.
```

```text
Command : WORLD MODULES
Usage   : WORLD MODULES ([ID])
Usage   : WORLD MODULES CHECK/PLAN/RELOAD
Usage   : WORLD MODULES ADOPT [ID]
Usage   : WORLD MODULES CONFIGURE [ID] [SETTING] [VALUE]
Usage   : WORLD MODULES STATE [ID]
Builder/DEV tooling for optional world modules. Flat JSON manifests live in
world/modules/<id>.json. MODULES selects root IDs; MODULESETTINGS supplies typed world
defaults as JSON. World settings take effect at the next process start.
CHECK validates definitions and selection; WORLD CHECK ONLY=MODULES also checks the current
clock. PLAN previews saved-state compatibility without applying it. RELOAD applies validated
 definition changes while retaining saved settings. ADOPT explicitly adds a world-selected
module and dependencies to a campaign. CONFIGURE changes one compatible active campaign
setting; SAVE keeps it and world defaults remain unchanged. STATE inspects a saved capsule,
including suspended records.
Saved versions, contract fingerprints, settings, removal policies and scoped state
participate in campaign saves. Missing/incompatible modules suspend with data retained, or
refuse restoration according to their saved policy. Version changes need declared
migrations. Ordinary MODULES/DEMO never grant creator permissions. See
docs/creator/14-optional-modules.md and its runnable example.
```
